## Agent fuzzer and fake model

A fake AI model plus a fuzzer that drives whole agent conversations. Three layers, one scenario schema (`"v": 1`, `crates/fake_llm/src/scenario.rs`); a failing case from any layer is a JSON file any other layer can replay. Nothing here ships in a release build: `fake_llm` is a dev-dependency of `app` only, and the app-side seam is `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-util"))`.

| layer | what it drives | where | state |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L0 wire** | the real genai client (`lib/rust-genai`, the BYOP decoder) against llmposter, a scripted raw server and a byte-level chaos proxy | `crates/fake_llm/tests/genai_decode.rs` | in this build |
| **L1 in-process** | the real controller / action model / queue in `App::test`, fed scripted turns through the stream seam, an actor stepping the user's side, an oracle checking I1-I8 after every step | `app/src/ai/blocklist/agent_fuzz/` | in this build (see below) |
| **L2 real app** | appci + a scripted fake provider, real PTY | `script/realapp/appci` (`fake_model.py`, a stdlib Ollama-protocol server, `APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1`; first user: the real-use replay, 2.16; llmposter itself is not used at L2) | in the replay |

**llmposter** (crates.io, AGPL-3.0-or-later, test-only; Phosphor is AGPL-3.0-only so the licences are compatible, and `AGPL-3.0-or-later` is on the `deny.toml` / `about.toml` lists for it) supplies the HTTP mock: OpenAI SSE, character-chunked text, HTTP error statuses, frame truncation. `crates/fake_llm` writes only the gaps: the in-process seam, byte-level cuts (inside UTF-8, a JSON string, between `data:` and `\n\n`), tool-call arguments streamed as many deltas, malformed arguments, chosen call ids, and the scenario schema.

### L0 (`genai_decode*`)

| test | what it proves |
|---|---|
| `genai_decode_llmposter_text_reassembles` (proptest) | text of any shape (multi-byte, quotes, newlines) chunked any way reassembles byte-exact |
| `genai_decode_llmposter_tool_call_arguments_parse` | every known tool's valid arguments arrive as the call's name and parsed arguments; the chunk the app accumulates by id carries the raw text |
| `genai_decode_llmposter_turns_follow_request_order` | the nth request gets the nth turn; past the script the fake answers `END` |
| `genai_decode_proxy_cuts_keep_text_exact` (proptest) | the stream cut at arbitrary bytes by `ChaosProxy` still decodes exactly |
| `genai_decode_wire_split_arguments_are_byte_exact` (proptest) | arguments streamed as 1-11 deltas, frames cut at arbitrary bytes, accumulate byte-exact |
| `genai_decode_wire_invalid_json_arguments_arrive_as_the_raw_text` | malformed / empty arguments reach the app as the exact text (the app parses and rejects them) |
| `genai_decode_wire_two_calls_keep_their_ids_and_order` | two calls keep ids and order |
| `genai_decode_disconnect_mid_stream_is_an_error_not_a_short_reply` | a connection dropped mid-stream is an error |
| `genai_decode_clean_close_before_done_is_a_visibly_missing_end` | a clean close before `[DONE]` is a plain end with no End event; the only defence is the app's "ended without a terminal End event" guard (`chat_stream.rs`) |
| `genai_decode_stall_is_catchable_with_a_timeout` | a silent connection can be timed out by the caller (the app has its idle timeouts) |
| `genai_decode_llmposter_truncation_never_looks_complete` | llmposter's frame truncation never yields an End |
| `genai_decode_llmposter_http_statuses_reach_the_caller`, `genai_decode_wire_html_error_page_is_an_error_with_its_status`, `genai_decode_llmposter_context_overflow_keeps_the_providers_wording`, `genai_decode_in_stream_error_event_is_an_error` | 429 / 529 / 503 / 500, an HTML 502, a context-overflow 400 and an in-stream error event reach the caller with the status or the provider's wording the app's classifiers match on |

### The seam and the test-only probes (L1 plumbing)

All `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-util"))`; none of it is in a release build.

| piece | where | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| stream seam | `app/src/ai/agent_providers/fake_stream_seam.rs`, hook `open_sdk_stream` in `chat_stream.rs` | `install(model_id, script)` registers scripted turns per model id; `generate_byop_output` asks the seam just before `exec_chat_stream` and, if a script exists, reads its `ChatStreamEvent`s instead of the network. Records every request (`RecordedRequest`: tool-message ids, tool-call ids, last user text, offered tools) for I3/I4. Open errors, mid-stream `Http` / `Transport` errors, `Stall`, `Wait` and a stream that stops with no `End` are all scriptable |
| `pending_snapshot_for_test` | `BlocklistAIActionModel` | every pending / preprocessing / running action with its stage (`PendingStage`) and kind; **panics on an action kind `fuzz_action_kind` does not classify**, so a new kind fails the fuzz run until it is given a verdict |
| `actionable_card_ids_for_test`, `card_ids_for_test` | `AIBlock`; `TerminalView::actionable_card_ids_for_test` aggregates | the actions a block shows an actionable card for (command / MCP / button cards while the action is blocked; the question card while it takes answers) |
| `complete_command_for_test`, `is_waiting_on_command_for_test` | `ShellCommandExecutor` | `MockTerminalManager` has no pty, so no block ever exists for a requested command; this finishes the waiting action as if the command exited, printing a chosen output |
| `interrupt_command_for_test` | `ShellCommandExecutor` | the pty's part of a Ctrl-C typed into a running agent command: finishes the waiting action with exit 130 and `interrupted` set, what the executor reports when the ^C the view wrote killed the command (`Block::was_interrupted_by_ctrl_c`). No cancellation reason is involved |
| `search_test_hook` | `agent_providers/tools/web_runtime.rs`, asked by `chat_stream::dispatch_byop_web_tool` | #2022: a dispatched `websearch` is answered inside the process, after the profile switch and the argument parse and before any request. **Always on in a unit-test build** (`cfg(test)`), so no test of the app crate can send a query through the dispatcher; in a `test-util` build that is not a unit test only after `answer_locally(hold)`; absent from a release build. `hold` keeps the answer out for a fixed time (a sleeping thread and a channel, no runtime needed). `run_websearch` itself refuses a call with no endpoint override in a unit test, before the request is built |

Seam unit tests: `fake_stream_seam_tests.rs` (unregistered ids fall through to the network, requests are recorded with their tool messages, dropping the handle unregisters, tool-call chunks and the End content match genai's, an open error carries its status, a duplicate id panics).

Request recovery (`agent_providers/stream_recovery.rs`, driven from `generate_byop_output`): before the first streamed byte a 429 / 408 / 5xx / transport failure is retried after 2, 4, 8 s (a `Retry-After` replaces that wait); after the first real event nothing is retried and the error is surfaced; a context-overflow answer (or a prompt over the known window, checked before the send) drops the oldest turns from that one request, whole tool rounds together, keeping system messages and the latest user message on, and retries once. Unit tests: `stream_recovery_tests.rs` (run against the seam, no sleeping: 429 with `Retry-After: 7` waits 7 s then succeeds; 503 x3 waits 2/4/8 s; schedule exhausted gives the note; 401 not retried; a drop before output is retried; a drop after output is not (one request, the error reaches the stream); overflow trims and retries once with the latest user message kept and no orphaned tool result (I4); a second overflow and an overflow with nothing older both surface; proactive trim before the first send; classification table). `SeamError::HttpRetryAfter` scripts a status with a `Retry-After` header. Corpus: `recovery_429_then_success`, `recovery_overflow_nothing_to_trim`, `recovery_midstream_disconnect_no_retry` (written without a build; confirm they pass on the box before they stay, per the corpus rule below). In unit-test builds the retry waits are divided by 1000. An error that used up the 2/4/8 s schedule (or stayed too long after trimming) is wrapped in `PreOutputRecoveryExhausted`, which `AIApiError::is_retryable` treats as terminal, so the outer layer adds no requests (a dead provider makes exactly 4; `a_dead_provider_makes_four_requests_and_the_error_is_not_retried_again`, `exhausted_in_stream_recovery_is_terminal_but_a_mid_stream_drop_still_resumes` in `response_stream_tests.rs`, which also pins that a mid-stream drop is still retryable and resumes once actions have run). The read-ahead's wait for the first event is deducted from the send loop's first-event window.

### The L1 harness (`app/src/ai/blocklist/agent_fuzz/`)

`cfg(test)` only. A case is one `App::test`: a real `TerminalView`, `BlocklistAIController`, action model and queue, the BYOP provider wired (`wire_mock_provider_config_with_model`) to a per-case model id whose replies come from the seam, and the active model set through `LLMPreferences`.

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `player.rs` | scenario -> `SeamTurn` per request (`Match`: nth request / last tool result / user token / default; an unmatched request gets `END`); records the call ids each reply emitted. `Missing` id = the id genai assigns (`call_<index>`), `DuplicateOf` = a repeated id, chaos = open error / mid-stream error / stall / no `End` |
| `rig.rs` | setup, `observe` (conversation status, stream in flight, action snapshot, actionable cards, queue rows), `drive_commands` (finishes `Quick`/`SetE` commands through `complete_command_for_test`; reports a never-ending one to the agent after a short wait, as the executor's stall snapshot does), `settle_until` Since #2104: `env.preprocess` holds every batch of tool calls in preprocessing (`set_preprocess_hold_for_test` at setup) and `drive_preprocessing` lets a `late_after_drop` batch go N ms after a stop dropped it |
| `actor.rs` | the scripted user, through the UI's entry points (table in the file header): Ctrl-C is the view's real key handling (`press_ctrl_c_for_test`) except into a running agent command, where the view would write the ^C to the pty and do nothing else: the rig has no pty and no block for the command, so it delivers the ^C itself (`Rig::interrupt_commands` -> `interrupt_command_for_test`, round 12; before that the view's handler did not find the command and took the status bar's cancel, which is the Stop path), a follow-up is typed into the input and `maybe_queue_input_for_in_progress_conversation` decides queue-or-submit (`type_and_try_queue_for_test`), Stop is the status bar's controller call. `AnswerQuestion` acts only on a question that is Blocked and has a card up, stages the answers, executes by id and then discards what was not taken (as `ask_user_question_view.rs` does), so it never completes a cardless question and works whether or not `ask_user_question` needs an approval step first |
| `oracle.rs` | I1-I4, I6, I7, I8 (I5 is `prompt_tests.rs`); its own unit tests cover the I4 and I8 checks on hand-built requests |
| `stop_tests.rs` | Stop means stop (#1942) end to end, counted on the seam's requests: a reply asks for a read and a command, the read finishes, the user presses Stop on the command's card -> no request is opened; the next user message opens exactly one request, which carries a result for both calls. Second test, the other half of the decision: the same reply, the user presses the card's Reject -> one automatic request is opened with no user message, it carries a result for both calls exactly once, the rejected command's persisted result says `rejected_by_user` (the read's does not), and the conversation goes on to `Success` |
| `runner.rs` | one case end to end; a panic becomes an I6 violation; a failure prints the scenario as schema JSON |
| `log_capture.rs` | ERROR-log tap on the unit-test logger (one tap per process: run under nextest) |
| `smoke_tests.rs` | a plain reply (status `Success`, one request, no tool message), and a command that waits for approval then runs (the step was performed on a `run_shell_command` card, two requests, exactly one tool message, `Success`): the smallest cases, so read their failure first; nothing orders them before the others |

Invariants (checked after every step; delta = 2 s, all waits scale with `AGENT_FUZZ_TIME_SCALE`):

| id | invariant |
|---|---|
| I1 | every blocked action has an actionable card within delta; nothing pending sits neither blocked-with-card, runnable nor running longer than delta (`transfer_shell_command_control_to_user` counts as carded only while the rig has a live never-ending command: its card is the CLI subagent view). Since the 2026-11-09 lifecycle audit (#1946) also: every tool call of the last cleanly finished reply has an action-model status (preprocessing, queued, blocked, running, finished) or a result message in the conversation within delta (`Obs::unsettled_calls`, read from the conversation and the action model separately; the clock runs only while no stream is in flight. Until round 18 the check was off after a `CloseTab`, whose rig stand-in erased the finished results on purpose; since #2103 the close keeps those calls' status and the check stays ON after a close, off only when the kill switch `PHOSPHOR_CLOSE_KEEPS_CALL_STATUS=0` makes the close erase them: `Oracle::tab_closed(results_erased)`) |
| I2a | script used up and every card answered -> conversation terminal within 5 s (+4 s per failing turn: retry backoff) |
| I2b | Stop, and a Ctrl-C that has nothing to interrupt (a card waits, a reply streams) -> terminal within 2 s, nothing pending or running, no stream in flight. A Ctrl-C typed while something RUNS is not a stop: it interrupts what runs and the turn goes on (I2c). `oracle::ctrl_c_interrupts` says which: (1) a RUNNING agent command (an action in the `Running` stage that the shell command executor waits on, `Rig::running_commands`): the key is the command's interrupt (#850, DECLINED.md IMPROVED; owner decision 2026-11-10, which closed the question on #1942), whether or not other actions of the reply wait behind it; (2) since round 17 (#2034) equally a running tool that is not a command (a read, a search), when no reply is streaming: `BlocklistAIActionModel::interrupt_running_actions`. A tool that runs while a reply still streams stays with I2b (the key cancels the reply). History: round 10 applied I2b to the command's interrupt too (what failed in matrix `pairs_hung_command` / `triples_hung_command` / `triples_read_files`, `CtrlCAfterFirst`); rounds 10-11 exempted any running action with later actions waiting; rounds 12-16 exempted only the command and held a running tool to I2b, which was the app's own inconsistency (#2034: the same key stopped the turn on a waiting card and one action on a running one) written down as a rule |
| I2c | that Ctrl-C: **(1)** what it interrupted stops running within 2 s (`Oracle::interrupted`: of the actions running at the key, at least one no longer runs; a command runs alone, and a file edit whose save is in flight is left to finish); **(2)** the turn goes on (`Oracle::turn_goes_on`): the action that waited next behind it and that only the user can end (a question; a command, with the allowlist off: `oracle::waits_for_the_user`) is still held when what ran has stopped. Gone means the key cancelled the rest of the turn too, which is a Stop's job. Not judged by I2c: how the step ends afterwards. That is the ordinary end-of-step rule (`plan_finished_batch`, no cancellation reason): the results go back to the model when any result of the step finished, and a step whose only result is the interrupted action ends `Cancelled` with the reason shown and sends nothing (#1178). The cards that follow are answered by the closing user and I2a still ends the turn |
| I3 | when terminal, locked queued rows unlock within 2 s; after a success, unlocked rows are sent within 3 s. After a cancel rows are restored to the input, not sent (#690 / #1026, kept by #1799) |
| I4 | each request carries exactly one tool message per emitted call id, in order, none extra, none orphaned; duplicates renamed `id#2`. The last request is cross-checked against the replies to the requests BEFORE it (round 10: it used to be zipped with every emitted reply, so a turn stopped after its newest reply, whose calls go back in no request (#1942), was reported as "the request holds [a], but the model emitted [b]"). Round 11: a reply whose stream the USER cut (a message sent and not queued, a Stop, or a Ctrl-C with no command running, while the stream was in flight; the runner tells the oracle, `Oracle::reply_cut`) may be whole or absent in later requests; every other reply must still be there, in place. Round 12 (`docs/design/r12-fuzz.md`): the app shows a call's card as soon as its chunk parses, as a tool-call message of its own, and that message stays when the stream then breaks or is cancelled (the next request answers it as cancelled). The player records, per reply, the calls that can be shown that early (`EmittedTurn::early_call_ids`: the delivered calls up to the first tool that gets no early card, such as `websearch`). A reply whose stream BROKE (disconnect, stall, no `End`) is absent or there with a leading part of those calls, never whole; a reply the user CUT is whole, absent, or there with a leading part of them. A finished reply nobody cut must be whole and in place, as before. The failure message names every reply the calls were held against and why it could be passed over, so it says by itself whether a cut was on record. Round 13 (`docs/design/r13-fuzz2.md`, the audit of the whole check): "no `End`" was two different things. The player now records how each reply's stream ended (`ReplyEnd`): `Finished` (the `End` came), `Broke` (failed open, disconnect, stall: the app leaves its stream loop by `yield Err; return`, no commit) and `ClosedEarly` (`never_end` alone: the body just stops, the loop ends as for a finished reply, the commit runs in full, in-stream tools included, and only then is the missing `End` reported). The rule per state: `Finished` or `ClosedEarly`, not cut = whole and in place, never passed over (`ClosedEarly` with one call per id: with no `End` the app accumulates chunks by id and renames nothing); either of them cut by the user = whole, absent, or a leading part of the early calls; `Broke` = absent or a leading part of the early calls, never more. So `ClosedEarly` is stricter than in round 12 (it may no longer be absent) and is allowed its whole form, which round 12 refused |
| I6 | no panic on any thread (a hook records panics in background futures), no ERROR log beyond the allowance per chaos kind and count: `status` / `context_overflow` / `disconnect` / `stall` 2 each, `never_end` 1, `split` / `delay` 0 (`oracle::error_allowance`). Log lines are not filtered by thread, so ERRORs from spawned futures count (run under nextest: one process per test) |
| I7 | no card takes accept keys for an action the model no longer holds (read from the card's own key routing, `AIBlock::key_routed_card_action_for_test` over `pending_command_card_view_id`, not from the action status) |
| I8 | the model is asked only when it should be, judged on the requests the seam received, never on the controller's bookkeeping (#1942, #1896, #1901, #1953). **(a)** after a Stop, and after a Ctrl-C pressed while no command is running, the request count is frozen until the user acts again (answers a card, sends a message); one more request is allowed only when a stream was in flight at the key, because a request is recorded when its stream opens, a moment after it is sent. A Ctrl-C into a running agent command is that command's interrupt and not a stop (owner decision 2026-11-10): it draws no line (its result may go back to the model, #1178) and, since round 12, it no longer counts as "the user stopped" for (b) either, so a plain submit that reaches no request in such a run is a lost message; `CloseTab` is not judged (the rig's close does not suspend the pane). **(b)** a message the user sent is the newest message of at most one request per submit, plus one per reply to such a request that failed or said nothing (those are retried); and a plain submit (not queued behind a turn) in a run with no Stop / Ctrl-C / CloseTab is in some request (the lost message). Only texts made of lowercase words, 8+ characters, are followed (the input may trim or rewrite others). **(c)** no request equals an earlier one or a prefix of it unless a reply in between failed or said nothing (a double send, or history going backwards); a request ending with a text the user sent more than once is left to (b). (a) is checked on every look, (b) and (c) at the end of the case (`oracle::check_requests`) |

I5 (`prompt_tests.rs`): the rig has no pty, so I5 drives the real `PromptDetector::observe` (now, termios shape, screen candidate and the #1796 `foreground_tty_read` probe) at the executor's 1 Hz poll with synthetic observations built from each command behaviour, plus the real hand-over on a `TerminalModel` block (`take_over_control_for_user` / `handoff_control_to_agent`, the calls `CLISubagentController` wraps and logs ERROR on failure).

| test | what it proves |
|---|---|
| `a_prompt_lookalike_is_never_handed_over_while_the_foreground_is_not_reading` | `Silent` / `TrailingColon` / `TrailingQuestion` with probe `NotReading`: never handed over in 30 simulated minutes (#1796) |
| `a_real_prompt_is_handed_over_within_the_window_plus_three_seconds` | `RealPrompt` + `Reading`: not before 15 s, not after 18 s |
| `a_secret_prompt_is_handed_over_at_once` | `read -s` (echo off, canonical) needs no probe |
| `with_no_probe_a_bare_question_gets_a_notice_after_ninety_seconds_and_no_hand_over` | probe `Unknown`: never handed over (owner rule: timers never decide routing); exactly one `MayBeWaiting` notice, not before 90 s |
| `handover_only_for_commands_that_read_the_tty` (proptest over every behaviour) | a hand-over happens only for a command that reads the tty (a secret prompt, echo off, aside) |
| `handing_over_and_back_logs_no_error_and_leaves_the_agent_in_control` | the real block hand-over round trip: no ERROR logged, agent in control afterwards |
| `a_second_hand_back_is_refused_without_a_panic` | a repeated hand-back is an `Err` (the controller logs it at ERROR): the executor must hand back once per take-over |

**Agent turn lifecycle audit (2026-11-09, `docs/design/agent-lifecycle-audit.md`, #1942-#1953).** Written without a build; the first box run is the first time any of it compiles. Deterministic tests added with the fixes:

| test | what it proves |
|---|---|
| `controller_tests::finished_batch::a_user_stop_after_a_finished_result_sends_no_request` | #1942: `plan_finished_batch` for Stop / Delete / a user shell command / a submit elsewhere over `[completed, rejected]` plans no follow-up, ends `Cancelled`, shows no notice; the same batch with no reason still follows up (#1178) |
| `preprocess_tests::has_pending_is_true_only_while_a_batch_is_still_preprocessing` | #1944: the fact a Stop keys its own status write on (a batch still preprocessing was dropped); parked, drained and abandoned batches are not it. The Stop path itself has no test (the rig cannot hold a preprocess) |
| `agent_fuzz::stop_tests::a_stop_after_a_finished_result_opens_no_request_and_the_results_ride_on_the_next_message` | #1942 on the rig, counted on `seam.request_count()` before and after `cancel_conversation_progress(.., ManuallyCancelled)` with one result already recorded |
| `agent_fuzz::oracle::tests::i8_*` | the I8 checks themselves, on hand-built requests; `i8_a_reject_never_freezes_the_request_count`: a Reject is the user acting, it draws no I8a line and lifts a standing one |
| `controller_tests::finished_batch::a_reject_after_a_finished_result_tells_the_model_at_once` | #1942 second part (owner decision 2026-11-09): `plan_finished_batch(Some(Rejected), [completed, rejected(, cancelled)])` plans an `Auto` follow-up with no notice; `Rejected` is not `is_user_stop`. `a_user_stop_ends_the_turn_without_a_notice` gained the lone-reject case (nothing finished: no follow-up, `Cancelled`) |
| `agent_fuzz::stop_tests::a_reject_after_a_finished_result_tells_the_model_at_once_and_the_agent_continues` | the same on the rig, through the actor's Reject (`cancel_action_with_id(.., Rejected)`), counted on `seam.request_count()` |
| `controller_tests::byop_message_for_a_rejected_call_says_the_user_rejected_it` | the persisted tool-result message of the rejected call: answered, no structured result, `server_message_data` = `{"status":"rejected","reason":"rejected_by_user","detail":...}`; the ordinary cancelled form never says "rejected" |
| `requested_command_test::the_reject_reason_keeps_both_labels`, `action_model_tests::only_a_user_reject_cancels_the_rest_of_the_turn` (extended) | the new reason keeps the card labels ("rejected by you" on the rejected row, "cancelled" on the later rows) and still cancels the rest of the turn (#1799) |
| `controller_tests::stashed_prompt::*` (6 tests) | #1948, third part of the decision: a stashed request that carries a prompt the user typed is never lost on Stop. `only_a_typed_prompt_counts_as_the_users_own` (pure: a `UserQuery` is the user's own, plan mode keeps its prefix; tool results, a resume, an empty request and a blank prompt are not). The others put a request straight into the controller's stash (`pending_byop_requests`), call `cancel_conversation_progress` and read the real terminal view's input: `stop_puts_a_stashed_typed_prompt_back_into_the_input` (stash gone, no stream opened, one `StashedPromptRestored`, the text in the input), `the_restored_prompt_is_appended_to_a_draft` (`draft\nprompt`, never over the draft), `delete_puts_a_stashed_typed_prompt_back_into_the_input`, `stop_still_drops_an_automatic_stashed_request` (no event, input empty), `a_follow_up_in_the_same_conversation_keeps_the_stash` (not a stop: neither dropped nor restored) |
| `response_stream_tests::an_offline_failure_parks_the_retry_and_the_dead_attempts_end_is_not_the_streams_end` | #1943: offline, a pre-action failure parks the retry; the failed attempt's transport ending emits no `AfterStreamFinished`; a Stop while parked emits exactly one |
| `conversation_tests::a_restored_turn_with_an_unanswered_tool_call_is_cancelled_not_successful`, `..._with_every_tool_call_answered_is_successful` | #1951: a conversation restored with a trailing unanswered client tool call is `Cancelled`; answered calls, a turn that moved on, and a turn whose only unanswered calls are subagent or carrier calls (never answered by the client) stay `Success`. `a_restored_turn_that_ends_in_a_subagent_or_carrier_call_is_cancelled` (round 10) pins the older rule that decides first: a turn whose LAST message is any tool call restores `Cancelled` (`into_exchanges`) |
| `conversation_tests::a_restored_passive_code_diff_that_was_accepted_is_successful`, `a_restored_passive_code_diff_that_was_never_answered_is_cancelled` | #1951, fourth part of the owner decision (2026-11-09): an accepted file edit counts as answered. A passive code diff conversation (`AutoCodeDiff` system query, `apply_file_diffs` call) that ends on the edit's result restores `Success` (so does a user-requested edit that ends on its result); the same conversation with no result, or with one of two edits unanswered, restores `Cancelled`. Both fixtures are checked to be `is_entirely_passive_code_diff` |
| `controller_tests::finished_batch::only_an_answered_passive_code_diff_is_recorded_without_a_follow_up` | what makes the first fixture real: `answered_passive_diff_results` picks the applied (or failed-to-apply) edit of a passive code diff for recording when its step ends with no follow-up; a cancelled / rejected edit, another tool's result, and any step that is not a passive code diff record nothing. The recording itself (`record_answered_passive_diff_results` -> `append_byop_action_result_messages`, the function a follow-up's preflight uses) is wired in the `FinishedAction` subscriber and has no test of its own: nothing in the unit rigs produces a passive code diff |

Expectation changed on purpose by the owner's "Stop means stop" decision: scenarios that stop after an earlier result of the same batch finished used to end `Success` after an automatic follow-up; they now end `Cancelled` with one request fewer (matrix `pairs_*` / `triples_*` `StopAfterFirst`, corpus `appr_order_fail_cmd_stop_after_first`). No test asserted the old status.

Second part of the decision (same day): a Reject is not a stop. Scenarios that reject a card after an earlier result of the same batch finished (matrix `pairs_*` / `triples_*` `RejectLast`, the Wave 0.5 `reject_middle_of_three`) end with the automatic follow-up again -- one request that carries every result of the step, then whatever the model replies -- not `Cancelled`. The fuzz actor's Reject sends `CancellationReason::Rejected`, and the runner reports it as the user acting (I8a never freezes the count after a Reject; I8b / I8c judge the request it opens). Expectations changed with it: `tui_cli_subagent_view_tests::reject_cancels_only_the_exact_displayed_action` now expects the `Rejected` reason on the rejected action's `FinishedAction` (it expected `ManuallyCancelled`, the reason the reject used to send); the two controller tests that press Reject (`reject_of_a_blocked_command_with_no_follow_up_unlocks_the_queued_row`, `rejecting_the_only_tool_call_drops_the_deferred_compaction`) pass the new reason and keep every assertion (a lone reject still sends nothing).

Not covered by a test, and why: a `RequestFileEdits` matrix kind with a slow-preprocess chaos (#1944) needs a preprocess hook in the executor and a file-edit tool in `fake_llm::KNOWN_TOOLS` (the rig would edit real files); an `offline` chaos (#1943) cannot reach the stream-level retry through the seam, because every pre-output failure the seam can script is absorbed by the in-stream recovery and comes out as the terminal `PreOutputRecoveryExhausted`; #1945 (task gone), #1947 (attachment read), #1948 (stash), #1949 (corrupt history) need a subagent task, attachments, a live call at preflight or a corrupt history, none of which the rig has. #1943 is covered at the unit level instead; the others are code-reviewed only. #1948's Stop half is covered from the stash onwards (`stashed_prompt::*` place the request in the stash by hand); how a typed prompt gets INTO the stash (a preflight that finds a call still winding down), the flush after a Reject, the restore on pane close and the restore when a newer request replaces the stash are not driven by any test.

**Round 10: the first run in which these tests were visible (pipeline 3048013125, `docs/design/r10-unit-lifecycle.md`).** The earlier Linux unit logs were cut at 4 MB before `agent_fuzz::matrix`, the stop tests and the restore tests; twelve lifecycle tests failed when the whole log was first read. What changed, per test family:

* `chat_stream` `controller_readiness_commits_the_cancellation_of_a_later_call_of_the_reply`, `controller_readiness_waits_for_a_live_later_call_of_the_reply` (new): the APP bug behind `stop_tests::a_reject_after_a_finished_result_...`. The readiness projection keys every call of a multi-call reply by the FIRST call's message id; the live-call lists keyed each call by its own. For the second and later calls the classifier never found the live call, so a cancelled result in the input was replaced by the synthesized "interrupted" placeholder (the Reject's `rejected_by_user` wording was lost) and a still-running call did not make the request wait. `rekey_live_tool_calls_to_projection` gives the live calls the projection's keys. Both tests fail on the old code; every older readiness test has one call per reply, where the keys coincide.

* `conversation_tests::a_restored_turn_with_every_tool_call_answered_is_successful`: TEST fault. Its third fixture ended in a subagent call and a carrier call and expected `Success`; a turn whose last message is a tool call was always `Cancelled` (the exchange conversion's own rule, older than #1951). The fixture now tests what it meant to (the #1951 rule does not count subagent and carrier calls: a client call answered with those two between it and its result is `Success`), and the trailing shape is pinned as `Cancelled` in its own test. No app change.

* `terminal::view::tests::open_pane_mid_batch_cancel_sends_the_follow_up`: STALE expectation, changed by the owner's #1942 decision. The mid-batch helper cancelled the blocked action with `ManuallyCancelled` ("what the reject button does", true until 2026-11-09). That reason is now a user stop and sends nothing; a Reject sends `Rejected` and does send the step's results. The helper passes `Rejected`, so the positive control (one request in an open pane) and `suspended_controller_mid_batch_cancel_sends_nothing_and_unlocks_the_queue` (nothing from a suspended pane, for a cancel that WOULD send in an open one) keep their meaning.
  **Round 11: still red in round 10, a second fixture fault behind the first.** The app did try to send (the log: "Not sending the request: no exchange could be added ... NoActiveTask"). The fixture's action and result named a task id, `"task"`, that the conversation does not have; since #1945 a request whose task is gone is refused before `SentRequest` instead of being sent into the void. The fixture now uses the conversation's root task. Until then the two "sends nothing" tests next to it could not fail either.

* `agent_fuzz::stop_tests::a_stop_after_a_finished_result_...`: TEST fault. It read the user's text off the request's last message, which on the OpenAI-compatible path is always the `<environment_context>` block (its own user message, appended to every request). The seam's record now tells the tail apart: `RecordedRequest::newest_message()` / `messages_without_environment_tail()`, and `last_user_text()` skips it (`fake_stream_seam_tests::the_environment_tail_is_not_the_newest_message`, built with the real renderer). The oracle written with the stop test had the same blind spot: **I8b ("one message, one request") and the prefix half of I8c never judged a request of the rig**, `Match::LastToolResult` and `Match::UserContains` could never match (no corpus file uses them). They read the newest message now (`oracle::tests::i8_is_judged_on_the_messages_before_the_environment_tail`). An I8 failure in the next run is the first real look at I8b, not a regression: triage it TEST-vs-APP from the printed requests.
* `agent_fuzz::fuzz_tests::paced_random_sequences_hold_the_invariants` (+ `_with_the_allowlist_on`): oracle fault in I4's cross-check (see the I4 row), `oracle::tests::the_reply_to_the_last_request_is_not_expected_in_it`. The proptest stops at its first failing case, so what the other paced cases do is not known until it runs again.
  **Round 11 (`docs/design/r11-unit5.md`): that fix did not cover the case that fails.** The same message came back in round 10 with the same shrunk scenario, which has no Stop in it: reply 0 runs a command, the user sends a message (request 1), reply 1 asks for a `websearch`, and the user sends a second message while the app is still running that search inside the stream. A sent message cancels the stream in flight; a reply's tool calls are committed in one piece only after the stream loop went through all of them, so reply 1 is in no later request. That is the user's cancel, not a lost call. The runner now records which replies the user cut and I4 lets exactly those be absent (`oracle::tests::a_reply_the_user_cut_may_be_absent_from_later_requests_and_no_other_reply_may`). If the message comes back with the cut recorded, the app dropped a committed reply: APP.
  **Round 12 (`docs/design/r12-fuzz.md`): the same message again in round 11 (build/r11a), and again a TEST fault (oracle).** The round 11 reading missed that reply 0 of the scenario has `disconnect_after: 1`: the stream delivers the command call and then drops, so reply 0 is never committed and nothing is approved or run. What stays is the call's early card, which the next request carries with a cancelled result. Then the two follow-ups as read before: the second one cuts the `websearch` reply. The last request holds the call of the BROKEN reply and nothing of the CUT one. The oracle kept no record of what a broken reply delivered, so with or without the cut on record it ran out of replies and printed the one message. By reading, the cut was on record (the search reply is absent, so its stream was cancelled before the commit, and the only step that cancels it is the second message, sent with the stream in flight); the trace cannot show it, because both paths printed the same text. So "the message returns with the cut recorded = APP" did not hold: the round 11 rule could not pass this scenario either way. Now: see the I4 row; `oracle::tests::a_broken_reply_leaves_the_calls_it_showed_early_and_nothing_else`, `a_cut_reply_may_be_there_with_only_the_calls_it_showed_early`, `player::tests::early_calls_are_the_delivered_run_before_the_first_tool_without_an_early_card`, and the scenario itself as corpus `i4_broken_reply_then_follow_up_cuts_search` (hermetic since #2022; it passes whether the second message lands inside the 120 ms search hold or after it). The checks that run after I4 at the end of a case (I8b / I8c, I6) have never run for this scenario: a failure there is a first look. Nothing compiled or run when written.
  **Round 13 (`docs/design/r13-fuzz2.md`): a different I4 message in round 12 (build/r12a), this time in `random_agent_conversations_hold_the_invariants` (+ `_with_the_allowlist_on`), and a TEST fault (oracle) again; it is the fourth change to this check, so the whole check was audited against the app's commit rules first.** Message: `the request holds calls [call_fixed, call_3729_0_1], which are in no reply. Held against ... the reply to request 0 (its stream broke: absent, or a leading part of the calls shown early [call_fixed])`. Reply 0 of the scenario is three call chunks (`call_fixed` an unknown tool, a `websearch`, `call_fixed` again as `read_shell_command_output`) with `never_end`: every chunk is delivered and the body then closes with no `End` and no error. The app's stream loop ends on a closed body exactly as on an `End`, so the commit runs: chunks are accumulated by id (2 calls, the log line says `tool_chunks=3 tools=2`), the search is run inside the stream, both calls and their results are yielded in one piece, and only then the "ended without a terminal End" error is raised and the turn resumed. That is the app's stated design for a truncated body (the `end_count == 0` comment in `chat_stream.rs`: what was received is kept, the user is told it is incomplete). Round 12 had put this reply in one state with a disconnect and a stall ("its stream broke: never whole"), which is only true when the loop is left by an error. Now: see the I4 row; `player::tests::a_body_that_closes_with_no_end_is_committed_and_a_broken_stream_is_not`, `oracle::tests::a_reply_that_closed_with_no_end_is_committed_whole`, and the scenario as corpus `i4_reply_closed_without_end_is_committed` (unused env commands removed; it has five `on_card` steps that find no card, so it runs for about 15 s). As in round 12, the checks after I4 (I8b / I8c, I6) have never run for this scenario, and the random proptests stop at their first failing case, so their later cases are unknown until this one passes. Nothing compiled or run when written.
  **Round 14 (`docs/design/r14-noend.md`, #2048, owner decision 2026-11-10): a reply whose body closes with no `End` is still committed whole, but the stream runs none of its tools.** The tools the commit used to run by itself (`websearch`, `webfetch`, `todowrite`, `search_codebase`, `get_relevant_files`; `chat_stream::runs_inside_the_stream`) are answered `not_executed` / `reply_incomplete` and nothing is awaited, and when such a reply used one call id for two different calls (the later one replaces the earlier in the buffer) the call that kept the id is answered `duplicate_tool_call_id` with the names of the calls it replaced. No I4 rule changed: the calls of the reply and their ids are what they were (one call per id, in place), only the results differ; the oracle, the player's `merged_by_id` and the round 13 table stand, with their wording brought up to date. Unit: `chat_stream::duplicate_call_id_tests::a_later_chunk_carries_on_its_call_and_a_reused_id_is_another_call`, `the_tools_the_stream_runs_itself_are_the_ones_an_incomplete_reply_does_not_run`, `an_incomplete_reply_answers_say_that_nothing_ran`. Corpus `noend_in_stream_tools_do_not_run` (grep, websearch, a file_glob with the grep's id, webfetch, todowrite, `never_end`), and `corpus_replay_tests::a_reply_that_closes_with_no_end_runs_no_search`: the rig's local search counter stands still across that scenario, after a control in which the same search in a finished reply moves it (the counter is per process: nextest). Worked, unproven: nothing was compiled or run.

The request builder no longer moves an `id#n` call next to `id`; instead the stream shows no NEW early card after a chunk that may be another call under a used id (`chat_stream::may_repeat_call_id`), so the repeat, which only gets its message at the `End`, is recorded before the calls emitted after it. The Anthropic streamer's opening pair of empty-argument chunks is not a repeat (`adapter_opens_calls_with_an_empty_chunk`: Anthropic, Vertex), or every call after an MCP call would lose its early card. Kill switch `PHOSPHOR_AGENT_REPEAT_ID_EMITTED_ORDER=0` (old rule: no card held, the builder moves the repeat). No I4 rule changed. Unit: `chat_stream::duplicate_call_id_tests::a_chunk_that_may_repeat_its_id_is_told_from_a_growing_call`, `a_repeat_that_is_not_next_to_its_original_keeps_its_emitted_place`, `the_request_lists_a_late_repeat_where_it_was_emitted`, `the_emitted_order_kill_switch_reads_the_usual_off_words`; `oracle::tests::a_repeat_stays_where_it_was_emitted`. Corpus (replayed with the rest): `i4_repeat_id_emitted_late_same_call` (`[x, y, x]`, the repeat equal to the first call; fails I4 on the old rule), `i4_repeat_id_emitted_late_other_tool` (`[x, y, x', z]`), `i4_repeat_id_adjacent_then_later_calls` (`[x, x', y, x'']`: the shape the old move was for, now kept in order by the held card). `dup_call_ids` (`[x, x, y]`, the repeat equal) stays as it is and must still pass. Worked, unproven: nothing was compiled or run.

Web access stays on in the rig: the cells keep going through the intercepted-tool path (turning it off would move them to the "tool not offered" refusal). What changes for the cells: a search that parses now always succeeds with the local text (before: a real answer, or a network error on a box without network).

They now end the way the app ends them: with other results in the step, one follow-up and the model's answer (matrix `pairs_*` / `triples_*` `CtrlCAfterFirst` with a command running, corpus `appr_order_hung_read_ctrl_c`); with the interrupted command alone, `Cancelled` with no request (corpus `ctrl_c_during_never_ending_command`, `appr_slow_command_ctrl_c_while_running`). No cell asserts a final status, so no expectation in the matrix or the corpus was edited. What is NOT modelled: a Ctrl-C after a never-ending command was reported as stalled (the rig's `lrc_alive`; no action is `Running` then) still goes through the view's handler and is judged as a stop, where the app would send the ^C to the live command.

**Diagnosing a failed fuzz test in CI (round 8).** The failing test's captured stderr is mostly app INFO/WARN spam, and GitLab caps a job log at 4 MB, so the panic text (the invariant and the shrunk scenario JSON, which `report` prints LAST) was cut off in round 8 (`paced_random_sequences_hold_the_invariants`, 126 s: the 120 s shrink budget ran out, so a real violation was found early). `test-linux` and `test-workspace-rest` now pipe nextest through `script/ci/filter_test_log.py` (drops timestamped `[INFO]/[WARN]/[DEBUG]/[TRACE]` app log lines, keeps everything else including `[ERROR]`, prints the drop count) and keep the UNFILTERED output as the job artifacts `nextest-linux.log` / `nextest-rest.log` (7 days). Read the panic in the job log first; the artifact has the full stderr. The macOS/Windows `run_suite.sh` jobs are unchanged.

Determinism: the default run uses a FIXED proptest seed and 12 cases (`AGENT_FUZZ_SEED=<0-255>` picks another, `AGENT_FUZZ_SEED=random` a fresh one), so an unrelated change is never gated by unseeded randomness. Deep runs are `script/agent_fuzz` with `AGENT_FUZZ_SEED=random PROPTEST_CASES=200` and/or `AGENT_FUZZ_MINUTES`. `.config/nextest.toml` gives `test(agent_fuzz)` a 120 s slow period (terminate after 5) because one test is many whole conversations with real waits.

Environment knobs: `AGENT_FUZZ_TIME_SCALE` (default 1.0), `AGENT_FUZZ_HUMAN_SCALE` (default 0.05, scales the actor's 400-2500 ms "human" delays). `stall` chaos needs `PHOSPHOR_BYOP_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS` and `PHOSPHOR_BYOP_STREAM_FIRST_EVENT_TIMEOUT_SECS` at 3 or less (`script/agent_fuzz` sets them to 1).

### Corpus, known failures, coverage, entry point

* `agent_fuzz/corpus/*.json` is replayed on every run by `corpus_replay_tests.rs`. Each file is a schema-v1 scenario named by its stem. The four Wave 0 scenarios are there as ordinary entries (they pass on this branch, where #1796, #1797 and #1799 are fixed): `wave0_1799_reject_then_transfer` (a held command and a hand-over behind it, a follow-up queued while blocked, then Reject), `wave0_1797_ask_empty_args` (`questions: []`), `wave0_1797_ask_valid` (a real question, answered), `wave0_1796_silent_then_handoff` (a silent, prompt-shaped command; L1 has no pty, so its detector half is `prompt_tests.rs`). Also `dup_call_ids`, `unknown_and_not_offered_tools`, `ctrl_c_during_never_ending_command`.
* Adding a case: copy the JSON a failure prints (or the file `AGENT_FUZZ_SAVE=<dir>` wrote) into `corpus/`. Never put a scenario in the repo that you have not seen pass or listed.
* `known_failures.toml` maps a corpus scenario to the issue that tracks it. A listed scenario must still fail with the same invariant; it fails the run the day it passes (remove the entry) or fails with another invariant (file that one). Empty today.
* `coverage.rs` counts (tool x op x timing) for performed user steps and (chaos x phase) for the model's turns. `WAVE0_FLOOR` lists cells the corpus must reach on its own (reject / approve / answer / follow-up on a card, Ctrl-C), checked in the corpus replay (nextest runs each test in its own process, so the floor cannot live in a separate test). `AGENT_FUZZ_COVERAGE=1` prints the table.
* `script/agent_fuzz` runs L0 + L1 through `script/check_test_failures -p fake_llm -p warp --lib --features warp/gui -E 'test(agent_fuzz) | test(genai_decode)'`, with `PHOSPHOR_BYOP_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS` / `..._FIRST_EVENT_TIMEOUT_SECS` at 1 so a `stall` turn ends in test time. Knobs: `PROPTEST_CASES` (12), `AGENT_FUZZ_SEED`, `AGENT_FUZZ_MINUTES` (time-boxed fresh rounds), `AGENT_FUZZ_SAVE`, `AGENT_FUZZ_TIME_SCALE`, `AGENT_FUZZ_COVERAGE`. Proptest never writes `proptest-regressions` into the tree (the corpus is the memory), and shrinks to a minimal (script, user) pair printed as schema JSON.
* CI jobs: none yet (manual, on the build box).
* **Cargo.lock:** `crates/fake_llm` adds llmposter (and its axum 0.8 tree). The first box build updates `Cargo.lock`; the coordinator commits it (do not build with `--locked` before that).
* **cargo-about:** `crates/fake_llm` is a workspace member, so `cargo about` lists llmposter in the third-party notices even though it is dev-only and never in a release binary. Over-attribution; acceptable.

A scenario that has only ever passed proves nothing. `script/ci/agent_fuzz_catches_wave0.py` puts each of #1796 / #1797 / #1799 back
into the tree under test, one at a time, and replays the corpus: the bug's own scenario (or prompt test) must FAIL. Written in round 14
(`docs/design/r14-hygiene.md` 4) without cargo; the table at the end of this section is empty until the box has run it.

| arm | the bug put back (each edit only disables the branch its fix added) | must fail |
|---|---|---|
| `control` | none | nothing: both tests pass, or the run proves nothing |
| `m1799` | `action_model.rs`: `rejection_cancels_rest_of_turn` is not consulted; `shell_command.rs`: `transfer_resolves_without_approval` is false | corpus `wave0_1799_reject_then_transfer` |
| `m1797_empty` | `ask_user_question.rs`: `should_autoexecute` ignores `has_no_answerable_questions`, `execute` no longer returns the error for an empty list | corpus `wave0_1797_ask_empty_args` |
| `m1797_valid` | `ask_user_question.rs`: `execute` drops the answer the card staged and waits on the old channel | corpus `wave0_1797_ask_valid` |
| `m1796` | `interaction_mode.rs`, `PromptDetector::observe`: silence past the notice window counts as a tty read | `agent_fuzz::prompt_tests::a_prompt_lookalike_is_never_handed_over_while_the_foreground_is_not_reading` |

`wave0_1796_silent_then_handoff` has no arm: L1 has no pty, so it cannot fail there; the detector half of #1796 is the prompt test.

**Procedure (build box only; it runs cargo through `script/agent-cargo`).**

1. Anywhere, no cargo: `python3 script/ci/agent_fuzz_catches_wave0.py --self-test` (the log parser and the verdicts, on fixtures) and
   `python3 script/ci/agent_fuzz_catches_wave0.py --check` (every edit still matches the source exactly once and every expected
   scenario / test exists). A failing `--check` means the code moved: update `MUTATIONS` in the script before anything is built.
2. On the box, in a checkout that has the commit under test:
   `python3 script/ci/agent_fuzz_catches_wave0.py --run --workdir <dir on real storage> [--commit <rev>] [--label <agent-cargo name>]`.
   It creates the worktree `<dir>/wt` at the commit (default `HEAD`), and for each arm resets the worktree, applies the edit, and runs
   `script/agent-cargo <label> nextest run -p fake_llm -p warp --lib --features warp/gui -E 'test(corpus_replays_as_listed_and_reaches_the_wave0_cells) | test(agent_fuzz::prompt_tests)' --no-fail-fast`
   with the two `PHOSPHOR_BYOP_STREAM_*_TIMEOUT_SECS` at 1 (what `script/agent_fuzz` sets). Five arms, one incremental build of the
   `warp` lib tests each; the default label `agent-fuzz-proof` has its own, cold, target directory, so pass the label of a target that
   is warm for this commit if there is one. Never under `/tmp` (the script refuses). `--arms control,m1799` runs a subset; `--keep`
   leaves the worktree; `--cleanup --workdir <dir>` removes it later.
3. Read `<dir>/verdict.txt` (also printed) and `<dir>/logs/<arm>.log` (each starts with the edit as a diff). Exit 0 = `PROVEN`.

**Reading the verdicts.**

- `control OK`, every other arm `CAUGHT`: proven. The line names the invariant (`.. fails I2a (..)`) and any other scenario that
  failed with the same bug; copy the table below and close #1836.
- `NOT CAUGHT`: the scenario passed with its bug put back. Either a later defence masks the bug (#1851 and #1858-#1861 added
  several around questions; the edit then has to switch that off too, which is a change to the script, with the reason), or the
  oracle has a gap. File it; do not edit the scenario until it fails.
- `INCONCLUSIVE`: the corpus replay timed out or did not run (a hang the rig did not turn into a verdict is still a finding: the
  oracle should have said I1). `BUILD FAILED`: no test ran; the edit did not compile at this commit (read the log; the edits are
  `false && ..`, one `.filter(|_| false)` and one `let`).
- `control FAILED`: the unedited tree is red in these tests; fix that first, the arms mean nothing.

Question scenarios tolerate either `ask_user_question` flow: the card appearing without an approval step (an owner decision in flight in another change), or after one. #### Approvals suite and the safe read-only allowlist (Wave 1.5 #2)

Nothing here has been compiled or run yet (written without cargo; the box run is the first).

**The matrix** (`agent_fuzz/matrix.rs`): a deterministic, exhaustive sweep next to the proptest. Every cell is a scenario built in code, run through the same rig and oracle (I1-I8 after every step), once with the safe allowlist OFF (`off`, the gate) and once ON (`on`, a separate test so an ON failure never hides an OFF result). One module per row, so nextest runs rows in parallel processes: `agent_fuzz::matrix::<row>::{off,on}`.

| sweep | rows | cells per mode |
|---|---|---|
| `kinds_*`: every action kind (command, listed command, failing, slow, never-ending, read_files, grep, file_glob, question, transfer, write-to-command, read-command-output, websearch, webfetch) x every response at the card (approve, reject, edit, Ctrl-C, stop, close the tab, switch mode, escape, follow-up, answer, skip, never) | 14 | 168 |
| `timings_*`: command / never-ending command / question x approve, reject, Ctrl-C, stop, close the tab, follow-up x early (during the stream), fast (10-25 ms), late, after the end, twice, burst of three | 3 | 108 |
| `pairs_*`: every ordered PAIR of six kinds in one turn x seven user policies (approve all, reject first, reject last, Ctrl-C / stop / close the tab / follow-up after the first) | 6 | 252 |
| `triples_*`: a seeded sample (12 per first kind, xorshift, no dependency) of ordered triples x three policies | 4 | 144 |
| `malformed_*`: every tool x every malformed-argument shape (empty, `{}`, truncated, wrong types, extra fields; four more for `ask_user_question`) x approve / reject / Ctrl-C | 10 | 162 |
| `command_behaviours`: quick, failing, slow, never ends, silent, pager, alt screen, secret prompt x approve / reject / Ctrl-C / stop / follow-up | 1 | 40 |

874 cells per mode, 1,748 with both. `the_matrix_sizes_are_what_the_docs_say` pins the counts and `the_matrix_names_every_tool_and_every_response` fails when a tool is added to `KNOWN_TOOLS` without a matrix kind.

Also: `paced_random_sequences_hold_the_invariants` (+ `_with_the_allowlist_on`): random conversations whose user steps are all `Timing::Fast` (10-25 ms apart), 3-9 steps; `random_agent_conversations_hold_the_invariants_with_the_allowlist_on`; `corpus_replays_with_the_allowlist_on`. 29 seeded corpus scenarios (`corpus/appr_*.json`, 36 files in all) cover each combination class: orders (6), timings (6), slow / failing commands (4), malformed arguments (6), kinds x responses spot checks (5), the allowlist (2). New schema piece: `CmdBehaviour::Slow { ms, out }` (finishes by itself after `ms`; `env.rs` `CompletesAfter`).

**The allowlist** (`ai/blocklist/safe_commands.rs`, ships OFF): `AISettings::safe_command_allowlist_enabled` (default `false`, `agents.warp_agent.permissions.safe_command_allowlist_enabled`) and `safe_command_allowlist` (entries `program` or `program subcommand`; default `ls cat head tail wc grep rg pwd whoami id uname df du stat file which basename dirname realpath tree uptime free`, and NO git subcommand: git runs helpers a repository's config names, so a user must add `git status` etc. deliberately). `BlocklistAIPermissions::can_autoexecute_command` consults it AFTER the denylist and the command-word analysis (a denylisted or unresolved line never reaches it) and before the profile policy; reason `SafeReadOnlyAllowlisted`. The matcher accepts one program with plain words only: it rejects any shell metacharacter (pipe, ampersand, semicolon, redirects, parentheses, braces, backtick, dollar, backslash, glob characters, quotes, `#`, `!`, `~`, `=`, `%`, `^`, `@`, `,`, `:`), newline or non-ASCII, a program that is not spelled exactly (no `/`), flags that write / run / never end (`sort -o`, `tail -f`, `rg --pre`, `date -s`, `git diff --output`), and never vouches for `find env xargs sudo sh sed tee cp rm curl less vim ...` even if listed. Residual risk for a git entry a user adds: git runs helpers a repository's config names (`core.fsmonitor`, `diff.external`, textconv); that is why the defaults hold none. Questions (`ask_user_question`) already need no approval and are unchanged. UI: Settings > AI > Permissions, under the command allowlist (switch plus an editable list, entries validated by `is_valid_entry`).

* `safe_commands_tests.rs` (pure matcher), `permissions_test.rs::safe_command_allowlist` (off by default and `ls` asks; on: listed lines allowed, pipes / redirects / `;` / `&&` / substitution / globs / `rm` / `git push` / `find` / `tail -f` asked; denylist still wins), `settings/ai_tests.rs` (ships off).
* `allowlist_tests.rs`: `allowlist_removes_the_approval_for_a_listed_line_and_only_that` (ON: `echo hi` runs with no card; `fake-cmd` lines still ask), and the differential `allowlist_on_and_off_reach_the_same_terminal_state` (proptest; a user who only approves / answers ends in the same status, request count and tool messages with it ON or OFF; the only permitted difference is the skipped approvals).
* The rig has no pty and so no shell type; `shell_command.rs::escape_char_without_a_session` (test / `test-util` builds only) assumes POSIX when the allowlist is ON, so the ON runs exercise the real decision. A release build and every OFF run keep "no session -> ask".
* Agent-mode vs terminal-mode coverage of the approval flows comes from the real-app replay case (`lab_replay`) and the agent appci cases, not from the in-process rig (which has no mode concept).
* **Owner rule:** the allowlist ships OFF. It is enabled by the owner only after this suite is green with it OFF (the `off` rows, corpus replay, both proptests). Do not flip the default in code.

#### `hop=` diagnostic lines (always on, owner-approved)

Info-level, written only when a state CHANGES, ids / kinds / states only, never content (no command text, prompt text, arguments, error text or the agent's hand-over reason). The later L2 (appci) reads them from the app log to see which hop of a conversation stalled.

| line | written by | states |
|---|---|---|
| `hop=agent_action id= kind= status=` | `BlocklistAIActionModel::hop` | `queued`, `blocked` (front of the queue, needs the user), `running`, `done`, `failed`, `cancelled` |
| `hop=action_card id= kind= shown=true` | `AIBlock` (`log_card_shown`) | a card came up: `run_shell_command`, `call_mcp_tool`, `action_buttons`, `ask_user_question` |
| `hop=handover action= reason=` | `CLISubagentController::switch_control_to_user` | `manual`, `stop`, `transfer_from_agent`, `blocked_on_input` (`action=-` when the block has no requested command) |
| `hop=queued_row id= state=` | `QueuedQueryModel` | `queued_locked`, `queued`, `unlocked`, `popped` (restored to the input), `fired`, `deleted` |
| `input_order hop=queued_row_restored id= buffer=` | `QueuedQuery::log_restored_to_input` (called by `TerminalView` after a popped row was put into the input) | what the input editor holds after the restore, read back from the editor: the text with `WARP_INPUT_ORDER_LOG_TEXT=1`, else `<N chars>`. `agent_fault_queued_rows` counts a row as held in the input from this line when no `hop=enter_begin` follows it (round 11: the Windows VM has no OCR engine) |
| `hop=turn conv= state=` | `AIConversation::update_status_with_error_message` | `in_progress`, `success`, `error`, `transient_error`, `cancelled`, `blocked`, `waiting_for_events` |

Run: `script/agent_fuzz` (L0 + L1). Nothing in this section has been compiled yet.

## #1801: remote Tab and path detection without the helper

A Phosphorized ssh session where the remote helper is absent, declined, failed or lost is the owner's PRIMARY remote
design. Its side commands run over the ControlMaster (`RemoteCommandExecutor`), which a VPN makes slow or breaks.

What changed and what pins it:

- **Tab asks the remote shell in-band.** An explicit Tab in such a session (`Session::is_remote_without_helper`)
  sends the `^Y` native-completions handshake to the session's own shell first and uses the completer only when the
  shell offers nothing (`app/src/terminal/input/native_completions.rs`, decision + span unit tests in
  `native_completions_tests.rs`; terminal mode and a shell command in agent mode take the same path, agent text never
  does; completions-while-typing never does). bash gained the handshake (programmable completion with COMP_*
  emulated, bash-completion's `-D` loader, `-C` commands, compgen actions, `-o` options), from 3.2 on (#1969, see
  "bash 3.2" below; `native_shell_completions_need_the_advertised_protocol_and_bash_3_2`). fish is off the path and its bootstrap has no
  handler: its read would need external commands, around which fish switches bracketed paste and keypad modes.
  **The exchange is self-identifying, and nothing is ever held behind it** (design comment in `pty_controller.rs`,
  "The in-band native-completions exchange"; third #1801 review). Wire: the app writes `^Y` only to a shell whose
  Bootstrapped hook advertised `!phosphor_nc_frames_v1` in its shell options (bash 3.2+, zsh); the hook names the
  exchange with a fresh token (OSC `9280;P;<token>`; a reused or missing token is cancelled); the app always ends it
  with ONE frame, `RS <token> : <%HH text> US` (RS = 0x1e, US = 0x1f), or the cancel frame `RS - : US`. The hook and
  the RS widget at the prompt consume nothing outside a frame: the first byte must be RS, then the frame's exact shape
  (`(<digits>x<digits>x<digits> | -) : (%HH)* US`), judged by CONTENT only with no inter-byte timing (a frame may
  arrive in pieces with any pauses; the only clock is the overall read deadline `PHOSPHOR_NC_DEADLINE`, a give-up net
  that hands back what was read and writes nothing); on the first byte that cannot continue a frame everything read goes back to the line editor, an Enter
  included (bash: ^Y and RS are macros that run the function and then a key it rebinds to accept-line), and a
  terminal reply (a DA report) is dropped whole. US is not bound (it stays the line editor's undo). App: an exchange
  starts only when the write queue is empty, no command is executing, the line editor is active and no other write
  path is engaged (including a `SetupChunked` job the writer still holds: `SetupLive` counts it until the writer
  drops it); while it waits
  for its prompt, ANY write (a command, typed or pasted bytes, agent bytes, ^C) first writes the cancel frame, then
  goes out, in order. The 2 s prompt timeout is a give-up that WRITES NOTHING: it closes the requester's channel (the
  completer answers) and marks the cancel frame owed; the owed cancel goes in front of the next real write, or when the
  shell's own late prompt arrives, exactly once (`the_cancel_owed_after_a_timeout_precedes_the_next_write_exactly_once`,
  `a_late_prompt_after_the_timeout_gets_the_cancel_once`). Nothing is queued behind `^Y`, so there is nothing to hold, hand back or reorder; the shell
  leaving first just ends the exchange. Unit tests (`pty_controller_tests.rs`, through the real write APIs):
  `native_completions_frames_are_self_identifying_and_never_end_a_line`,
  `an_exchange_starts_only_when_nothing_is_queued_or_running`,
  `writes_during_an_exchange_go_out_in_order_after_the_cancel_frame` (an editor command and agent bytes; the queue
  stays empty), `a_direct_byte_write_during_an_exchange_is_preceded_by_the_cancel_frame` (bytes, paste, ^C),
  `the_prompt_is_answered_with_one_frame_and_later_writes_follow_it`, `a_reused_or_missing_prompt_token_is_cancelled`,
  `prompt_timeout_cancels_without_a_toast_for_a_remote_first_request` (now: the timeout writes nothing),
  `prompt_timeout_of_a_fallback_request_asks_for_the_toast`,
  `keys_after_the_prompt_timeout_and_a_late_prompt_lose_nothing` (#1674/H14: `^Y`, timeout cancel, keys, command, then a
  late prompt: the tty order is kept and the late prompt writes nothing; same for Legacy and Table, the pty layer is
  shared), `a_second_request_while_one_is_in_flight_is_refused`,
  `the_shell_leaving_ends_the_exchange_without_a_frame`,
  `an_exchange_does_not_start_while_the_writer_holds_a_setup_job`,
  `a_setup_write_during_an_exchange_is_preceded_by_the_cancel_frame`; terminal-query replies and a resize do not pass
  through the cancel-first rule (why each is safe: the design comment); `native_shell_completions_need_the_advertised_protocol_and_bash_4`
  (`warp_terminal`); `completions_prompt_token_is_letters_and_digits_only` (`ansi/mod_test.rs`). Tab then a fast
  Enter runs the COMPLETED line remotely too: the editor holds the Enter for the in-band answer with NO time budget
  (`REMOTE_NATIVE_TAB_ENTER_BUDGET` is gone; owner decision: no timer decides what Enter runs). The answer is an
  event: candidates run the completed line however late; an answer of nothing (the shell found none, or the app
  cancelled the exchange: the cancel sends an empty result) runs the typed line and the completer answers the menu;
  The remote as-you-type completer listing has no debounce timer any more (`REMOTE_AS_YOU_TYPE_DEBOUNCE` is gone; it
  only ever delayed the ssh side-command listing, never the `^Y`): it is single flight, latest wins (`RemoteListingFlight`:
  a keystroke while a listing runs holds only the newest request, replayed when the listing ends if still current; an
  explicit Tab supersedes without a replay; `test_remote_as_you_type_listing_is_single_flight_latest_wins`, pure and
  mode-independent). A hung listing is freed by EVENTS, no timer: the next Precmd, ExitShell/Exit, `SSHControlMasterError`, `PreInteractiveSSHSession` or a cwd change aborts it and drops the held request (`end_remote_listing_on_event`; `test_remote_listing_event_frees_a_hung_flight`); each flight step logs `hop=listing_inflight event=<start|held|replay|drop|abort> gen=<n>` through the input-order log (`log_hop`; generation only, never buffer text; format pinned by `test_listing_inflight_hop_detail_format`; the lab case `nohelper_listing_single_flight` reads it); the cancel closure and the result callback both go through `remote_listing_finished`, so the replay does not depend on which runs first.
  The shell's Precmd/ExitShell/Exit ends an exchange awaiting its RESULTS too (an event beats the 15 s net, which only
  drops state and writes/releases nothing; `the_shell_leaving_during_the_results_wait_ends_the_exchange_by_event`,
  `the_results_net_drops_the_exchange_and_writes_nothing`);
  a second Tab for the same text while an exchange is in flight attaches to it (Tab, Tab, Enter runs the completed line;
  a cancelled first exchange runs the typed line; `a_second_tab_for_the_same_text_gets_the_first_exchanges_answer`,
  `an_attached_tab_follows_the_cancel_and_the_give_up_of_the_exchange`, pty layer shared by Legacy and Table); a different
  text is refused;
  NO answer at all (the pty's 2 s give-up closes the channel, or the shell left) hands the line back and runs nothing
  (`give_up_unanswered_remote_hold`, #1577/#1666), keys typed meanwhile held in order. Only the 9 s hold backstop
  remains as a lost-signal net with the same hand-back. Tab-path timers left: pty 2 s prompt give-up (writes nothing),
  hook read deadline 20 s (writes nothing), results timeout 15 s (writes nothing), 9 s hold backstop (hands back),
  and the local Tab's 150 ms cap / 500 ms backstop (hand back, never run) (`input_test.rs`, Legacy and Table):
  `test_tab_then_enter_remote_in_band_answer_runs_the_completed_line_in_both_modes`,
  `test_tab_then_enter_remote_in_band_give_up_runs_nothing_in_both_modes`,
  `test_tab_then_enter_remote_in_band_keys_typed_during_hold_follow_the_completed_line`,
  `test_tab_then_enter_remote_native_miss_submits_the_visible_line_at_once_in_both_modes`,
  `test_remote_native_miss_without_enter_makes_the_next_enter_not_wait_in_both_modes`. Known limits: a quoted word
  with spaces is not one token to the app; a backslash-escaped word is not dequoted before bash's compgen; a byte
  outside a frame that is not text, ^P or a bracketed paste cannot be handed back by bash (only a writer outside the
  app could put one there: the app sends the cancel frame before any write).
  Every shell writes candidates as the whole whitespace-delimited token (zsh now adds its
  IPREFIX and -P/-p prefixes, so `cd dir/fo` no longer offers `foo/`). The OSC parser rejoins a payload split at `;`
  (`completions_osc_payload_rejoins_a_payload_split_at_semicolons`). Shell side: `script/test_native_completions` (also: a frame split with 0.5 s and 3 s pauses is consumed whole with
  no junk, RS + `ls` + Enter and RS + letters + Ctrl-C hand back by content, a stale-token frame is consumed; ESC after RS is classified by the NEXT byte, not by time: DA / OSC / DCS XTVERSION replies are dropped whole, an arrow, Alt-x and a lone ESC + Enter are handed back).
  Kill switch: `PHOSPHOR_REMOTE_NATIVE_COMPLETIONS=0`.
- **Chips re-run when the session registers.** A remote session's blocks carry its id before its bootstrap completes
  (the ssh setup holds the bootstrap while it checks for the helper), so chips refreshed then failed with "could not
  prepare execution context" and the refresh after the bootstrap, with an unchanged block and cwd, was skipped by the
  #1167 dedupe. The dedupe key now includes whether the session is registered
  (`test_chips_rerun_when_the_blocks_session_registers` in `current_prompt_test.rs`).

App case `remote_tab_no_helper` (`appci/cases_caseremote.py`, full tier, both modes; Git Bash pane on Windows, where the session is managed on one connection since #1933, so the in-band line is required there as everywhere): the
harness default `ssh_extension_install_mode = never_install` IS the helper-missing setup. Creates `~/phxtab_<tok>/` on
the remote side only (and `phxtab_local_only/` locally), `ssh fake`, types `cd phxtab_<counter>_<1 char>` (`tok_prefix`: unique per trial; the old 3-char prefix `t12` was shared by t126-t128 and made Tab ambiguous, r18w6), Tab, waits 1.5 s
(3 s with a delay applied), Enter. Pass: the REMOTE rec.log's command is `cd phxtab_<tok>/`, the next remote `pwd` ends in
`/phxtab_<tok>`, nothing reached the local shell, and the app log has `candidates from the remote shell in N ms`
(metric `remote_tab_in_band_ms`). `remote_tab_enter_no_helper` (same setup, ctx.count(3) trials): Tab, Enter 30 ms later;
the remote rec.log must hold the COMPLETED `cd phxte_<tok>/`, never the typed prefix. Both RUN on macOS since #1969
(they used to skip there: the test host's remote shell is /bin/bash 3.2, which now answers the exchange), so the macOS
rows of these two cases are the real-app proof of the bash 3.2 path. No fish remote case: fish is off the path.

**bash 3.2 (#1969; macOS `/bin/bash`, the usual remote shell on a Mac).** The exchange is the same wire protocol; the
text to complete travels in the app's frame, so the answer never needed `READLINE_LINE`. What bash below 4.0 lacks is a
way for a `bind -x` function to put a byte back into the line, so there the hook queues what it must hand back as the
KEYS it read, and `__warp_nc_finish` rebinds the macro's second key (`\C-x\C-_9`) to a macro of exactly those keys:
readline runs it right after the function, in front of anything still in the tty, so order is kept. That macro can
carry an escape, so an arrow or an Alt-key read where a frame was expected goes back whole (4.0+ can only drop it); a
bracketed paste's text is queued with `^V` in front of every control byte, so a pasted newline is inserted, not run.
Three more things differ below 4.0 and are handled in the bootstrap: `read` has no `-N`, so the byte read uses
`-n 1 -d ''` (a newline is then a byte, not an empty delimiter); readline moves to a NEW line before a `bind -x`
function instead of clearing the current one, so the hook first writes cursor-up + erase-line; and the DEBUG trap
cannot see a readline binding by `READLINE_LINE`, so it returns for the hook's commands by name (and while the hook's
`__warp_nc_running` flag is set), or every Tab would send a Preexec with no CommandFinished (the same defect existed
for the prompt-mode keys ESC p / ESC w on bash 3.2: #2002, same guard). App side: `Shell::supports_native_shell_completions`
takes an advertising bash from 3.2 (unknown version: no); `PHOSPHOR_BASH3_NATIVE_COMPLETIONS=0` turns bash below 4.0
alone off (`bash3_native_completions_kill_switch_reads_only_zero_as_off`), `PHOSPHOR_REMOTE_NATIVE_COMPLETIONS=0` the
whole in-band path as before. Checked with the real bootstrap in bash 3.2.57, 4.0, 4.3, 4.4, 5.1 and 5.3 in a pty
(`script/test_native_completions --bash-image bash:3.2 ...`); not compiled, and not run in the app.
Both read the remote rec.log through `remote_cmds_after`, which drops the harness's own `~/.appci_where` probes: the precondition probe's
line can reach rec.log AFTER the mark is taken (round 7: both cases failed with only the probe 'received' while the completed `cd` ran).

Lab spec, netem 150 ms (manual; needs root, the harness never applies it): on the Linux box,
`sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 75ms` (150 ms round trip on loopback, where the fake sshd listens), run
`remote_tab_no_helper` with `PHOSPHOR_APPCI_NETEM_NOTE="lo netem 75ms"` (recorded as a note, longer settle), then
`sudo tc qdisc del dev lo root`. Pass as above, with `remote_tab_in_band_ms` below ~2 round trips plus the shell's own
completion time; typing during the Tab must not lag (the editor never waits on the handshake). The helper-missing
"install refused" variant is the same case with `ssh_extension_install_mode = always_ask` and "Continue without
installing" chosen.

**Path detection without the helper (a pushed cwd listing).** On a remote session path detection reads directory listings
from a cache only (#1295, never a command per keystroke), so without a recent Tab a typed directory (`cd somedir`) was not
recognised. The remote bootstrap now sends the listing itself: `__phosphor_cwd_listing` (`bash_body.sh`, `zsh_body.sh`,
`fish.sh`) appends `"cwd_listing"` to the Precmd JSON when the cwd or its contents changed since the last one it sent, and
only when `WARP_IS_LOCAL_SHELL_SESSION` is not `1` (a local listing is already fast; kill switch `PHOSPHOR_CWD_LISTING=0`).
Entries only, with a dir flag (`d` follows symlinks), hidden files included, names `%HH`-encoded outside
`[A-Za-z0-9._+@,=~-]` so no filename can break the JSON or the DCS. Bounds: `P` (cut) at 500 entries or 32 KB, `T` (too
large, no entries, and the directory is not globbed again until a `cd`) above 2000. No fork anywhere: the glob, the
`-d` test and the encoding are builtins (fish: `string escape --style=url`). Freshness is the listing itself: it is rebuilt
at each prompt of a listable directory and sent only when it differs from the last one sent, so a file a command creates is
in the next prompt's payload; a file created outside the session shows at the next prompt. The app parses it
(`app/src/completer/pushed_listing.rs`, unit tests `pushed_listing_tests.rs`) into a per-session slot keyed to the pwd it
came with; `SessionContext::list_directory_entries` answers from it before the 2 s cache, the failed-listing memory or any
remote command: a complete listing answers every consumer, a truncated one only the per-keystroke ones (highlighting,
suggestions), never an explicit Tab (`test_pushed_cwd_listing_answers_background_contexts_without_a_remote_command`,
`test_truncated_pushed_listing_is_not_used_for_explicit_listing` in `completer/test.rs`). The app logs
`hop=cwd_listing session=<id> kind=<L|P|T> entries=<n>` per listing and `hop=path_detect source=pushed session=<id>
entries=<n> complete=<bool>` (at most every 250 ms): ids and counts only. Shell side: `script/test_cwd_listing`
(timings printed). App side: `lab_path_detect` (above). Measured on the dev box, per call of `__phosphor_cwd_listing`
with a rebuild forced (steady state is the same glob with a string compare), 10 / 500 / 2000 / 10000 entries: bash 0.3 / 4.9 / 6.9 / 7.4 ms, zsh 0.1 / 3.2 / 10 / 31 ms, fish 1.3 / 21 / 25 / 17 ms (fish's own prompt is ~46 ms either way). The 10000-entry directory is globbed once per `cd` (`T`), not per prompt: a `true` there costs the same as in an empty directory (bash 14 vs 12 ms, zsh 4.0 vs 4.1, fish 46 vs 47).



## Remote helper client switch (Wave H step 5, #1804)

What changed for tests and CI when the GitLab download of the full app binary was removed and the bundled `phosphor-remote` helper became the ssh remote server. Nothing the app installs is fetched: the helper is gzip-compressed inside the app bundle (`<bundled_resources>/remote/phosphor-remote-<os>-<arch>.gz`), uploaded IN-BAND over the existing ControlMaster (`ssh::run_ssh_script_with_payload`: `bash -s` reads the install script, which ends in one call to `main`, so `gunzip -c` inside it receives the gzip bytes that follow the script on the same stdin; scp is the fallback), verified against a SHA-256 compiled into the client, started once (`--version`) before anything older is removed, and linked as `current`.

- `crates/remote_server/src/setup_tests.rs`: the install script is driven with real bash and a gzip payload on stdin. `in_band_upload_installs_verifies_and_links_the_helper` (mode 0755, `current` link, a created dir is 0700, no `.up*` leftovers), `staged_upload_installs_and_removes_the_staged_file` (the scp-fallback shape), `a_helper_failing_the_pinned_digest_is_rejected_with_the_integrity_code` (exit 6, nothing installed), `no_pinned_digest_is_refused_before_anything_is_read` (exit 4), `unusable_digest_tool_reports_no_digest_tool_never_a_mismatch` (exit 5, three broken tools shadowed on PATH), `an_empty_or_broken_stream_is_an_upload_failure_not_a_verdict` (exit 7, and a failed run removes a directory it created), `a_helper_that_does_not_start_is_removed_and_old_versions_are_kept` (exit 9), `install_leaves_exactly_one_version_and_removes_the_legacy_app_binary`, the exit-code reserved-status and uniqueness checks, the tilde-expansion test (the probe now closes `main`), `nothing_in_the_install_path_can_reach_the_network`, `digest_decision_fails_closed_unless_a_source_build_computed_its_own`, `install_script_renders_every_placeholder`, `the_script_ends_in_a_single_call_so_the_payload_stays_unread`. Removed with the download (owner decision, #1804): the GitLab URL test, the curl-shim download tests and the tarball install tests. Changed: `binary_name()` is `phosphor-remote`, the staged upload is `.upload.gz`, the digest-mismatch headline says the install was not retried.
- `app/src/remote_server/ssh_transport.rs` tests: `classify_install_failure` now has exit 7 as the only script-level transport failure (plus 255 and `Other`), exit 3 (no gunzip/gzip) is fatal, `exit_codes_in_install_script_are_all_classified` follows the script's `EXIT_*` table, `remote_proxy_command_quotes_identity_key` expects `<versioned helper path> proxy <key>`, and `gzip_round_trip_hashes_the_decompressed_bytes`, `a_non_gzip_bundle_is_an_error_not_a_hash`, `unavailable_helper_message_names_the_platform_and_the_fallback` cover the local preparation.
- `crates/remote_server/src/policy_tests.rs`: per-host consent. Default `ask` follows the app-wide `ssh_extension_install_mode`; a host's own `allow`/`never` beats it; only `never` stops an existing helper being updated; `never` wins if a host is in both settings lists (`warpify.ssh.remote_helper_allowed_hosts`, `warpify.ssh.remote_helper_denied_hosts`, keyed `user@host`). The choice block's *Don't ask me again for this host* (en; ja and zh-CN translated) now stores that for the host instead of changing the app-wide mode.
