The appci selftest (`agent_file_edit_pieces`) checks the `MIXED` builder and that a one-ending rewrite of a mixed file is judged a failure.

`agent_edit_touch_only` (local) and `lab_fam_agent_edit_touch_only` (nohelper, upload): the mtime moves, the bytes do not, then accept: it must succeed with no conflict report (local: `warp_files::save_if_unchanged` compares content; remote nohelper: the size+mtime `Expect` may give a false conflict until branch `fix/1837-remote-edit-conflict` lands, a FAIL there is that defect). The lab edit cases (`conflict`, `endings`, `touch_only`) now require `hop=backend_route family=file_write` with nohelper -> shell, upload -> helper: `RoutedBackend::save_buffer_content` and `write_file_expecting` log it (the buffer-protocol save used to log none). Per-hunk accept stays unbuilt (all-or-nothing UI; deliberate note, no case).

Unit/contract tests for the #1837 guard (run on the box with the usual suites): `backend/contract_tests.rs` `the_shell_backend_refuses_a_stale_guarded_write` and `the_helper_refuses_a_stale_guarded_write` (same assertions on both backends: matching hash and `Absent` write, a user edit / appeared / deleted file writes nothing and leaves the user's bytes and no temp file); `backend/router_tests.rs` `a_guarded_write_with_no_way_to_check_is_refused_and_leaves_the_file`; `daemon/fs_ops_tests.rs` `write_file_with_an_expectation_writes_only_when_it_holds`; `capability.rs` `write_expect_is_never_assumed_for_a_legacy_daemon`; `warp_files` `remote_write_expectation_names_the_exact_bytes_that_were_read`; `code_diff_view_tests.rs` `toast_message_carries_the_remote_host_conflict` (the accept surfaces the host's refusal in the toast and the `Failed to save file for accepted AgentMode diffs` log line).

#1837 follow-ups. (1) Remote DELETE carries the same expectation: `DeleteFile.expect` (optional `WriteExpect`, the SHA-256 `delete_file_if_unchanged`'s read approved, via `remote_write_expectation`), capability `file_delete_expect`, `RoutedBackend::delete_file_expecting` (helper that lists the capability, else the guarded shell script `posix_guarded_delete_command` / `pwsh_guarded_delete_command`, else REFUSED, never an unguarded delete), `warp_files` refuses when it has no exact hash to send. Tests: `contract_tests.rs` `the_shell_backend_refuses_a_stale_guarded_delete` and `the_helper_refuses_a_stale_guarded_delete` (same assertions: user edit -> nothing removed and the message says `not deleted`; matching hash deletes; already gone is an error); `router_tests.rs` `a_guarded_delete_with_no_way_to_check_is_refused_and_leaves_the_file`; `daemon/fs_ops_tests.rs` `delete_file_with_an_expectation_deletes_only_when_it_holds`; `capability.rs` (same test as for the write capability); `shellcmd/write_tests.rs` `a_guarded_delete_checks_before_it_removes_and_the_plain_one_stays_plain`; lab case `lab_fam_agent_delete_conflict` (above). (2) A host with no `sha256sum`, `shasum` or `Get-FileHash`: the guarded script exits `EXIT_NO_HASH` (6, output `NOHASH`), distinct from the conflict exit 5, and the message is `could not check that the file on the host is unchanged (no sha256 tool), so nothing was written` (or `deleted`), never `changed on the host`; still fail closed. Tests: `write_tests.rs` `a_hash_guarded_script_reports_a_missing_hash_tool_apart_from_a_conflict` (script outcome and message), `contract_tests.rs` `a_host_with_no_sha256_tool_refuses_guarded_changes_and_says_why` (a local `sh` whose PATH has base64 but no hash tool: write and delete leave the file, no temp file, truthful message; an `Absent` guard still works). `file_delete_expect` is registered as `fam_file_delete_expect` in `cases_lab_helper.py` like `file_write_expect`. Self-test: `agent_file_edit_pieces` also covers the deletion prompt and report matcher.

The lab coverage guard (`lab_helper_coverage_guard`) needs every helper capability to have a lab case with a helper arm; `file_write_expect` is registered as `fam_file_write_expect` in `cases_lab_helper.py`, which always skips and names `lab_fam_agent_edit_conflict` as the real proof.

Partial accept: the diff card has no per-hunk accept (Up/Down only navigate hunks), so accept is all or none; each case records that as a note. A case that cannot reach its precondition (no action card, or the first Enter already applied the edit when a reject was wanted) is UNVERIFIABLE, never a pass. A clobber of the user's change is a FAIL on every arm, including the helper arm.

Run: `APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1 python3 script/realapp/appci/run.py --cases 'agent_edit_*'` (agent mode); the lab pair with `--cases 'lab_fam_agent_edit_*'` (needs the lab; `upload` arms need `APPCI_LAB_HELPER_BIN`). Platforms: Linux and Mac; not Windows (`winmap.NOT_WINDOWS`). Self-test: `agent_file_edit_pieces` (fake-model reply, expected-bytes builder, judges).

## Agent-mode latency and the fast steer (#1828)
Three appci cases in `script/realapp/appci/cases_agent_latency.py`, agent pass only (`modes=("agent",)`), all `gui=True`. They need the scripted fake model (`APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1`, `fake_model.py`) and skip with the reason without it. The fake model gained a **slow steady stream**: any conversation whose user turns contain `STREAMLONG` is answered by 240 six-character pieces 50 ms apart (about 12 s, flushed as produced, sticky for the rest of that conversation) and every `/api/chat` request body is kept in `fake_model.FakeModel.ACTIVE.reqs` (`{"t", "messages"}`), which is the steer oracle.
- **`agent_latency_key`**: key -> first frame built, from the app's own log. A key that never reaches the pty (the agent input) has no echo, so the old `frame` line never fires for it; the app now also logs `input_order hop=key_frame layout=<bool> t=<ms>` for the first frame after any key-down (tiny hook in `crates/warpui_core/src/input_order.rs`, separate flag from the pty-echo `frame` line, which is unchanged). Samples: agent input idle, and agent input while a fake reply streams (only keys typed 0.3-11 s after that request count; the stream is restarted every 30 keys and cancelled with Ctrl-C). Reference: the same measure typed into the **terminal-mode input editor** of the same session (half before, half after the agent phases, so drift shows in `lat.evaluate`'s block-drift rule). Verdict: overhead (agent median minus terminal-editor median) against `APPCI_KEY_BUDGET_MS` (2 ms) by `lat.evaluate` (2 SE; thin evidence is `noref`, never a pass). Also the UI-work rule of `latency_key_log` (`hop=ui_item` event/action items >= 4 ms while typing; frame items WARN). Records: `lat.agent_latency_key/idle`, `.../streaming`. Skips (not passes) on a build without the hook.
- **Render-latency step A: measurement hops, metrics only (`docs/design/render-latency.md`, #1848 #1843 #1838).** No behaviour change; every new field is an `input_order` hop, parsed by `appci/render_hops.py` (`render_hop_metrics`, `record`; self-test `render_latency_step_a_hops_parse`). macOS: `hop=key_presented submit_to_presented_ms= key_to_presented_ms= sync=<0|1> wait_ms=` for each presented KEY frame (submit = the moment `warp_frame_track_drawable` runs, a little before encode/commit, so it slightly over-counts by the encode time; `sync` = `CAMetalLayer.displaySyncEnabled` at submit); `hop=key_frame_sched ms=` = `request_redraw`/`render_scene` of a key-driven frame -> `warp_update_layer` entry (the dispatch_async turn + CA commit hop); `hop=frame_skip_run ... key_frame_skipped=<n>` = how many of the run's skipped frames were key-driven (the #1838 gate is not key-aware). The key tag for the last two is a measurement-only twin of `warpNextFrameFromKey` in `host_view.m` (set by `keyDownImpl`, consumed by `displayLayer:` even when display-sync-off-while-typing is disabled). Linux/Windows: `hop=frame_drawn ... acquire_ms= present_ms=` (`present_ms` = time inside `surface_texture.present()`, 0 when the frame did not present; `acquire_ms` already existed). `latency_paint`, `ctrl_c_flood_ab` (per gate arm, prefix `ctrl_c_flood_gate_<on|off>_`) and `agent_latency_key` (prefixes `agent_idle_` / `agent_streaming_`) record p50/p95/max of each field as metrics (`key_submit_to_presented_ms`, `key_to_presented_ms_hop`, `key_presented_wait_ms`, `key_presented_sync_on/off`, `key_frame_sched_ms`, `key_frames_skipped`, `frame_present_ms`, `frame_acquire_ms`); a note says when a build logs none of them. No new verdicts. Decision rule from the design: submit->presented about one composite period -> option E; key_frame_sched >= 1 ms -> B; Linux present_ms >= 8 under streaming -> F default change. Unverified until the first Mac/Linux run (no cargo here); the `acquire_ms=\S+ present_ms=` shape of `frame_drawn` changed, `cases_agent_latency.FRAME_DRAWN_RE` and `windows/agentkey/an2.py` accept both.
- **`agent_latency_key` present-mode A/B (design option F, Linux only, metrics + notes).** After the judged default run the case relaunches the app per block (`App.extra_env`, new for the Linux launcher; `render_hops.arm_schedule`: two rounds of default / `PHOSPHOR_KEY_FRAME_NOW=0` (`keynow_off`). The original `PHOSPHOR_PRESENT_MODE=mailbox` and `PHOSPHOR_FRAME_LATENCY=1` arms were dropped after round 8, owner decision: raw -0.92 / +0.52 ms, slot-adjusted +0.1 ms both, i.e. no effect; the metric names stay `present_mode_ab_<arm>`. First `APPCI_LAT_BLOCK_LEAD` samples of each block discarded) and types keys while a fake reply streams (`stream_keys`). Metrics `present_mode_ab_<arm>` (streaming raw and slot-adjusted key->frame stats, `present_ms`, `acquire_ms`) and `present_mode_ab_deltas` (arm minus default, p50, raw and slot-adjusted; negative = faster), plus one note per arm. A failed relaunch or skipped block is a WARN note (`ArmR`), never a verdict; the final relaunch with the default environment is a real check. `APPCI_RENDER_AB=0` turns the A/B off. macOS and Windows skip it (no such switch / launcher).

- **`agent_latency_key` key-frame-now A/B (#1843, Linux, metrics + notes; `docs/design/1843-1848-latency.md`).** Round 8 showed the streaming penalty (raw 7.24 ms over the terminal editor) is winit's Wayland frame-callback throttle: `RedrawRequested` is withheld while a callback is outstanding, so a key typed after a streaming frame waits up to a refresh before its frame is even built (`present_ms` / `acquire_ms` are 0.1-0.2 ms; the mailbox and frame-latency arms change nothing). The app now draws a key's frame at the end of the loop iteration that handled the key when the window is still invalidated (Wayland, a present mode that never waits; kill switch `PHOSPHOR_KEY_FRAME_NOW=0`, default ON), logging `hop=key_frame_now wait_ms=<acquire + present>` per such frame and `hop=key_frame_now_off` if two in a row block (the path then turns itself off for the window). The JUDGED run is unchanged (default environment = path on; raw streaming delta against the terminal editor, 2 ms budget; the slot-adjusted delta stays a metric): with the fix the streaming p50 should sit near the idle one. The A/B blocks have the arm `keynow_off` (`render_hops.ARMS` is default / keynow_off; it was default / keynow_off / mailbox / lat1 until the mailbox and lat1 arms were dropped), so the fix and the old behaviour are measured in the same run: `present_mode_ab_<arm>` now also carries `key_frames_now`, `key_frames_now_off` and `key_frame_now_wait_ms`, and the note `#1843 key-frame-now A/B (streaming key->frame p50): on ... / off ...` gives both medians and the counts. WARN notes (`render_hops.key_frame_now_warns`): the keynow_off arm logged `hop=key_frame_now` (the switch did not reach the app), the default arm logged none (X11, a present mode that waits, or an old build: both arms are the same measurement), or the path switched itself off. `render_hops.render_hop_metrics` parses the new lines on every platform (`key_frames_now`, `key_frames_now_drawn` (macOS), `key_frames_now_off`, `key_frame_now_wait_ms` (Linux), `key_frame_now_ms` (macOS)), so `agent_streaming_*` / `agent_idle_*` and `latency_paint` record them too. Unit: `crates/warpui/src/windowing/winit/event_loop/key_frame_tests.rs` (`a_key_with_an_undrawn_invalidation_is_drawn_at_the_end_of_the_iteration`, `without_a_key_nothing_bypasses_the_frame_callback`, `a_key_is_offered_once_and_many_keys_in_one_iteration_make_one_frame`, `a_frame_drawn_in_the_same_iteration_satisfies_the_key`, `every_fact_is_required`, `two_blocked_frames_in_a_row_turn_the_path_off_for_the_window`, `a_fast_frame_between_two_slow_ones_keeps_the_path_on`, `only_zero_is_the_kill_switch`, `the_hop_detail_is_the_shape_the_harness_parses`) and `rendering/wgpu/resources_tests.rs` (`present_never_waits_only_for_immediate_and_mailbox`). Self-test: `render_latency_step_a_hops_parse` (the new lines, the arm list, the WARNs). Not built or run yet.
- **Per-key frame build split: `hop=key_frame_build`, metrics only (#1961, `docs/design/key-scene-build.md`).** No behaviour change and no verdict. Round 8 showed the per-key frame build is 0.8-2.0 ms at the median (the "4 ms" of the earlier documents was the >= 4 ms tail `hop=ui_item` logs), and that its stages, the views it is spent in and the synthetic mouse-move after it are not measured. The first frame built after a key-down now logs `input_order hop=key_frame_build passes= layout_passes= views= mounted= render_ms= layout_ms= after_layout_ms= paint_ms= hover_ms= total_ms= layout_top= paint_top=` (`views` = views re-rendered, `mounted` = views in the tree, `hover_ms` = the synthetic mouse-move after the build, `passes` > 1 = the frame was laid out and painted again in the same build, `*_top` = `ViewType:ms,...` for the three view types with the largest self time; type names only, never text). `appci/render_hops.py` (`render_hop_metrics`) parses it on every platform, so the cases that call `render_hops.record` (`latency_paint`, `agent_latency_key` with its `agent_idle_` / `agent_streaming_` prefixes, `ctrl_c_flood_ab` per arm) record `key_frame_builds`, `key_frame_builds_multi_pass`, `key_frame_build_<render|layout|after_layout|paint|hover|total|other>_ms`, `key_frame_build_views`, `key_frame_build_mounted` and `key_frame_build_<layout|paint>_top_ms` ({view type: mean self ms per key frame}; each line names only its three largest, so a type's mean is a lower bound). No case was added and no expectation changed. Unit: `crates/warpui_core/src/frame_split_tests.rs` (`self_time_leaves_out_the_child_views`, `a_view_visited_twice_is_two_entries_and_an_unmatched_exit_is_ignored`, `top_views_adds_up_a_type_and_names_the_three_largest`, `passes_add_up_and_a_paint_only_pass_adds_no_layout`, `the_detail_is_the_line_the_harness_parses`), `presenter_tests.rs` (`test_view_timing_records_each_visited_view_and_nothing_when_off`), `input_order.rs` (`the_key_frame_build_line_is_the_hop_the_harness_parses`). Self-test: `key_frame_build_hop_parses`. Not built or run yet.
- **A typed character re-renders only the views it changed (#1962, option A of `docs/design/key-scene-build.md`; kill switch `PHOSPHOR_KEY_VIEW_SKIP=0`, default ON).** Round 8 showed 2 (terminal typing), 4 (agent typing) and 6 (`latency_paint`) views re-rendered per key frame; each view other than the editor was notified by a call that did not compare what the view shows. Each now compares before it notifies (the rule and the per-view cause are in section 8 of the design document); only notifications are skipped, no key is read, held or routed differently. `app/src/util/key_view_skip.rs` holds the switch (read once; `input_order hop=key_view_skip enabled=<0|1>` is logged at the first use, so a log names its arm) and `display_changed`. The decisions are pure functions with the switch as a parameter, each tested for (a) a typed character that leaves the view's display as it is does not notify, (b) a change of what it displays does, (c) the switch off notifies always. Unit tests: `app/src/util/key_view_skip_tests.rs` (`only_zero_is_the_kill_switch`, `an_unchanged_display_is_not_notified_and_a_changed_one_is`, `with_the_kill_switch_every_change_notifies`); the autosuggestion keybinding hint, `app/src/editor/accept_autosuggestion_keybinding_view_tests.rs` (`an_edit_with_the_menu_closed_does_not_rerender_the_hint`, `closing_an_open_menu_rerenders_the_hint`, `with_the_kill_switch_every_close_rerenders`; #1993: a changed keybinding now notifies the hint itself); the two message bars compare the ROW they would draw with the row their last render drew (`Message::display_fingerprint` / `display_fingerprint_with`: text, keystrokes, icons, colors, and the clickable groups a bar vouches for; a link, a chip, an image or any other clickable group makes the row incomparable, which renders), so a row left stale by state without a notification of its own is still corrected at the next key: `app/src/terminal/input/message_bar/mod_tests.rs` (`equal_messages_have_equal_fingerprints_and_any_visible_change_differs`, `a_message_with_a_click_handler_or_an_image_has_no_fingerprint`, `a_clickable_group_in_a_vouched_slot_is_compared_by_what_it_shows`, `a_row_event_renders_only_when_the_row_differs_or_cannot_be_judged`), `app/src/terminal/input/terminal_message_bar_tests.rs` (`an_event_that_leaves_the_row_as_drawn_does_not_rerender`, `an_event_that_changes_the_row_or_cannot_be_judged_rerenders`, and on a real terminal view `the_first_typed_character_keeps_the_default_row_and_a_command_prefix_changes_it`), `app/src/ai/blocklist/agent_view/agent_message_bar_tests.rs` (`a_slash_event_that_changes_neither_the_state_nor_the_row_does_not_rerender`, `a_slash_event_rerenders_when_the_state_or_the_row_changed`); the agent status bar on an empty <-> non-empty change of a shell-mode buffer (its `render` reads nothing of the buffer; skipped only when the last render drew nothing and one now would draw nothing), `app/src/ai/blocklist/block/status_bar_tests.rs` (`an_empty_state_change_does_not_rerender_a_bar_that_draws_nothing`, `an_empty_state_change_rerenders_a_bar_that_drew_or_would_draw_something`, and on a real terminal view `a_terminal_mode_status_bar_is_known_to_draw_nothing`); the input button bar on the same change (only its segmented control reads the empty state and is still notified; the bar itself renders again only when what it is built from differs from its last render), `app/src/terminal/universal_developer_input_tests.rs` (`the_first_typed_character_does_not_rerender_the_bar_itself`, `a_bar_that_would_be_built_differently_is_rerendered`, `an_unknown_side_is_rerendered`, `with_the_kill_switch_every_empty_state_change_rerenders_the_bar`); the agent input itself, which was rendered again for every edit in an agent view and now only when a fact its render branches on differs from its last render (`AgentInputDisplayFacts`: empty buffer, detected slash command, input type and lock, the kind of open menu, banner, attachments, workflow info, voltron, focus, x-ray, shortcuts, inline view, queued-prompts panel, pane height), `app/src/terminal/input/agent_tests.rs` (`one_more_character_in_a_non_empty_buffer_does_not_rerender_the_agent_input`, `an_edit_that_changes_a_fact_the_agent_input_is_built_from_rerenders_it` (one case per fact), `an_input_not_yet_rendered_as_the_agent_input_is_rendered`, `with_the_kill_switch_every_edit_rerenders_the_agent_input`); the queued-prompts panel, which is not rendered while it is hidden and stays hidden, and now tells the input when it appears or disappears (#1994, `QueuedPromptsPanelEvent::ShownChanged`), `app/src/terminal/view/queued_prompts_panel_tests.rs` (`a_hidden_panel_is_not_rerendered_for_typing`, `a_shown_panel_and_a_panel_that_changes_visibility_are_rerendered`, `with_the_kill_switch_every_event_rerenders`). **Same-run A/B: `latency_key_views_ab`** (`script/realapp/appci/cases_viewskip_ab.py`; PROVING; Linux, macOS and Windows (`winmap.BOTH`), terminal and agent mode; on Windows `WindowsApp.extra_env` is merged last into the dict `WindowsApp.env()` builds, which `_spawn` hands to `Popen(env=...)` for the suspended-then-job-assigned app process, so the variable is in the Phosphor process's own environment; pinned by self-test `windows_app_extra_env_reaches_spawn_1962`). Like `latency_paint_ab`: blocks alternate between the default environment and `PHOSPHOR_KEY_VIEW_SKIP=0` (`cases_ctrlc_ab.ab_schedule`), one relaunch per block, the lead key frames of every block dropped. Per block two typing patterns, each read from the app's own `hop=key_frame_build` lines (#1961): `first` = `latency_paint`'s pattern (a character into the empty input, then Delete, a pause between keys; on macOS posted by kl3 through `cases.paint_samples`, which also gives key -> first changed pixel) and `burst` = lines of 10 characters at 10-25 ms/key into a non-empty input. Metrics `key_view_skip_on` / `key_view_skip_off` (per pattern: `key_frames`, `views`, `render_ms`, `layout_ms`, `total_ms`; `key_to_paint` on macOS; `skip_flags` = the `hop=key_view_skip enabled=` values of the arm's launches) and `key_view_skip_deltas` (ON minus OFF at the median), one note per pattern. It judges no latency and reads no budget (`latency_paint` and `agent_latency_key` keep the verdicts, on the default arm). It FAILS on a harness problem (a relaunch without a prompt, fewer than a third of the expected key frames in a pattern) and when the skips re-render MORE views per key than no skips; no `hop=key_frame_build` line at all is UNVERIFIABLE (noref), never a pass. WARN notes: the kill switch did not reach the app (the off arm logged `enabled=1`), the default environment already has it set, neither arm logged the switch (a build before #1962), a pattern with the same view count in both arms. The name starts with `latency_` so `script/ci/lat_evidence.py` keeps its hop lines in the committed results. Self-test: `viewskip_ab_pure_parts_1962`. Not built or run yet. **Why `Input` is re-rendered alone in 16-31 % of terminal key frames (#1995): `hop=notify_cause`.** Every `ctx.notify()` of `Input` (all 132 in `app/src/terminal/input.rs`, via the `notify_cause!` macro, and the five in `input/agent.rs` and `input/slash_commands/mod.rs`) first calls `warpui::input_order::log_notify_cause("Input", "<fn>[_N]")`, which writes `input_order hop=notify_cause view=Input cause=<enclosing fn>[_N] t=...` only when `warp::input_order` debug logging is on (both arguments are `&'static str`: nothing is allocated or formatted when it is off). `render_hops.render_hop_metrics` counts the causes logged since the previous `hop=key_frame_build` into the informational metrics `input_notify_causes` (`{"view:cause": count}`, most frequent first) and `input_notify_frames` (key frames that had at least one), so every case that records the hops (`latency_paint`, `agent_latency_key`, `ctrl_c_flood_ab`, ...) carries them. It counts every notify of the window, including ones that did not render in that frame, and a notify between two keys is attributed to the next key frame. Rust test: `input_order::tests::notify_cause_lines_have_the_shape_render_hops_parses`; self-test `notify_cause_hops_counted_per_key_frame_1995`. Not built or run yet.
- **A completion result that changes nothing does not re-render `Input` (#1995, owner decision 2026-11-11; kill switch `PHOSPHOR_SKIP_REDUNDANT_COMPLETION_NOTIFY=0`, read once, default ON).** Design: `docs/design/r16-agent2.md` section 2. `Input::handle_completion_suggestions_results` ended in an unconditional `ctx.notify()` (cause `handle_completion_suggestions_results_3`), which with completions as you type re-rendered `Input` beside the editor in 16-31 % of terminal-mode key frames. A result with nothing to show (no result, or no suggestions) now notifies only when a menu was up (it closes), the stale flag (#1355) was set, or it answers a Tab; a result with suggestions notifies as before. The handler returns whether it notified. Unit: `terminal::input::tests::test_completion_result_that_changes_nothing_does_not_notify_input` (no result and an empty result with no menu up return `false`, with four controls that still notify: a Tab, a set stale flag, a result that opens the menu, an empty result that closes it) and `test_completion_result_needs_render_table` (the decision and its kill switch). Run proof: `latency_key_log`'s informational `input_notify_causes` / `input_notify_frames` (terminal-mode typing): the count of `Input:handle_completion_suggestions_results_3` before key frame builds should fall to the results that open or close a menu, and `hop=key_frame_build views=` for a character typed into a non-empty buffer should be 1. No harness change. Worked, unproven: nothing was compiled or run.
- **Round-6 corrections (Linux Wayland agent@fake pass)**: (1) streaming key -> frame is still JUDGED on the raw delta (coordinator review, owner rule: never dismiss bad numbers -- a key that waits for the next streaming frame slot is a wait the user sees, #1843). `paced_key_frame_deltas` (slot wait = previous frame start + median frame spacing, from `hop=frame_drawn`) is reported as the metric `key_to_frame_agent_streaming_slot_adjusted_ms` only, to show how much of the overhead is that wait: in round 6 the raw 10-14 ms was mostly the ~17 ms frame pacing, 2.3 ms median after it (design: `docs/design/agent-input-latency-streaming.md`). (2) `enter_shares` starts at `hop=core_enter stage=handle_window_event` (an Enter an editor binding takes, Linux and Windows, logs no `input_order keydown` line), so the pair was never found ("no Enter keydown -> enter_begin pair"). (3) The steer/Enter judges read the request through `fake_model.clean_messages` (the app appends an `<environment_context>` user message after the prompt). (4) `agent_fault_queued_rows` skips with the reason when the first prompt is not `in_progress` when the rows are typed: `/queue` sends at once with no reply running (no `hop=queued_row`). (5) App: the final-failure note for an unreachable provider (`PreOutputRecoveryExhausted`) is a WARN, not an ERROR (`agent_fault_down`).
- **`agent_latency_enter`**: the app's own share of Enter (Enter key-down -> `hop=enter_begin`) for a prose line typed at 10-25 ms/key with Enter in the same call, idle and while a reply streams (each line typed over the previous line's running reply, i.e. a steer; conversation restarted every 20 lines), against a shell line (`true # tok`) in the terminal-mode editor; budget `APPCI_ENTER_BUDGET_MS` (2 ms). Enter -> the request arriving at the fake model is a metric with a 500 ms sanity bound. Records `lat.agent_latency_enter/idle`, `.../streaming`.
- **`agent_steer_fast`** (#851, by design: input while a reply runs is a steer): three times in a row, while the stream runs, a 200+ character line with shell-looking text (`ls -la | grep x`, `$HOME`, `&&`, a redirect, `rm -rf` as prose) at 10-25 ms/key with instant Enter. Oracles: (1) the fake model's next request has the steer as its LAST user turn, equal byte for byte, in exactly one request, occurring once in it (`steer_verdict`); (2) after the third, the last request holds all three once each, in typed order (`steers_in_order`); (3) the app's `hop=enter_begin` buffer is the steer routed `AI`; (4) no `input_order pty_write` line and no shell command (rec.log) from the first steer on. If the stream had already ended or aged past 4 s when the keys began, the case reports `noref` (precondition not provable), never a pass.
- **Platforms**: Linux, macOS, Windows Git Bash pane (`winmap.GITBASH_ONLY`: the terminal-editor reference and rec.log are POSIX; PowerShell pane skips with the reason). There is no terminal-mode twin of the steer (it exists only in the agent view); the terminal editor is the reference of the other two. Run: `APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1 python3 script/realapp/appci/run.py --cases agent_latency_key,agent_latency_enter,agent_steer_fast` (agent mode). Pure parts (`key_frame_deltas`, `enter_shares`, `steer_verdict`, `steers_in_order`, the stream reply) are in `run.py --self-test` (`agent_latency_pure_parts`).

### appci shell-depth check (subshell leak, Mac fix tier round 6)

A `subshell_ready_*` case could leave the pane inside a LOCAL bash subshell: its "back in the parent" proof was `echo tok >> file`, which runs just as well in the
inner shell when the `exit` was eaten, and run.py's `where_now()` cannot see a local nested shell (same HOME). Every later case then typed into the inner bash
(`latency_enter`: `print: command not found`, 0/60 timings; `routing_table` lines ran in bash). Fixed in two layers:

- `cases_subshell_ready.py`: every case is wrapped by `@guarded` (leaves its inner shell in a `finally` on pass, fail or skip) and leaves through
  `leave_inner`, which proves the ROOT shell by PID (`Ctx.leave_nested`), typing `exit` only while a probe shows a different shell in front (max 3).
- `run.py`: after every case for which `cases.wants_depth_check` is true (all PROVING cases plus names starting `ssh_`, `remote_`, `subshell`, `lab_`) the shell in front
  must be the pane's root shell. The root PID is recorded (`sh -c 'echo tok:$PPID >> ~/.appci_pid'`, shell-agnostic: fish has no `$$`, PowerShell `Add-Content ~/.appci_pid tok:$PID`) at the first checked case after
  each (re)launch; cmd.exe panes have no PID probe and skip the check. Otherwise `exit` is typed while the PID differs (max 3, never at the root); still nested or no answer
  emits `pane_not_local_after_<case>` and relaunches the app, as the ssh block does. A case that relaunched the app itself skips the check (fresh pane). The probe runs in
  whatever view the pane is in, exactly like `where_now`. Cost: one typed line plus a file poll, about 0.7-1 s per checked case and once per relaunch.
- Self-test: `shell_depth_probe_pure_parts` (probe syntax per pane, parser, which cases are checked, exits only while nested, never at the root).

### Mac round 7 terminal pass: subshell exit keys, vim typeahead, fish probe, zsh newuser (fix/subshell-exit-keys)

- `subshell_ready_rc_questions` / `subshell_ready_vim_typeahead` (leave): after the inner bash exited into the root shell, the typeahead
  mode stayed the inner bash 3.2's `InputMatching` (the mode was set only by a `Bootstrapped` hook, one per app). A young Enter then
  opened a `HandoffReport` gate, the command was written as "unengaged", and nothing ended the gate: every key after it was held for the
  60 s net. APP bugs, fixed: the terminal model remembers each session's mode and puts it back at that session's prompt
  (`typeahead_mode_by_session`), and an unengaged user command now lets the held keys follow it (`on_unengaged_user_command_written`;
  unit tests in `typeahead_handoff_tests.rs`).
- `subshell_ready_vim_typeahead`: the Enter of vim's `:wq` was judged a user line in the shell and cancelled the armed setup
  (`why=UserDrove`). APP bug, fixed: a line ended while a program (leader `Other`) owns the tty re-arms (`on_user_line_ended`,
  `r2_a_line_typed_into_a_program_that_owns_the_tty_re_arms`).
- The PID probe is now `sh -c 'echo tok:$PPID >> ~/.appci_pid'`: fish has no `$$`, so `leave_nested` got "none" in an exec'd fish.
  The self-test runs the probe in every installed sh/bash/zsh/fish/dash.
- `subshell_ready_zsh_newuser_install` skips where an empty-HOME zsh shows no newuser menu (Apple's zsh); the check is made on a pty
  before the case types anything (the case typed `q` at a plain prompt: `qecho ...: command not found`). TEST fix.
- `subshell_ready_secret_after_prompt`: APP bug, fixed: the R8 key-path secret check ran only on the legacy route
  (`write_user_bytes_to_pty_inner`); in table mode the keys were held by row H7 before it, so the typed password was held and later ran
  as part of a command line. `dest_table.rs` now runs the same check before the subshell gates are prepared.
- `subshell_sh_probe` (dash): the failing check is the EXPECTED outcome missing (the case passes when `subshell_setup_unsupported`
  is logged). The app judged dash once (`Wait(CookedNoPrompt)`, tail none, right after the first line's Enter) and never again for
  6 s, so it never wrote the probe at the idle prompt. Open app issue; not fixed here (needs a live tty).
- `subshell_ready_secret_after_prompt` on Linux (round 7): not an app bug. The log shows `Secret` judged 5 ms after the setup write (0 held chunks), then 41 `Pty(Typed)` keys straight to the `read -s`: the typed line (no Enter, by design) and `hunter2` reached the read in typed order as one line. The rc now sleeps 1 s before the `read -s` so the line is typed while the setup is still out and is held, then handed back.

### Round 8 Linux Wayland terminal pass: `subshell_sh_probe` and `subshell_ready_vim_typeahead` (fix/r8-subshell-linux)

Both failures are TEST bugs (build 0b817b355, with #1847 options 1 and 2).

- `subshell_sh_probe` (dash): the app never wrote the probe because dash drew no prompt at all. The appci bashrc exports `PS1` and Phosphor
  blanks it, so a dash started from the pane inherits an empty `PS1`: the cursor stays at column 0 (`tail=None`) at the idle "prompt"
  (`Wait(CookedNoPrompt)` at arm time, 0 bytes) and after the first line, and the judge does not write into a shell it cannot prove idle.
  busybox ash passed (a line reader: written at arm time, `subshell_setup_unsupported` 20 ms later). The case now gives dash / ash a
  real `$ ` prompt through `$ENV` (an rc file the case writes; `export ENV=...` before the trials, `unset ENV` after), as a user's dash
  has, and its comment states the #1847 option 2 expectation. The empty-PS1 dash is not written to by design.
- `subshell_ready_vim_typeahead`: the oracle counted the Write decision that caused the write as an earlier one (its `subshell_ready_judged`
  hop is logged just before `subshell_setup_ready_write`). The log shows vim waited the whole time (`Wait(AltScreen)`), then `Write(None)`
  at bash's prompt after `:wq`. The case now allows exactly that one decision, requires it to exist, and requires the AltScreen wait to
  precede the write.

## Paste routing in table mode (#1853)

In `table` mode `paste()` is decided by the table's plan alone (`paste_plan_via_table`); the legacy ssh probe is not consulted, so one phase source (the ssh edge machine) judges the paste and the keys around it. Unit tests in `view_test.rs` (Legacy and Table via `set_destination_mode_for_test`): `ssh_paste_between_held_keys_keeps_typed_order_in_both_modes` (keys, paste, key held together; delivered once, in order, after ownership), `paste_during_a_subshell_setup_is_held_behind_earlier_keys_in_both_modes`, `paste_during_a_powershell_setup_is_held_behind_earlier_keys_in_both_modes`. Written without a compiler; first run is on the build box.

- **Round-7 restart/queue corrections (Linux Wayland agent@fake)**: `agent_restart_quit_*` failed on "unexpected ERROR line: error creating connection to Xorg server" from the RELAUNCH log; this was an APP defect, not the harness (every Wayland launch logged it at line 4, the first launch too, and the relaunch uses the same environment): `windowing/winit/window.rs` now logs it at debug when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set and `DISPLAY` is not. `agent_fault_queued_rows` treats a missing `hop=turn` as the implicit InProgress of a new conversation (`implicit_in_progress`, self-test row `agent_resilience_pure_parts`).

Remote no-helper payloads on stdin (#1864, #1869, #1870; `docs/design/remote-backend-parity-audit.md` findings 1, 6, 7). File chunks, git patches and commit messages no longer ride in the ssh argv or the host's `sh -c` argument (visible in `ps`, kept by audit logs, 128 KiB E2BIG, 32 767 characters on Windows): `ExecRequest.stdin` carries them (`posix_write_payload` base64 for `base64 -d >> "$tmp"`, raw bytes for the `cat` no-decoder fallback, `pwsh_write_payload` read with `[Console]::OpenStandardInput()`; `ShellGitRunner` passes the patch as stdin and `run_commit` uses `git commit -F -`, which also changes the helper's git call). Unit tests: `shellcmd/write_tests.rs::no_content_is_in_any_write_command_and_the_pwsh_one_fits_a_windows_command_line` (the pwsh `-EncodedCommand` line stays under 6 KiB for a 200 KiB file), `backend/shell_git_runner_tests.rs::a_200_kib_patch_stages_and_never_appears_in_the_command_line` and `a_commit_message_is_stdin_not_argv` (real git through a recording `sh`), `backend/contract_tests.rs::a_shell_write_keeps_the_file_content_out_of_every_command_line` (200 KiB write, byte-exact, no command line holds raw or base64 content). `ops_tests.rs` now expects `commit -F -`. Lab: `lab_diff_apply_remote` starts a detached process sampler on the host (patterns in a file, plus a control process so a blind sampler is caught) and fails if a command line ever held the written content raw or base64; skipped (unverifiable) on a pwsh login shell. `run_over_master` now feeds stdin concurrently with collecting output. Not run yet: nothing here has been compiled or run.

## Harness reliability audit fixes (`docs/design/harness-reliability-audit.md`, 2026-11-09)

The read-only audit of `script/realapp/appci` found three ways the harness could QUIT the app it was testing, two false passes and a family of
false fails. Each fix below names its finding (1-12) / cross-cutting letter (A-F) and its selftest pin.

- **A / E / #1a / #3 / #11 — one probe primitive, unseeded tokens, per-probe snapshot.** `Ctx.probe(cmd, token, name, dirs=None, remote=False, timeout)`
  guards first, snapshots the size of every file the probe can land in, types, waits for the token appended AFTER the snapshot and then for the
  prompt count (local or remote, where a hook exists) to advance past the pre-probe count; it returns `(where, tokens)`. `where_now`, `shell_pid`
  and `pane_responsive` are built on it. Probe tokens come from `Ctx.ptok()` (an UNSEEDED `probe_rng`; `ctx.tok()` stays seeded for the replay
  cases), so no earlier run or pass can have left this probe's token in a file nobody clears (the PowerShell pane's real-home `~/.appci_pid`, which
  once supplied a dead process as the "root pid" and had every later `leave_nested` type `exit` at the root shell). `return_to_local` and
  `leave_nested` sample `before = prompts()` after the probe's own prompt was counted, type `exit`, and wait for the NEXT prompt
  (`Ctx.wait_prompt_after_exit`: local or outer-remote prompt, then the app's `ssh_pty_owner ssh=false` hop when the local shell is back; the
  fixed `sleep(0.5)` settles are gone). `leave_remote` uses `wait_ssh_gone` on every platform instead of the hook-less pane's fixed 2 s settle.
  Pins: `audit1_shell_pid_counts_only_tokens_appended_after_its_snapshot` (a stale `tok:pid` before the snapshot is not an answer; tokens
  differ between contexts), `audit3_probe_waits_for_its_own_prompt_and_exit_waits_for_the_next` (a prompt logged 100 ms after the effect file:
  `exit` is typed only after it, the next probe only after a further one).
- **B / #1b / #2 — root pid once per launch, `Ctx.exit_nested`, one `relaunch()`.** `run.relaunch()` is the only relaunch path inside a pass
  (six copies before): keep the dying instance's log, stop, start, `await_shell`, `settle_first_run` (the pane's `hop=view_mode` line plus 0.5 s
  instead of a fixed 4 s), then `record_root_pid` behind `be.guard()` while the pane is provably clean -- on POSIX only when the process tree shows
  exactly ONE shell under the app, else the depth check stays off and a `depth_check_off_after_<why>` skip row says so; Windows records it in
  `prove_keys` after the key proof put the pane in the case dir. The lazy capture at "the first checked case" is gone (it typed before
  `be.guard()`/`reset()` and once named a leaked nested shell as the root). A case that relaunches the app itself gets a fresh record before the
  next case, under the same one-shell rule. `Ctx.exit_nested(base, r, label)` is the only way a case leaves a shell it started: `exit` is typed
  when the PID probe names a pid other than `root_pid`, or the where probe lands REMOTE, or it lands local/nowhere and the shell count rose above
  `base` (a `su` shell answers in root's home); otherwise `exit` is NOT typed and the row notes why. Every former raw `exit` (subshells,
  subshell_sh_probe, remote_heredoc's inner shells, shell_nu's nested nu, palette and split panes, the scripted zero-network ssh, tmux, sudo/su,
  AltGr Git Bash, editor-memory Git Bash, the lab's nohelper bash, `leave_inner`'s fallback) goes through it. The PowerShell pane (no rc hook)
  gets its prompt event from the app's own `hop=precmd_seen` line (`Ctx.precmds_since`): `probe()`, `wait_prompt_after_exit`, `await_shell`
  (first prompt report + 1 s instead of a flat 12 s; the 12 s stay as the give-up net) and `set_ps_pane_state` use it. Pin:
  `audit2_raw_exit_is_banned_outside_ctx_and_the_root_pid_is_recorded_once_per_launch` (source lint: `.type("exit"` only inside `Ctx`,
  `cases_caseremote.leave` or a line marked `reference terminal`; `await_shell` called from two places only; `exit_nested` decision table;
  `record_root_pid` refuses with 2 shells).
- **#4 (#1911) — the ssh trial verdict waits for the remote log and knows the effect.** The remote rc hook writes a command's `C` line at the
  NEXT prompt, after the command's effect file exists, so a verdict read right after `until(tok in file)` said "#1292: ... the remote shell logged
  nothing for the line" under a passing check. `ssh_trial_note(..., effect_seen=)` now takes the case's own effect observation: when the effect
  was seen it first waits (3 s give-up net) for the remote `rec.log` to hold a non-probe command past the trial's start index; `ssh_trial_facts`
  treats a SILENT remote log with the effect seen as exact (`rec_silent`, text "exact (by its effect ...)"); and a trial whose effect succeeded
  while the log holds a DIFFERENT line is `r.unverifiable` (status `noref`), never a pass with a contradicting note. `ssh_connect_typing`,
  `ssh_enter_then_immediate_command` and `ssh_nested_typeahead` pass their effect; the nested case's fixed 1 s sleep before the verdict is gone.
  Pin: the audit #4 block of `ssh_trial_facts_name_the_issue`.

- **#5 / C (#1912) — injector accounting reads to the case's end, on Windows too, and a loss outside the loss cases is `noref`.**
  `injacct.window(calls, t_end)` ends at the moment of accounting (the case's end) when that is later than the old "last injector call + 3 s"
  (a held ssh-typeahead Enter or a slow-classifier Enter is processed later than 3 s and read as "Enter: sent 2, app saw 0"). `run.account_case`
  runs on every backend that records its calls (the Windows backend always did; the run loop excluded it) against `ctx.log_path`. The row is no
  longer only informational (this supersedes the "informational note" wording of the #1509 paragraph above): `injacct.loss_verdict` — lost-before-app
  > 0, or fewer Enters seen than posted, on a case that is NOT in `injacct.LOSS_CASES`, with an app key trace present and no failure of its own —
  makes the row `UNVERIFIABLE` (status `noref`): the case passed on its effect check while keys never reached the app. A failing case keeps its
  failure, loss cases keep their `WARN loss case` note, paste-only rows and trace-less runs are not judged. Pin:
  `audit5_accounting_window_runs_to_case_end_and_a_loss_outside_loss_cases_is_noref`. **Not yet run on a real build**: the first Windows pass
  decides whether its call records and the app's key trace line up (a systematic mismatch there would show as many `noref` rows with the same count).
- **#6 / #7 / D (#1913, #1914) — the harness's probe lines are not a case's commands; comparisons wait for the log.** `Ctx.HARNESS_MARKER_RE`
  also matches the where / pid probes (the `>> ~/.appci_where` echo, the `sh -c` pid probe into `~/.appci_pid`, PowerShell's `Add-Content ~/.appci_pid`), so
  `cmds_since(mark)` drops one that the rc hook logged after the next case took its mark ("shell received 31 commands for 30 typed, first
  mismatch: echo wT... >> ~/.appci_where"). `Ctx.await_commands(mark, n_or_predicate, timeout=5)` returns `cmds_since(mark)` once the shell has
  logged what the case compares (the `C` line is written with the prompt, after the effect file); the timeout is the give-up net and a pane with no
  rec.log is not waited on. Used where a count or an exact list is compared: `effect_run` (fast_typing, rollover), the Ctrl-C integrity read, the
  reference-shell exact count, the cadence audit, `cases_caseintl.check_cmd`, the tmux line of `cases_coverage_a`. Negative checks ("nothing
  reached the shell") keep their settle time: there is no event for something that must not happen. Pin:
  `audit6_7_harness_probe_lines_are_not_the_cases_commands_and_comparisons_wait_for_the_log`.
- **#10 / C (#1917) — the per-case app-log slice is saved on every platform.** `run.save_case_log` was called under `if win`; Linux and macOS
  kept only the end-of-pass `phosphor.log` plus the retained `.in_session.N` chunks, so a long pass rotated a failing case's lines away. Every
  non-skipped case on every backend now writes `logs/<label>/case_<case>.log`: a failing or `noref` case keeps its start (12 MB cap) plus the
  tail of `ssh/sshd.log`, a passing one its newest 1 MB; a case that ends in the app's death is saved before the relaunch. The slice is
  `run.case_log_text`: everything after the case's `LogOffset` (`ctx.log_size()` taken before the case; `Ctx.log_since` follows the file across
  the app's in-session rotation), preceded by the case's own earlier launches (`ctx.extra_logs`, the first read from the case's offset), and on
  Windows followed by the timestamp cut of a log file the case's own relaunch created. With no offset it is the old timestamp cut. Artifacts grow
  by at most 1 MB per passing case on Linux/macOS (as on Windows since r18e9). Pin:
  `audit10_case_log_slice_on_every_platform_follows_the_log_across_a_rotation`.
- **#8 / #9 / #12 / F (#1915, #1916, #1919) — `Profile.read` retries, post-case invariants, wedge probe everywhere.** `Profile.read` (under
  `prompts()` / `commands()`, polled inside `until` lambdas) retries a `PermissionError` five times like `Ctx.lines` (Windows: the shell has the log
  open); a log that stays unreadable RAISES rather than reading as "no prompts, no commands". `run.post_case_invariants(ctx, prof, be)` runs right
  after every case returns or raises, before the screenshot and any probe: `prof.ref_active` must be False, `be.guard_override` None, and with no
  lab arm `ctx.remote` a `LocalRemote` and `prof.remote` None. Anything else is reset (then `be.refocus()`) and reported in a
  `harness_state_reset_after_<case>` row: `pass` when the case itself failed (the leak is that failure's debris), **`fail` when the case passed or
  was `noref`** (its cleanup has a hole: a TEST defect to fix, the later cases are protected either way). Before this a case that raised between
  switching to the reference terminal and closing it made every later case read the reference shell's logs and guard against a closed window.
  The wedged-pane probe (`ctx.pane_responsive()`, an effect probe) now runs after ANY failing case on every platform, not only on Windows: a
  program left in the foreground that ignores Ctrl-C gets a `pane_wedged_after_<case>` row and a relaunch instead of failing every later case.
  A failing case therefore costs one extra marker command (about a second) on Linux/macOS. Pin:
  `audit8_9_12_profile_read_retries_and_post_case_invariants_reset_leaked_state`.

## Foreground-group lookup without the /proc scan (#1958)

Nothing here was compiled or run when it was written (laptop rule); the first box run decides. The logic and the generator of
`made_up_trees_give_the_scans_answer_in_every_mode` were ported to Python and run once on the laptop: 400 process tables, 1057 groups, every
one equal to the scan in every mode (the leader answers 625, the walk 52, the list 380; 330 "plain" verdicts; in 33 the list found a shell
or hop the walk had not seen).

**What changed.** On Linux the hand-off's platform sample (`shell_prompt_fact` -> `foreground_is_plain_program`) and the #1796 tty-read probe
found the members of the pty's foreground process group by reading `/proc/<pid>/stat` of every process on the machine (4-16 ms on the main
thread), and the `hop=hand_route` log line ran that sample for every key written to the pty. Now `hand_route` prints the fact the decision
sampled (`prompt_fact=unsampled` when it took none) and never runs the probe, and the group is looked at by `local_tty/fg_group.rs`. macOS
and Windows are unchanged apart from the two log changes (`prompt_fact=unsampled`, the `prompt_fact_sample` hop).

**How "is the foreground a plain program" is answered (owner decision 2026-11-09: the walk WITH a list fallback, the scan's answer always).**

1. `path=leader`: the group leader's own `stat`. A shell or login hop there (`ssh`, an inner shell, `sudo -i`, `tmux`) is "not plain" with
   one read.
2. `path=walk`: a walk of the pty's session tree (`tcgetsid`, then `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/children`), at most 32 reads, looking for one
   thing: a member that is a shell or login hop (`make` running `sh`, `timeout 60 bash`). One seen is "not plain".
3. `path=list_confirm`: everything else, so EVERY "plain program" verdict: `/proc` listed, `getpgid(2)` per pid, `stat` of the members only,
   the scan's membership exactly. (`path=list`: the same with no walk before it, when `tcgetsid` gave no session leader or the mode is `list`.)

Why the walk may only say "not plain": it sees a subset of the group. A member whose parent died hangs under init or a subreaper, outside
the shell's tree; the tty reports the group's id and never its size, so nothing says a member is missing. A member the walk saw is a member
for the scan too, so "a shell or hop is a member" is safe from a subset. "No shell or hop seen" is not: it would be "plain program", the
verdict that DELIVERS a key instead of holding it, and one unseen member can turn it around. That verdict is therefore always the list's.
The walk's other blind spots (an unreadable process, a kernel without `children` files, the read budget) end the same way, in the list.

The members themselves (`foreground_process_names`, the #1796 tty-read probe) always come from the list: a caller that wants the members
wants all of them.

**What it costs** (Python on the laptop with 497 processes, so indicative; the Rust is not slower). Leader read: about 10 us. A 4-read
walk: about 40 us. The list: about 650 us, of which about 450 us is the kernel listing `/proc`, so it grows with the machine's process count
(about 1.3 us per process). The old scan: about 8000 us.

| where | what a sample costs |
|---|---|
| typing at a shell prompt (the shell's own group in front) | nothing: `tcgetpgrp` alone decides, no lookup, no hop line |
| `ssh`, an inner shell, `sudo`, `tmux` in front | the leader read |
| a build tool or wrapper with a shell among its children in front | the leader read and the walk (the list is not run) |
| a plain program in front (`cat`, `vim`, `less`, a REPL) | the leader read, the walk AND the list, on every sample: the first key of a line and every Enter typed into the program, the counts-diverged check |
| the #1796 tty-read probe (an agent's command showing a prompt-shaped line; not the key path) | the list, at every observation |

`PHOSPHOR_FG_GROUP_LOOKUP`: unset or `walk` is the above; `list` skips step 2; `scan` is the pre-#1958 scan (A/B only). All three give the
same verdicts and members.

**Hops (input-order logging on).** `hop=prompt_fact_sample what=<prompt_fact|plain_program> answer=<..> us=<micros>`: one per sample an
installed probe took (every unix). `hop=fg_group_lookup for=<plain_program|members> path=<leader|walk|list|list_confirm|scan> reads=<n>
members=<n|none> us=<micros>`: one per look at the group (Linux). Counts and times only, never a process name.
`latency_key_log` reports them as the metric `typing_prompt_samples` and a `#1958` note. The metric STAYS informational (owner decision
2026-11-09), like `key_to_pty_write_ms`: the case types into `cat`, a plain program, so its samples include the list, whose cost is a fact
about the test machine's process count and not about the app.

| layer | tests | what they pin |
|---|---|---|
| local_tty (Linux, a made-up process table behind `ProcSource`) | `fg_group_tests.rs`, every test through `assert_all_ways_agree` | for the group asked about: the members in `walk` and `list` mode are exactly the scan's; the plain-program verdict is the scan's in `walk` mode, in `walk` mode with no session leader and in `list` mode; the walk alone says "shell or hop" only when the scan has one; in `walk` mode "plain" is said by `list_confirm` and nothing else |
| the same | `a_plain_program_is_said_by_the_list_after_a_four_read_walk`, `every_stage_of_a_pipeline_is_a_member`, `a_pipeline_whose_first_stage_exited_is_still_a_plain_program`, `a_zombie_member_counts_as_it_does_in_the_scan`, `other_groups_of_the_session_are_not_members`, `a_shell_with_the_leaders_pid_but_another_group_does_not_decide`, `a_group_with_no_process_left_is_empty_not_plain` | plain programs: `path=list_confirm`, 1 + 4 + 2 reads for a shell running `cat`; an empty group is not plain |
| the same | `a_login_hop_leading_the_group_is_decided_by_one_read`, `the_shells_own_group_is_the_shell_and_its_groupless_children` | `ssh` / an inner shell / `sudo` / `tmux` leading the group: not plain after ONE read, `/proc` not listed |
| the same | `a_shell_among_the_members_is_decided_inside_the_shells_tree`, `a_shell_below_the_leaders_child_makes_the_group_not_plain`, `a_shell_below_a_plain_leader_makes_the_group_not_plain`, `a_shell_forked_by_a_worker_thread_is_seen_by_the_walk`, `a_threaded_shell_is_walked_through_all_its_threads`, `the_walk_alone_says_only_what_it_saw` | a shell among the members: `path=walk`, 4 `stat` reads and no `/proc` listing with 2000 other processes on the machine (the scan reads them all); children are found under the thread that forked them |
| the same | `an_orphan_beside_a_living_leader_gets_the_scans_answer`, `orphans_are_members_wherever_they_hang`, `a_group_wholly_outside_the_shells_tree_is_decided_by_the_list`, `a_living_leader_outside_the_shells_tree` | the owner decision: a member re-parented to the user manager or init is invisible to the walk and still decides (an orphaned `sh` beside a living `tee`: not plain, by `list_confirm`, as the scan says). Replaces `the_walk_does_not_see_an_orphan_beside_a_living_leader`, which pinned the opposite answer as a stated limit |
| the same | `a_tree_of_thread_heavy_programs_is_decided_by_the_list`, `a_kernel_without_children_files_is_decided_by_the_list`, `an_unreadable_process_in_the_tree`, `a_shell_that_is_gone_is_no_obstacle`, `without_a_session_leader_the_list_answers`, `the_list_falls_back_to_the_stat_where_getpgid_refuses` | the walk's other blind spots end in the list: the 32-read budget, no `children` files, an unreadable process (the walk goes on past it), no shell, no session leader; `getpgid` refusing makes the list read each `stat` |
| the same | `made_up_trees_give_the_scans_answer_in_every_mode` | 400 generated process tables (fixed generator: pipelines, nested jobs, threads, zombies, shared groups, one process in five orphaned to the user manager or init, unreadable processes, kernels without `children` files), every group of each through `assert_all_ways_agree` |
| the same | `the_stat_line_gives_comm_group_state_and_thread_count`, `the_lookup_mode_is_the_walk_unless_asked_otherwise` | `num_threads` is field 20 of the line; the env values |
| local_tty (Linux, the real `/proc`) | `the_real_proc_finds_this_process_in_its_own_group` | the scan and the list find the test process in its own process group through the real `/proc` and `getpgid`; the verdict in `walk` mode is reached by `leader`, `walk` or `list_confirm` |
| appci self-test | `prompt_sample_audit_counts_samples_and_lookup_paths` | the two hops are parsed into the `typing_prompt_samples` metric (sample path renamed `list_after_walk` -> `list_confirm`) |

**What a fixed Linux run shows.** `latency_key_log`: `key_to_pty_write_ms` median under 1 ms in both modes; `kh_hold_exit -> hand_route`
about 0.1 ms as on macOS for the keys that take no sample; `typing_prompt_samples.samples` about one per `cat` line typed (its first key),
not one per key, with `lookups` showing `list_confirm` for `cat` (reads = 7; its `us` is the list's cost on that machine, expect a few
hundred microseconds per 500 processes), `leader` over ssh, never `scan`, and never `walk` for a plain program.

## Round 10 group A (#1966 #1985 #2004 #1907 #1938; design `docs/design/r10-groupa.md`)

- **Windows RUST_LOG covers every module whose `hop=` lines a case reads (#1966).** The Windows launcher's `warn` base hid the plain `log::info!`
  `hop=agent_action` line (module `warp::ai::blocklist::action_model`), so `agent_question` on Git Bash judged a shown card `hung`. The string is now
  `app.WINDOWS_RUST_LOG` with an `=info` directive for each of the 13 modules that emit a case-read `hop=` through a plain log call. Selftest
  `windows_rust_log_enables_every_hop_module_1966` scans the Rust sources and fails when such a module is not enabled (a new plain-log hop needs its
  module added to the constant); it also proves the pre-fix string hid `action_model`. Worked, unproven: no Windows run yet; the next Git Bash
  `agent_question` run should show `hop=agent_action ... status=blocked` and verdict `answerable`.
- **`flood_scrollback_find` rests on the app's record when OCR is blind (#1985).** `cases_robust.find_verdict`: OCR reading the marker is judged as before;
  when OCR read the marker nowhere the verdict comes from the `hop=find_scroll` lines. Match ON screen and `moved=true` -> pass (noted as app
  evidence); match OFF screen -> FAIL; only `no_match` hops -> FAIL; no hop, no usable geometry (`busy`, older build) or on screen with `moved=false` -> NOREF
  (`unverifiable`), never a pass. Selftest `coverage` row in the `flood_scrollback_find` block of `selftest.py` has one assertion per situation. Worked,
  unproven: the next Mac agent-mode run that OCRs blind should now be a pass with the note "OCR was blind; the app's own record says ...".
- **`big_paste` times the Enter and the largest UI item (#2004, #1191).** The case now sends Return at once behind the 1 MB paste and polls `big.out` for its
  full size (the Enter's effect: the paste's last line has no newline, so cat only gets it on Return): `big_paste_time_to_enter_ms` is that time from the end of
  the paste. rec.log cannot time it (it stamps `cat > big.out` after Ctrl-D). **Budgets, OWNER DECISION 2026-11-10 (they were proposals until then):**
  time-to-Enter <= 1500 ms (`APPCI_BIGPASTE_ENTER_BUDGET_MS`), judged only on a byte-exact paste; largest single `hop=ui_item` <= 250 ms
  (`APPCI_BIGPASTE_UI_ITEM_BUDGET_MS`), judged whenever an app log exists. The variables follow `latency_paint`'s pattern (`APPCI_PAINT_BUDGET_MS`): a
  positive number overrides the budget for a diagnosis run; anything else (a typo, 0, a negative number) is ignored, so the budget can never be voided by
  accident. The round 10 names `APPCI_BIGPASTE_ENTER_MS` / `APPCI_BIGPASTE_UI_ITEM_MS` are still read when the new one is not set. The metric
  `big_paste_budgets` records what a run was judged against. The byte check, the Windows conhost control and both session modes are unchanged. Selftest
  `big_paste_time_budgets_2004`. Worked, unproven: the next run prints `big_paste_time_to_enter_ms`, `big_paste_ui_items.max_ms` and `big_paste_budgets`
  and FAILS the case over either budget.
- **Child shells get no PS1 instead of an empty one (#1907).** `bash_body.sh` blanked PS1 after every prompt in the Phosphor-prompt mode; a user who
  exported PS1 (`export PS1=...` or `set -a`) made every child shell (dash / sh / ash read PS1 from the environment) draw no prompt. The blank now un-exports
  PS1 first (`compgen -A export -X '!PS1'` says whether it is exported; builtins only), and `warp_change_prompt_modes_to_ps1` exports it again. `script/test_child_ps1`
  (real bootstrap in a pty, `printenv PS1` in a child) fails on the old bootstrap with `empty` and passes now; the other bash script tests were re-run
  (`test_bash_bootstrap_builtins`, `_nounset`, `test_hijack_bootstrap`, `test_bash_preexec_large_command`, `test_line_editor_markers --only bash`, `test_hook_forks`,
  `test_local_counted_bootstrap`, `test_bootstrap_hook_equivalence`, `test_ssh_raw_bootstrap_hook`). `test_init_shell_escaping` fails the same way on the
  base commit (its `_hostname` snippet search finds nothing in `bash_body.sh`), unrelated to this change. (Repaired in round 12, 2026-11-10: see `test_init_shell_escaping` in the script-test table.) Not covered: the real app's `sh` child in a real
  pane (no run yet; worked, unproven).

## Round 10: `ssh_nested_typeahead` on Linux Wayland (#2013; design `docs/design/r10-wl-ssh-nested.md`)

- **APP bug, a race; the case is unchanged.** Round 9b terminal mode: the nested `ssh fake` was written 1 ms after the first remote Precmd, before the
  remote shell's line editor had the tty, so the cooked tty echoed `^Pssh fake` and the editor echoed `ssh fake` again. The block's echoed command no longer
  parsed as ssh, and `AfterBlockStarted` released the window that the submit of this command had armed (`ssh_gate_released how=other_command` right after
  `Received Preexec hook`); the typed line was split (`ssh_handed_back chars=7 dest=stashed_until_block_end`, the rest `gate_open_live` to the inner shell).
  Agent mode passed in the same run and Wayland passed in rounds 5, 7 and 8: who wins the race depends on load.
- **What changed.** `AfterBlockStarted` carries the Preexec hook's own command (`reported_command`); the connect window remembers the submitted ssh command
  until its block starts; a block whose hook reports that command is the ssh's block whatever the echo shows (`ssh_submit_running_in_started_block`).
- **Unit tests (`terminal/view_test.rs`).** `ssh_submit_is_recognised_in_its_started_block_by_the_hooks_report_not_the_echo` (the pure decision: the round
  9b echo, white space, an expanded alias, another command, an empty report, no waiting submit, a clean echo);
  `an_ssh_window_survives_its_own_block_start_with_a_polluted_echo` (the view: the window stays armed, no `OtherCommand` release, the pending ssh host comes
  from the submitted command); `an_ssh_window_is_still_released_when_another_commands_block_starts` (#983's rule is unchanged).
- **No new app case.** `ssh_nested_typeahead` is the case; the losing side of the race cannot be forced from the harness without slowing the remote shell's
  start on purpose. Worked, unproven: nothing was compiled or run. The next Linux run should show, in both modes, `ssh trial verdicts: exact=1`, hand-overs
  `precmd` then `finish` (`delivered=tty_owner`), and NO `ssh_gate_released how=other_command` between the nested `ssh_pty_owner ssh=true site=ssh_submit`
  and its `site=tty_owned`.

## Round 10: `subshell_ready_zsh_newuser_install` on Linux (#2015, #2016, #2017; design `docs/design/r10-wl-zsh-newuser.md`)

- **The case never showed the menu (#2015, TEST fault; rounds 7, 8 and 9b, Wayland, both modes).** The Linux app is started with `ZDOTDIR` = the scratch
  home (`app.py`), which has a `.zshrc`; zsh looks for its startup files in `$ZDOTDIR` first, so `HOME=~/w/lab_zsh_home zsh` started at a plain prompt and
  the setup was rightly written there (`subshell_ready_judged ... kind=LineReader tail=ShellPrompt decision=Write`). The guard ran in the harness's
  environment (no ZDOTDIR), saw a menu and did not skip. The case's `q` then ran as `qecho ...`, and with HOME changed the PID probe (`~/.appci_pid`) answered
  into the inner HOME: "got none", `pane_not_local_after_*`.
- **What changed in the case.** It types `ZDOTDIR=~/w/lab_zsh_home zsh` (HOME untouched, so the probes answer where the harness reads). The guard
  `zsh_runs_newuser_install(dotdir, home)` starts its zsh with the same two variables on a 24x80 pty and looks for the menu's footer. Before Ctrl-I the case
  reads the pane's zsh from the OS (`pane_zsh_facts`: `ZDOTDIR` in `/proc/<pid>/environ`, the tty size by `TIOCGWINSZ`; Linux): another `ZDOTDIR` FAILS as
  `TEST precondition: ...` and the case stops; a pane under 15x72 (zsh-newuser-install shows no menu there) skips; no `/proc` is a note. Every check the
  case made is still made, unchanged.
- **Self-test `subshell_ready_newuser_guard`**: the guard's environment, the `/proc` environ parser, the precondition verdicts, that `app.py` still exports
  `ZDOTDIR` and the case overrides exactly that, and on a machine with zsh a real zsh on a real pty: startup files in `ZDOTDIR` = no menu whatever HOME
  holds; an empty `ZDOTDIR` = the menu although HOME has a `.zshrc` (Linux).
- Worked, unproven: no app run yet. The next Linux run must show `tail=InputPrompt decision=Wait(InputPrompt)` at Ctrl-I, no
  `subshell_setup_ready_write` before the `q`, then the write, the typed line in `lab_zshnew.txt`, one `exit` and the root shell in front.
- **zsh-newuser-install's other key prompts are input prompts (#2017, APP, found by reading).** `--- Type a key ---`, `--- Edit abandoned, type a key ---`
  and `--- Type a key in forlorn hope ---` read as a shell prompt (no `:`/`?` ending), and a raw tty under a shell leader with a shell-shaped tail is where
  the setup is written. `output_tail_is_input_prompt` now takes a tail that ends in `---` and says "type a key" for a prompt. Unit test
  `key_facts_tests.rs`: `the_other_zsh_newuser_install_key_prompts_are_input_prompts` (the three prompts; shell prompts that mention a key or end in
  dashes are not). Not compiled or run yet. No app case walks the sub-menus (the case answers `q` at the first screen).
- **A one-key answer no longer leaves the setup armed (#2016, APP, found by reading).** The menu's `q` has no line end, so the hand-off counted it as
  text in the shell's line and every look was `Wait(LineDirty)` until the user's next Enter (or the 60 s ceiling). New pure rule
  `subshell_ready::key_read_took_the_typed_keys`: the keys are gone when the line was clean before the first of them, that look showed a question on a
  raw tty under a shell leader, and this look shows a line editor (queue empty) at a shell-shaped tail on a LOWER row that neither shows the typed
  text nor repeats the question. The view then judges with a clean line for this attempt (hop `subshell_ready_key_read rows_below= bytes=
  line_dirty=`); the next user byte ends that. Never without a tty probe (ConPTY).

| layer | test | what it proves |
|---|---|---|

## Round 10: the lab's first run (job 17885063245; design `docs/design/r10-lab.md`; #2019 #2020 #2021)

The fix-tier lab job ran the PROVING lab cases for the first time (build `413cd4241`): 36 judged rows, 2 PASS, 21 FAIL, 13 NOREF. Two causes are app
defects, five are faults of the harness or the job. Everything below is worked, unproven: nothing was compiled or run against a build.

- **APP, #2019: a fish or nu LOGIN shell on the remote (8 FAIL rows, "no remote prompt after `ssh lab-u_fish` / `lab-u_nu`").** sshd runs the wrapper's
  POSIX bootstrap as `<login shell> -c <script>`; fish and nu refuse the whole text (`warp_rb=false` is a syntax error), so the managed session ended
  30 ms after `ManagedSSHSessionStarting`. The three wrappers (`bash_body.sh`, `zsh_body.sh`, `fish.sh`) now ask a second question over the same master
  when the first probe answer is not definitive, `sh -c 'echo warp-login-$SHELL-'`, and run the plain session (`PlainSSHFallback`, as for a Windows
  host) for fish, nu, csh, tcsh, xonsh and elvish. Unit tests (`terminal/bootstrap_test.rs`): `ssh_wrapper_decides_after_connecting_over_one_master`
  gained the cases `fish-login`, `nu-login`, `tcsh-login-behind-jump`, `noisy-rc-bash`, `unlisted-login-shell` and `probe-ssh-failed`, and its stub
  ssh answers the second question (`$LOGIN`) and can fail the first (`$PROBE_STATUS`); **expectation changed:** the `inconclusive` case now expects TWO
  `-T` probes (it was one), because an answer that is not definitive is now followed by the login-shell question, and the test checks that question's
  exact text. New test `ssh_login_shell_question_is_answered_by_every_login_shell` runs the question in the real sh, bash, zsh, dash and fish that are
  installed. `script/test_ssh_probe_cache` (**expectation changed** the same way: its cumulative ssh-call counts for the `inconclusive` and `garbage`
  cases went up by one per call, return codes unchanged) gained the login-shell cases: fish, nu and tcsh are remembered as non-POSIX, bash behind a
  printing rc file as POSIX, an unlisted shell is never remembered. The timer guard entry moved with the 5 s net (`warp_ssh_probe_over_master`,
  `script/input_path_timers.allow`). Run by hand on the laptop
  with a stub ssh in real bash 5, zsh 5.9 and fish 4.2.1 (all cases as expected); nu could not be run there. The next lab run should show, for the
  fish and nu arms, `Received PlainSSHFallback hook`, two `Starting session: command for u_<shell>` lines in the lab sshd log and a remote prompt.
  **Owner question:** these hosts get a plain session with no remote features; the agent-mode `nu` arms are expected to get past the connect and then
  fail on their first remote tool call until a managed session for such login shells is designed.
- **APP, #2020: remote agent edits lost the file's line endings (`lab_fam_agent_edit_endings.bash.lan.nohelper`).** On an ssh pane a CRLF file's accept
  was refused every time (`family=fs_basic`, then `Failed to save file for accepted AgentMode diffs`) and a mixed CRLF / LF file was written back with LF
  only; the local `agent_edit_endings` wrote the right bytes in the same pipeline. The remote diff read (`apply_diff_model.rs` `read_remote_file`) used
  `ReadFileContext` text, which is LF-normalised for the model, where the local path reads the file itself. It now also reads the bytes
  (`read_file_bytes`) and uses them when they are the same text (`with_the_files_own_line_endings`). Unit tests `apply_diff_model_tests.rs`: a CRLF and a
  mixed file keep their endings and a missing final newline; an LF file, bytes of a different text, a failed read and non-UTF-8 bytes keep the normalised
  text; the normaliser equals `shellcmd::read::read_text`'s per-line rule. The case is unchanged. The next lab run should show all five shapes
  byte-exact and one `family=fs_basic` line next to each `family=file_context` line at proposal time (one more side call per proposed file).
- **TEST, #2021: the harness's own state after a lab arm (8 FAIL rows `harness_state_reset_after_lab_fam_agent_context.*.helper`).** `lab_prepare` points
  `ctx.remote` at the lab arm before its gates and left at "APPCI_LAB_HELPER_BIN does not name a built phosphor-remote binary"; `_runner` only cleaned up
  around the case body. The `try` now covers `lab_prepare` (early return, skip or error). The eight `.helper` rows themselves stay NOREF until a helper
  binary is provided (2.15 checklist item 6).
- **TEST, #2021: the lab's fish hook logs prompts.** Every lab connect waits for a `P` line in the remote `prompt.log`; the fish hook was the local scratch
  config, which logs none (fish runs inside the bash pane there and shares its ctl dir). `profile.lab_hooks()["fish"]` = `FISH` + `FISH_LAB_TAIL` (an
  `--on-event fish_prompt` function); `FISH` is unchanged. Pushed at lease time: no image rebuild. NOT changed: the dash / ash hook (`SH_HOOK`) logs no
  prompt either, so those arms (outside the quick matrix) cannot connect yet.
- **TEST, #2021: agent commands are judged on their own effect, not on `rec.log`** (`lab_agent_remote_flow.bash`, `lab_agent_remote_drop.bash` and the
  `pane_not_local_after_...drop.bash` row that followed it). See the #1827 section above for the new commands and oracles. In the run the commands did
  reach the host (`pty_write bytes=2043`, `Received Preexec hook`, a tool result with the edited content).
- **TEST, #2021: `lab_fam_agent_delete_conflict` requires the route of the accept's re-read** (`family=fs_basic`), not a write route: the delete was
  refused correctly and no write is ever sent for a refused accept.
- Self-test `lab_first_run_fixes_round10` pins all four (a helper arm with no binary and a skip inside `lab_prepare` both leave `ctx.remote` /
  `prof.remote` at rest; the lab fish hook logs `P` and the local one does not; `refused_route_verdict`; `drop_command` and the flow command's text;
  `LabRemote.exists` tells an empty file from a missing one).

  nu no-helper arms past the connect (terminal `lab_fam_agent_context.{fish,nu}` then NOREF like bash / zsh, "no scripted app driver"; the agent-mode nu
