  `lab_fam_agent_delete_conflict.bash` and `lab_fam_agent_edit_endings.bash` judged on the new oracles / the app change; the eight `.helper` rows NOREF.

## Round 11: the macOS app-test failures of round 10 (build/r10a; design `docs/design/r11-mac.md`)

All four rows were TEST faults; no app code changed. Self-test: `r11_mac_round10_test_faults`.

- **`subshell_ready_secret_after_probe` (macOS and Wayland, both modes).** The case asserts the hop `subshell_stage_two_pending`, and the lab's
  `hops()` kept only a fixed list of hop names that did not have it, so the lookup could never succeed. The list is now the module constant
  `cases_subshell_ready.HOPS` (with the missing name), `hops_in()` is the pure part, and the self-test reads every hop name the cases look up
  from the module's source and fails when one is not in `HOPS`.
- **`md_viewer`, `md_viewer_big`: the viewer tab is closed and the close is proven (`cases.close_file_viewer`).** `uri::open_file` opens a
  handed-over file in a NEW TAB and focuses it. The cases left it there. On Linux a later case that relaunches the app happened to run before
  anything typed; on macOS those cases skip, so the next case typed into the viewer. Now, in a `finally`: when the app log since the open shows
  `dispatching action for "root_view:add_file_pane"`, the tab is closed with `editor_close()` (`APPCI_KEY_CLOSE`; on macOS the command palette's
  `Close Current Session`, as the editor cases do), and the PID probe must be answered, by the pane's root shell when that pid is recorded
  (`viewer_close_verdict`). No log line: nothing is pressed (the close acts on whatever is in front). A failed proof FAILS the case with the
  reason. Second layer: `md_viewer*` is in `cases.DEPTH_PREFIXES`, so the runner's root-shell probe runs after it and relaunches the app when
  the pane is still not a shell. The case's end-of-case screenshot therefore shows the pane again; the viewer is in `shots/*_md_small.png`.
  Unproven until a Mac run: that the palette entry closes a viewer tab (it is the same `PaneGroupAction::RemoveActive` as the key).
- **`ui_vertical_tabs_many`, `ui_vertical_tabs_panel_click`: precondition (`first_tab_in_front`).** Before a tab is opened or the settings file
  is touched, the pane that has the keyboard must answer `pwd` with the work directory. Otherwise the case stops with that one failure (it is
  a FAIL: the case did not run), instead of 260 s of typing into the wrong place and a dozen derived failures.
- **OCR on macOS reads with Apple Vision first (`cases.ocr_engines`).** `ctx.ocr` used tesseract whenever one was on the PATH, on macOS too,
  and only fell back to `mac/tools/ocr` without it. The Mac runner has a Homebrew tesseract, which reads the agent header but not the small grey
  model chip; agent `mode_proof` failed "model chip not visible" on a screenshot that shows it. On macOS the Vision read now always comes
  first and tesseract's read is added to it (as the X11 2x read is added, never replacing). Other platforms are unchanged. The word-box
  helpers of `cases_ui` (pointer cases, tesseract TSV) are not touched.

## Round 11: the Windows failures of round 10 (build/r10a, pipeline 3048440714, job app-test-windows)

Design note with the per-case evidence: `docs/design/r11-win.md`. Nothing here was compiled or run; every row is "worked, unproven" until the next
Windows run.

- **APP, #2024: `giveup_keys_reach_shell` (PowerShell pane, terminal 6/20 and agent 7/20, KEEP-TOGETHER broken).** A ready signal handled after the model
  had parsed the Preexec of a typed-ahead line was only remembered, and the cycle that Preexec ended was counted as a missed signal: the session was
  demoted and the next prompt handed input to the editor unproven, with the first typed characters of the next line left in the shell's line
  (`handoff_request_skipped reason=line_editor_not_proven`, `decision=Committed`). `LineEditorStatus::set_line_editor_inactive` no longer records a miss
  when a signal was remembered. Unit tests `line_editor_status_tests.rs`: `a_remembered_signal_is_not_a_missed_signal_when_a_typed_ahead_line_ends_the_cycle`
  (the next prompt still waits for its signal, no unproven decision at the Precmd) and `a_cycle_with_no_signal_at_all_is_still_a_miss` (#1825 unchanged).
  The case is unchanged. Next Windows run: 20/20 in both modes, no `handoff_request_skipped reason=line_editor_not_proven` in the case's log slice, every
  second prompt of a round ends in `decision=SendRequest` (or `Committed` with nothing typed).
- **APP, #1923 (the fix did not work): `gitbash_precmd_secret` (Git Bash pane, the PIN never reached `read -s`).** At the prompt hold's cap the screen fact
  (`screen_tail_asks_for_input`) read the active block's OUTPUT grid; a precmd function's `pin: ` is written after the Precmd, into the fresh block's
  prompt-and-command grid, so the fact was false and the keys stayed held (`prompt_hold_kept_overdue hold=44 entries=6`, screenshot: `pin: ` on screen
  under the "waiting for the shell" toast). The fact is now `key_facts::active_block_tail_asks_for_input`, on the grid the block writes to. Unit tests
  `key_facts_tests.rs`: `a_question_printed_after_the_precmd_is_seen_on_the_grid_the_block_writes_to`,
  `the_tail_fact_reads_a_running_commands_output_and_ignores_a_shell_prompt`. No view-level test of the cap with a fresh block was added (the existing
  hold fixtures start the block themselves; a wrong fixture written without a compiler would prove nothing): the case is the proof. The case is unchanged.
  Next Windows run: at the cap after the first half `hop=prompt_hold_expired precmd_wait=true` and the warning `typeahead prompt hold N gave up with no
  line-editor signal: releasing 6 chunk(s) ... to the pty` (no `prompt_hold_kept_overdue`, no `prompt_hold_handed_back`); the second half and its Enter
  as `hand_route reason=unheld state=pty_owned` writes (read from the code: the wait ended at the cap, so nothing holds them; if the log shows a second
  hold instead, it must end the same way); `gbpin.txt` holds the PIN; the line typed after the read runs. The first half is written 1.5 s after its
  first key (the cap), by design of #1923. To watch: the Enter that ended the `read` is counted as a line by the hand-off and no Precmd answers it;
  the cases that follow in the same pane show whether the editor takes input again at the next prompt.
- **TEST, no issue (the app kept the row): `agent_fault_queued_rows` (agent@fake and agent@gitbash+fake, "'QA...' was lost").** The app popped the
  first row back into the input when the failing reply ended (`hop=queued_row id=... state=popped`, then `keystroke: Agent by request-shape
  (AgentConversation, head "please", 40 bytes)`: 40 bytes is exactly `please answer with the word <token>`), and kept the second in the queue
  (`queued_rows_stored`). The case's only eye for the input is OCR, and the Windows VM has no OCR engine, so the row counted as lost. The same case
  passes on macOS (OCR). The app now logs what the input holds after such a restore (`hop=queued_row_restored`, table above) and the case counts a
  token found there as held (`cases_agent_resilience.restored_inputs` / `tokens_in_input`; metric `queued_rows_in_input`). Not weakened: a row that
  is neither sent, stored, on screen nor in that record is still "lost" (self-test), an Enter after the restore voids the record, and a count-only
  line proves nothing. Self-test: the block after `row_hops` in the agent-resilience checks. Next Windows run: PASS with
  `queued_rows_in_input` naming the first row and `queued_rows_stored` the second.
- **APP, #2025 (second defect behind #2006): `subshell_ready_rc_questions` (terminal and agent) and `subshell_ready_rc_clear` (terminal), Git Bash pane.**
  The #2006 change held (two `verdict=ReArm`, `Wait(UserLineAtCursor)` at each echo, one `subshell_setup_ready_write` after the answers, no cancel; the
  answers file was right). The setup then reached `InitShell`, the controller typed the 83 KB bootstrap into the inner bash (41 `SetupChunked` writes) and
  readline took it at 32-49 lines per second: no `Bootstrapped` 15 s later, the typed line held, the harness's probe unanswered, its Ctrl-C aborted the

  clear").** The inner bash drew `LAB$ ` 32 ms BEFORE the setup was armed (`decset_2004 on=true`, then `subshell_setup_armed`, then

  when the prompt was there first, the setup written, the inner line runs within 2 s only if the bootstrap is sourced (#2025 above).

## Round 12 policy decisions (owner 2026-11-10; design `docs/design/r12-policy.md`)

Nothing here was compiled or run on a build: `rustfmt --check`, the script tests named below and the self-tests only. Worked, unproven.

- **The timer rule says what the code does (#1996).** The owner kept the 9 Nov ruling: a give-up net may WRITE the keys it held to the pty in typed
  order; it never discards, reorders, merges or splits a key, never chooses between the shell and the agent, never submits an undecided editor line and
  never re-asks. `script/input_path_timers.allow`'s header, the guard's rule text (`script/check_input_path_timers`, also what it prints on a failure) and
  the `check_input_path_timers` row above still said "a timer never writes to the pty". Every allowlist line was read against its code: 16 nets write
  their held keys unconditionally (`ENTER_GATE_LEAK_NET` behind an Enter that ran, `UNREADY_ENTER_GIVE_UP`, both `arm_give_up`,
  `YOUNG_HOLD_GIVE_UP`, `EVENT_HOLD_GIVE_UP`, `AFTER_ENTER_REPLAY_PTY_WAIT`, `settle_enter_queue`, `CLI_SUBMIT_LEAK_NET`, `BOOTSTRAP_PROGRESS_GRACE`,

## Round 12: the `key_facts` unit failure of round 11 (build/r11a; design `docs/design/r12-keyfacts.md`; #1923)

- **APP, #1923 (the round 11 fix covered one prompt mode only): unit
  `key_facts::tests::a_question_printed_after_the_precmd_is_seen_on_the_grid_the_block_writes_to`.** The test's setup is real: its Precmd carries no
  `ps1`, which is what bash sends with the shell's own prompt (honor PS1 on: `"ps1": ""`, read as `None`). Such a Precmd does not START the fresh
  block's prompt-and-command grid (`HeaderGrid::prompt_only_precmd`; the prompt's start marker does, and bash prints the prompt after its precmd
  functions), an unstarted `BlockGrid` has length 0 and `contents_to_string` returns nothing, so `active_block_tail_asks_for_input` was false with
  `pin: ` in the grid's cells. With the app's prompt (the Windows CI setup) the Precmd carries the PS1, the grid is started and the round 11 fix
  works as written. Now an unstarted grid is read from its cells, the rows ending at the cursor's row (`BlockGrid::tail_at_cursor_to_string`); a
  started grid is read as before. The failing test is unchanged except for one added assertion of its premise (the grid is unstarted) and three
  added checks (a question under other text, an ended line, plain text under an answered question). New:
  `a_question_printed_after_a_precmd_that_carries_the_prompt_is_seen` (the app-prompt Precmd, a started grid), with the test helper
  `TerminalModel::finish_block_with_ps1`. No appci case runs with honor PS1 on: `gitbash_precmd_secret` proves the app-prompt mode only, the unit
  tests are the proof for the other. Next unit run: both tests pass.

## Round 12: honor PS1 and the precmd secret (design `docs/design/r12-ps1case.md`; #1923; nothing compiled or run when written)

- **APP, #1923 (rounds 10 to 12 read the wrong block): where a precmd function's question is written.** Read from the code, not yet from a run.
  What the shell prints between a prompt's Precmd and the command's start is EARLY OUTPUT: the block list's own handler (`blocks.rs` `delegate!`,
  `is_early_output`) sends it to a background block (`EarlyOutput`), in either prompt mode, and that block's output grid is what the pane draws
  (the round 10 screenshot's `pin: `). The fresh active block gets none of it. The screen fact at the prompt hold's cap read the ACTIVE block in
  every round (its output grid, then its prompt-and-command grid, then that grid's cells when unstarted), so it was false with the question on
  screen and the PIN stayed held (`prompt_hold_kept_overdue`). The round 12 reading ("the grid is unstarted with honor PS1") explains the failing
  unit test wrongly: `TerminalModel::mock` is past its bootstrap Precmd, so the test's `pin: ` went to a background block too. Now:
  `BlockList::block_receiving_output` (the block the stream is written to, by the handler's own rule) and `key_facts::block_tail_asks_for_input`
  (renamed from `active_block_tail_asks_for_input`; the view passes it that block). Unit tests `key_facts_tests.rs`:
  `a_question_printed_after_the_precmd_is_seen_on_the_block_the_stream_writes_to` (the round 11 test; its last assertion now reads the block
  the stream writes to, and it also pins that the active block holds nothing of the question: an EXPECTATION CHANGE of an uncompiled round 12
  assertion, because its premise was wrong, not a weaker test), `a_question_printed_after_a_precmd_that_carries_the_prompt_is_seen` (the same
  with the app's prompt), `a_fresh_prompt_with_nothing_printed_asks_nothing`, `a_question_in_an_unstarted_grid_is_read_from_its_cells` (the
  round 12 arm, kept for a block written directly). Next unit run: all four pass; if the first fails at `written.is_background()` this reading
  is wrong and the round 12 one stands.
- **New appci case `precmd_secret_honor_ps1`** (`appci/cases_precmd_secret.py`, `cases.PROVING`, both session modes; no case ran with honor PS1
  on before). A bash precmd function (sourced from a file the harness writes) runs `read -s -p "vault pin: "` once; the PIN is typed in two halves
  around a pause longer than the prompt hold's give-up (1.5 s). Two arms: `hp0`, honor PS1 off (the app's prompt: the control, and on Windows the
  scenario of `gitbash_precmd_secret`), and `hp1`, honor PS1 on. The setting is read when the pane's shell starts, so the case writes
  `terminal.input.honor_ps1` into the profile's `settings.toml` and relaunches the app (`cases_robust.stop_for_restart` / `start_app`), and it puts
  the file back and relaunches once more at the end. Each arm first proves its premise from the pane itself (a typed line records
  `$WARP_HONOR_PS1` and whether the shell is bash); an arm whose premise is not met is UNVERIFIABLE. Oracles per arm: the function reached its
  `read` (a file it writes first); the question is on screen (OCR for `vault`, which no typed line contains: a failing check in terminal mode,
  a metric `question_on_screen_<arm>` in agent mode, where a block that belongs to no command of the conversation may be hidden by design;
  since #2053 it is judged in agent mode too, see "Round 13: the question of a precmd function in an agent conversation"); the
  `read` got the PIN whole and in order (effect file); no `hop=enter_begin` line of the app log shows the PIN or a half of it in the input
  editor's buffer (needs `WARP_INPUT_ORDER_LOG_TEXT=1`, which the harness sets), and, since #2040 withholds text while a secret is read, no `hop=enter_begin` line with a count-only buffer above 0 (`withheld_enters`: text in the editor at an Enter while the log withheld it); #2040's own oracle (`secret_log_verdict`, metrics `secret_log_*_<arm>`): no line of the app log from the first PIN key on holds the PIN or its random half, a `hop=secret_text_withheld active=true` is in the log, and the PIN's key lines (`typed_characters text=`, `keydown key=`) are count-only (none may show its character on Linux and macOS, at most the first half on ConPTY, where the reader is noted at the first key or the hold's cap), with the keys of `touch <go>` typed just before as the control that the log shows text at all (no text there: a note, not judged); no command in

  macOS (the pane is zsh, so both arms relaunch with `session.startup_shell_override = "bash"`, the system bash 3.2; metric `pane_made_bash`).
  Cost: two relaunches on Linux and Windows, three on macOS, about 1.5 min per pass. Selftest `precmd_secret_honor_ps1_pure_parts`. Unverified

## Round 12: a reader ahead of the line editor gets the keys (design `docs/design/r12-pin.md`; #2038, behind #1923; nothing compiled or run when written)

- **Why.** Round 11 Windows, `gitbash_precmd_secret` (the only failing Windows app case): every key stayed held (`prompt_hold_kept_overdue`).
  1d389cfa4 makes the screen fact read the right block. Read from the code, the case would then still fail its last check: the released PIN
  is counted as the shell's line, the Enter that ends the `read` is held as a young Enter (10 s net), then counted as a line no prompt
  answers and opens an enter window nothing closes; the next typed line is held with no event to release it (#2038).
- **Unit, `model/typeahead_handoff_tests.rs`** (fixture `conpty_prompt_after_a_command_in_a_shell_that_signalled`: the hand-off of the round 11
  log at the question): `without_the_reader_the_pin_is_the_shells_line_and_its_enter_is_held_for_a_report` (the control: the defect's first
  two steps, on code this round did not change; if it fails, the diagnosis is wrong),
  `a_reader_ahead_of_the_line_editor_gets_every_key_and_the_signal_hands_input_to_the_editor` (hold, cap, note, release, second half, Enter,
  signal, `Committed`, next prompt held again), `a_question_already_on_screen_sends_the_first_key_to_the_reader_without_a_hold` (inside and
  past the cap), `a_reader_is_noted_only_between_a_precmd_and_its_line_editors_signal`,
  `keys_the_reader_left_unread_are_the_shells_line_once_the_line_editor_signals` (no typed key is left in the shell: `SendRequest`).
- **View, `terminal/view_test.rs`**: `a_precmd_functions_question_sends_the_pin_and_its_enter_to_the_read` (question first as the case runs,
  and keys first then the hold's cap; Legacy and Table; one pty write per key in typed order, the editor empty, no gate left, no unanswered
  line), `the_look_for_a_reader_at_a_key_never_waits_for_the_parser` (the look is `try_lock`: with the model held by another thread the key
  is held as before and no blocking key-path lock is counted).
  **Round 13 (r13-pin2, design `docs/design/r13-pin2.md`; nothing compiled or run when written):** the first of these failed in the round 12
  unit run (`Legacy question_first=true: the first half is with the read`, left `[]`). Verdict TEST: it read `collect_pty_writes` inside the
  view update that typed the keys, and an emitted event reaches its subscribers only when the outermost update returns
  (`AppContext::flush_effects`), so the recorder is always `[]` there. The test now types in separate updates and reads the recorder between
  them; every old assertion is kept and three are added (three queue entries and no reader before the question is printed; the queue idle
  after the cap's release; the signal writes nothing more). No app change. **Rule for view tests:** a pty-write recorder is read after the
  update, never inside it; an `is_empty()` on it inside an update proves nothing.
- **appci.** No case changed. `gitbash_precmd_secret` and `precmd_secret_honor_ps1` (PROVING) are the proof. New hops to read in their logs:
  `prompt_key_screen_asks reader_noted=true` (or `prompt_hold_screen_asks` when keys were held first), `prompt_reader_asks`,
  `hand_route reason=prompt_reader bytes_len=1` per key (length only), `prompt_reader_end why=line_editor_signal line_dirty=false`, then
  `handoff_decision decision=Committed`. A `young_hold_cap` warning or a second `prompt_hold_kept_overdue` in these cases is a FAIL of this
  change.

## Round 12: the Windows ssh cases were a quiet SKIP for two rounds (design `docs/design/r12-winssh.md`; #2043; nothing run on Windows when written)

**What happened.** From round 10 (build/r10a) on, every Windows ssh case in every pass (`ssh_connect_typing`, `ssh_enter_then_immediate_command`,
`ssh_nested_typeahead`, `ssh_gitbash_managed`, `ssh_gitbash_typeahead_managed`, `ssh_gitbash_kill_switch`; 22 rows in round 11) was SKIP with
`fakesshd_win.py did not listen on 127.0.0.1:<port> (see ssh/fakesshd.stderr)`. Round 9 (build/r18w9) had the server running.

**Verdict: TEST fault.** Not the app, and nothing is missing on the Windows machine. `ssh/fakesshd.stderr` of every pass of both rounds is
`import ptyhost` / `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ptyhost'`. The Windows machine's Python is the python.org embeddable layout
(`python312._pth`, `script/ci/nodes/windows.ps1`): `sys.path` is exactly what the `._pth` file lists and the folder of the script being run is
not added. `run.py` and the case modules insert their own folder; `fakesshd_win.py` runs as its own process and got its first sibling import with
the #2007 change (1766c6a2b) without that line. So the #2007 repair (`exec` + pty on a measured terminal) has not run on Windows yet either.
`lab.py stop <run dir>` (called by `windows/ci/after_job.ps1`) had the same fault, unseen because no Windows lab job has been played.

**Repairs.**

- `fakesshd_win.py` and `lab.py` put their own folder on `sys.path` before the sibling import. Selftest `appci_programs_find_their_siblings`
  holds every appci file that is run as a program (shebang or `__main__` block) to that rule, and checks that every program `sshd.py` starts
  is in the scan.
- The skip reason now quotes the last lines of `ssh/fakesshd.stderr` itself (`sshd.stderr_tail`) instead of pointing at the file.

**A required test host that does not start is loud (decision).** `sshd.required()`: the ssh test host is required when `CI` is set (every GitLab
job) or with `APPCI_REQUIRE_SSH=1`; never for the `sim` backend, which has no ssh by design. In a pass where it is required and there is none
(the server did not start, or the setup probe `ssh fake true` failed):

| row | status | why this status |
|---|---|---|
| `ssh_test_host` (one per pass, a harness row like `harness_crash`) | **FAIL** | the run exits non-zero, the release gate and the trend report's failing list show it; the detail starts with `TEST HOST MISSING (harness or test machine, not an app verdict)` and carries the reason and the server's stderr tail |
| every ssh case of the pass (all go through `cases.need_ssh`) | **NOREF** (`cases.HostMissing`, a `Skip` subclass; `run.skip_status`) | "not judged", listed by name under the trend report's "NOREF without the injector explanation" (`results_trend.noref_kind` files a `TEST HOST MISSING` row under `other` whatever else the row says); a SKIP reads as "does not apply here" and is what hid the loss |

A check that failed before the host check still makes the row a FAIL (#1498). A local run on a machine without sshd keeps the plain SKIP with the
same reason text. No existing expectation changed: the same cases run the same checks wherever the host starts. Selftest
`ssh_test_host_missing_is_loud` covers the rule, the row, the status mapping and the wiring; `results_trend.py --self-test` covers the listing.

**What the next Windows run should show.** The job log line `ssh test host: ...` (the measured `exec` + pty arm) in every pass, no
`ssh_test_host` row, and the six ssh cases with real verdicts in both panes and both modes. Their verdicts are the first evidence for the #2007
repair on Windows: failures there are new information, not regressions of this change. If the server fails for another reason, the row says which.

## Round 12: the round 11 failures in the Linux lab (build/r11a; design `docs/design/r12-lab2.md`; #2044 #2045 #2046; nothing compiled or run when written)

Round 11 (integ/r11 `c61b6a3b8`, pipeline 3049602519, job `app-test-lab-linux`): 29 PASS / 21 FAIL / 50 NOREF. The round 10 lab changes were in that
build and each is seen working (#2019 fish and nu connect, #2020, #2021, #2027). The 21 FAIL rows have four causes; everything below is worked,
unproven.

| rows | verdict | what changed |
|---|---|---|

## Round 13: the Git Bash ssh failures of round 12 on Windows (build/r12a; design `docs/design/r13-winssh2.md`; #2051; nothing run on Windows when written)

Round 12 was the first run in which the Windows test sshd served a managed session (#2043 and #2007 worked: the server started, the `app` arm
measured byte-exact both ways, both remote hooks arrived). Every ssh case of the Git Bash pane that takes the managed one-connection path
(#1933) then failed, in both modes: `ssh_connect_typing`, `ssh_enter_then_immediate_command`, `ssh_nested_typeahead`, `remote_tab_no_helper`,
`remote_tab_enter_no_helper`, `ssh_gitbash_managed`, `ssh_gitbash_typeahead_managed` and their `pane_not_local_after_*` rows.

| rows | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| the seven cases above, terminal@gitbash and agent@gitbash | **APP #2051** (design of #1933), worked: nothing; a design is proposed | the app writes the 62 KB bootstrap in one pty write on InitShell; the test sshd takes every byte at once (`written` equals `received` on every line) and receives about one byte per packet at 1.1 to 1.5 KB/s (`65536 bytes in 57530 chunks` after 51 s); the app's nets end the wait after 6.5 s and 15 s. Round r18u28 measured the same rate for a paste into a plain ssh of the same pane, and for the reference console with no app: msys `ssh.exe` reads a Windows console that slowly |
| `subshell_ready_rc_clear`, agent@gitbash: "ran 3.75 s after its Enter (budget 2 s)" | **not an app wait**: the shell's own setup time on that machine; the budget is unchanged and the row stays a FAIL when it happens | app log: `subshell_ready_judged source=armed decision=Write(None)` at age 0 (the inner prompt was already drawn when Ctrl-I arrived), the typed line held behind the written setup, `InitSubshell` at 1189 ms, `InitShell` at 2778 ms, `Bootstrapped` at 3742 ms; no net and no judge wait in between. terminal@gitbash passed the same case because there the prompt was not drawn yet (`decision=Wait(Unknown)`), so the line was typed into the inner shell before the setup and ran at once: the two rows measured different orders of the same race against `BANNER_S` |

**Harness changes (no expectation changed; `run.py --self-test` check `fakesshd_app_arm_da1_and_input_stats_2051`).**

- `fakesshd_win.py`, `app` arm only: the app's console host opens every pseudo console with a device-attributes request to its terminal and
  waits for the answer (`conpty first output after 0.01 s: 4 bytes` before any program output; the start-up probe took 5 s on `app` against 1 s
  on `inbox`; in a session the remote's hooks came 4.3 s after the mode byte). A POSIX sshd's pty asks its client nothing, so the test sshd
  answers the request itself (`ptyhost.DA1_REPLY`, what the app answers) and does not pass it on. The log line says so, and the first-output
  line now carries the first 16 bytes in hex, so the next run shows the request as it is.
- `client input ended: N bytes in M chunks, W written to the pseudo console (...)` now ends with the time from the first to the last byte, the
  rate and what the bytes were (ESC, CR, LF, other control, non-ASCII, the first 48 bytes): round 12's sessions received more bytes (78814 and
  still coming) than the app wrote (62007), and the log could not say what they were. `cases_caseremote.sshd_input_bytes` reads the line as before.
- `subshell_ready_rc_clear` notes where the setup's time went (`cases_subshell_ready.setup_timeline`: the judge's decision when the setup was
  armed and the age of each progress event). The 2 s budget and every check are as they were.

**What the next Windows run should show.** The seven Git Bash ssh cases FAIL as in round 12 until #2051 is decided and built (the harness changes
do not touch what they judge). In `sshd.log`: `console host start-up request 1b5b3063 answered by the test sshd` (or `1b5b63`) once per exec on
the `app` arm, the start-up probe of that arm in about 1 s instead of 5 s, and the composition of the client input on every `client input ended`
line. `subshell_ready_rc_clear` carries its `clear: setup armed decision=...` note in both panes and modes; it fails whenever Ctrl-I arrives after
the inner prompt on that machine (the setup then takes over 2 s there), and passes when the line gets in first.

## Round 13: a secret read by a precmd function on Linux and macOS (design `docs/design/r13-wlps1.md`; #2050; nothing compiled or run when written)

- **Why.** Round 12 Linux Wayland (build/r12a), `precmd_secret_honor_ps1`, the only two failing rows, both arms (`hp0`, `hp1`) in both modes.
  Verdict APP: where the prompt hold is not armed (everywhere but ConPTY) the Precmd hands input to the editor before the precmd functions
  run, so the PIN was typed into the editor in clear text and its Enter ran it as a command (the `read` got the app's kill-line byte 0x10
  and the PIN) or sent it to the agent. The case was right and is unchanged.
- **Unit, `model/typeahead_handoff_tests.rs`** (fixtures `sampled_prompt_after_a_command` / `sampled_prompt_the_editor_owns`: the hand-off of
  the round 12 Linux log at the question, with a probe that answers what one `tcgetattr` would):
  `a_secret_read_at_a_prompt_takes_input_back_from_the_editor_and_gets_every_key` (nothing reads: no change; the tty reads a secret: the pty
  owns input, six keys `WriteCounted` in order, no young Enter, no unanswered line, no commit while the reader has the tty; marker and signal:
  `Committed`), `a_secret_read_seen_before_the_precmd_commits_keeps_input_with_the_pty`,
  `the_tty_is_asked_for_a_secret_read_only_between_a_precmd_and_its_line_editor` (no probe as on ConPTY, marker parsed, a command running, a
  reader already noted), `a_secret_reader_ends_on_events_and_its_unread_keys_are_the_shells_line` (`SendRequest` for keys typed after the
  read's Enter; Preexec; next Precmd), `a_secret_read_ends_keys_following_the_editors_text` (#1658).
- **View, `terminal/view_test.rs`** (fixture `sampled_prompt_the_editor_owns`):
  `a_secret_read_at_a_prompt_takes_the_keys_from_the_focused_editor` (keys through the pane's sink with focus reported in the input's editor;
  Legacy and Table; one pty write per key in typed order, the editor empty; the control arm with nothing reading a secret puts the keys in
  the editor and writes nothing), `a_secret_question_at_a_prompt_takes_input_back_at_its_output` (the wakeup's look, before any key). The
  pty-write recorder is read after the update, never inside it (the r13-pin2 rule).
- **appci.** No case changed. `precmd_secret_honor_ps1` (PROVING) is the proof on Linux and macOS, `gitbash_precmd_secret` stays the proof
  of #1923 / #2038 on Windows (no probe is installed there; nothing of this runs). Hops to read in the Linux log after `touch pp_<arm>_go.txt`:
  `prompt_reader_asks by=tty_secret took_from_editor=true`, `secret_reader_takes_input site=output` (`site=key`: the tty was not yet set at
  the question's wakeup; still a pass), `hand_route reason=prompt_reader bytes_len=1` per key, `prompt_reader_end why=line_editor_signal
  line_dirty=false`, `handoff_decision decision=Committed`; on macOS (bash 3.2, no bracketed paste) `prompt_reader_end_retry` before the
  decision. An `enter_begin` whose buffer holds the PIN, or a `kh_editor_action` for one of its keys, is a FAIL of this change.
- **Kill switch.** `PHOSPHOR_SECRET_READER=0`: the probe is not installed and the app behaves as in round 12.
- **Not covered, filed:** an echoing question from a precmd function on Unix (#2052); an agent conversation does not show the question
  (#2053, the case's `question_on_screen_*` metric: false in the agent pass); an Enter as the very first key while the editor still has
  focus (design note section 5).

  heights while waiting; asking twice changes nothing; hidden and the old height when the reader is over),
  `a_tty_readers_question_changes_nothing_in_the_terminal_scope`,
  `a_finished_question_block_is_hidden_in_the_conversation_and_not_reported` (the next command finishes the block: the flag is dropped before the

  the reader is noted, kept while the PIN is typed, hidden at the look after the line editor's signal; the control arm is the kill switch; the

- **appci, `precmd_secret_honor_ps1` (PROVING), expectation made stricter by the owner decision:** the agent arm judges the question. Before a

  After the first half of the PIN and the pause (`question_on_screen_typing_<arm>`, OCR of the shot `pp_<arm>_after_pause`): judged in agent
  mode on every platform. Self-test: `precmd_secret_honor_ps1_pure_parts` (`question_in`, `asked_look_is_judged`, and that the case no longer
  says "recorded, not judged").
- **Hops.** `reader_question_in_conversation site=output|key|cap shown=true` after `prompt_reader_asks`, and `shown=false` at the wakeup after
  `prompt_reader_end`. A noted reader with no `shown=true` line: the block was not found (not early output, or still pending).
- **Kill switch.** `PHOSPHOR_READER_QUESTION_IN_AGENT_VIEW=0`: the block stays hidden in a conversation as in round 12; the keys still go to the

## Round 14: the Linux fallback key and query predictions in ssh sessions (design `docs/design/r14-secure.md`; #1932 #1982; nothing compiled or run when written)

### #1932: the secure-storage fallback is sealed with a per-install key

Unit tests, `crates/warpui_extras/src/secure_storage/linux_test.rs` (Linux only; run with the crate's suite). They use a temp fallback directory and keyring stand-ins (`FakeKeyring`: down; `PickyKeyring`: answers, refuses one key), never the real Secret Service: the direct `write_fallback_value` paths seal with the key file and do not consult the keyring.

| test | what it pins |
|---|---|
| `the_fallback_key_depends_on_the_secret_the_source_and_the_service` | key derivation (HKDF): same inputs open the blob; another secret, source (`K`/`F`), service name or associated data does not |
| `the_install_secret_round_trips_through_its_keyring_encoding` | the 64-hex keyring encoding of the 32-byte secret; short or non-hex text is rejected |
| `without_a_keyring_a_value_is_sealed_with_the_key_file_never_the_built_in_key` | the no-keyring path: `PSF1F` blob, a 32-byte 0600 key file, the built-in key does not open the blob, the value is not in the clear, a second handle reads it, only those two files exist |
| `a_legacy_blob_is_resealed_with_the_key_file_on_read` | migration: a blob sealed with the built-in key reads, is replaced by a `PSF1F` blob (0600, no temporary file left), reads again, and reads from a handle that never saw the old blob |
| `a_legacy_blob_survives_a_failed_reseal` | migration never costs the value: with the key file's name blocked the legacy blob is byte for byte unchanged and still reads |
| `a_legacy_blob_moves_into_a_working_keyring_without_a_key_file` | with a working keyring a legacy blob goes to the keyring (#1805 behaviour) and nothing is left in the directory |
| `a_lost_or_damaged_key_file_is_reported_and_never_replaced_on_read` | a missing or wrong-length key file is an error that is not `NotFound`; the blob and the damaged key file are untouched; a write is refused; restoring the key file restores the read |
| `a_tampered_blob_is_an_error` | a flipped byte in the header or the body fails |
| `concurrent_key_file_creation_settles_on_one_secret` | eight threads creating the key file all return the secret that is on disk; 0600; no temporary file left |
| `with_a_keyring_the_fallback_key_comes_from_the_secret_in_the_keyring` | a keyring that refuses one value: `PSF1K` blob, the secret stored once in the keyring, no key file, a later handle reads it; with no keyring the blob is an error at the fallback layer (`NotFound` to the caller, as for any unreadable blob) and stays in place |
| `a_malformed_keyring_secret_is_not_replaced` | a keyring secret that does not decode is left alone and the write uses the key file |

Changed tests, same assertions: `test_encrypt_decrypt_returns_same_value`, `test_encrypt_decrypt_works_across_storage_instances`, `test_decrypt_fails_on_malformed_data` and the seed of `reading_a_world_readable_fallback_migrates_it_to_owner_only` now call `legacy_encrypt` / `legacy_decrypt` (the built-in key only opens old blobs now; these tests keep that format readable). `read_fallback_value` returns the value with a `legacy` flag, so four reads take `.value`.

App: `keyring_unavailable_startup` (#1805) is unchanged. The change adds no keyring call at startup and no log line it judges; in its `absent` / `hang` launches a credential write now also creates `<state dir>/dev.phosphor.Phosphor-secure-storage.key`. There is no app case for the migration (it needs a state directory seeded by an older build).

### #2095: a fallback store that exists but cannot be opened is told to the user (round 16, `docs/design/r16-agent2.md` section 4)

Follow-up to #1932, owner decision 2026-11-11. No kill switch: the notice adds a toast and changes no read result (see the design note).

- Unit, `crates/warpui_extras/src/secure_storage/linux_test.rs`: `an_unreadable_fallback_is_recorded_for_the_notice_and_a_missing_one_is_not` (a value never saved and a blob that reads record nothing; a blob whose key file is lost still reads as "not found" for the caller but is recorded, subscribers hear of it once, later ones are only counted, the blob is untouched and no key file is made up) and `a_fallback_file_that_cannot_be_opened_is_not_reported_as_missing` (a mode-000 blob is an error at the fallback layer, not `NotFound`; skipped when the process can open it anyway, i.e. root). `unreadable_record_tests.rs` `the_first_unreadable_store_of_a_run_is_reported_once`.
- Unit, `app/src/secure_storage_notice_tests.rs`: `an_unreadable_store_shows_one_notice_per_launch`, `the_notice_stays_due_until_a_workspace_displayed_it`, `the_notice_text_carries_no_secret_and_no_path` (the string exists in en, ja, zh-CN and takes no arguments).
- Changed expectation: none. `read_fallback_value` now returns an error instead of `NotFound` for a blob that exists and cannot be opened or read (permission, I/O); the existing tests only read blobs that are absent (still `NotFound`) or present and openable.
- No app case: it needs a state directory with a blob and no key file before launch. The log line an app case can wait for is `Showing the secure-storage-unreadable notice` (the twin of `KEYRING_NOTICE_LINE` in `cases_ui.py`). Not written.
- Worked, unproven: nothing was compiled or run.

  expectation changed.

  (`selftest.py`, with the lab pieces): `lab.RAW_KEY_LOGGER` / `raw_key_logger_line`, `lab.raw_key_arrivals` (the logger's file),
  `cases_lab.key_write_times` (the app's `input_order pty_write bytes=N t=` lines; replies and Ctrl-C hops are other lines),
  `lab.raw_key_samples` (paired by position, and only when the arrivals are the typed keys and one byte was written per key),
  `lab.ss_tos_by_pid` and `cases_lab.tos_note`. What the lab cannot show: its netem link delays every class alike, so the class is
  read from the socket and never inferred from a time. What a result means: FAIL on the paired median = sharing the connection costs

  `tos_app` 0x0 next to `tos_plain` 0xb8 in a `helper` arm = OpenSSH 10.1 or later, the state the design note leaves to the owner.

## Round 14: test hygiene: view tests that read the pty recorder inside the update that wrote (design `docs/design/r14-hygiene.md`; nothing compiled or run when written)
**The rule (r13-pin2).** A pty write of the terminal view is an event (`Event::WriteBytesToPty`, `Event::WriteHandoffUserBytesToPty`).
`ViewContext::emit` queues it; the test's recorder (`collect_pty_writes`, `record_pty_writes`, `record_all_pty_writes`,
`subshell_pty_writes`, or a hand-rolled subscription) runs when the OUTERMOST update returns. Inside `terminal.update(&mut app, |view,
ctx| { .. })` the recorder holds only what earlier updates wrote: `assert!(pty_writes.borrow().is_empty())` after typing in the same
update passes whatever the app did, and an exact-content assertion there cannot pass. Read the recorder after the update.
**The audit of `terminal/view_test.rs` (round 14).** 389 reads of `pty_writes`, 72 of them (51 assertions) inside an `.update(`
closure, 9 more inside `with_ssh_hold_path` bodies (the helper ran the whole body in one update), and the same pattern under the names
`written`, `retries`, `etx_writes`, `executed`, `delivered`. Every in-update read was an `is_empty()` or a length; none could fail.
Each was read and sorted: a *real read* (nothing emitted before it in its update), *carried* (a later read after the update is still
empty; or the same update counts the held entries and the read after it has every byte exactly once, as one exact chunk, or in an
order an early write would break), or *vacuous* (nothing reads the recorder after the update at all, or a release follows in the same
update and only a flag stands between "held" and "written early and not again"). No assertion was removed or weakened; a vacuous one
now reads the recorder after the update, at the same point of the same sequence.
- **Moved after their update (nothing read the recorder after it; the claim "nothing reached the pty" was unproven):**
  `ssh_run_by_the_agent_does_not_take_the_agent_view_editor_keys`, `pane_key_with_editor_focus_is_inserted_once_and_not_written_to_the_pty`,
  `pane_key_typed_into_a_text_field_inside_the_pane_is_not_the_sinks`, `ssh_middle_click_paste_with_a_pending_read_keeps_typed_order_around_it`,
  `ssh_paste_between_held_keys_keeps_typed_order_in_both_modes` (both reads), `shadow_mode_changes_no_destination_and_logs_nothing_when_they_agree`,
  `replayed_text_is_delivered_by` (the legacy and table tests), `table_mode_text_replayed_after_an_ssh_recognised_at_preexec_only_is_held_not_run_locally`,
  `table_mode_text_replayed_into_a_new_ssh_connect_is_held_then_delivered_once`, `a_held_signal_is_discarded_when_the_connect_ends_without_a_remote_shell`,
  `only_table_mode_decides_live_keys_with_the_table`, `table_mode_text_typed_behind_a_gate_waits_as_a_neutral_entry_and_is_routed_when_it_opens`.
- **The update ended at the read, the next update continues (a release followed in the same update):**
  `keys_held_behind_the_subshell_bootstrap_reach_the_pty_in_order`, `text_typed_during_a_stalled_subshell_setup_is_held_then_delivered_in_order`
  (its first half), `key_typed_between_bootstrapped_and_the_first_prompt_in` (legacy and table),
  `typeahead_handoff_releases_held_shell_lines_to_the_pty_when_the_submit_runs_nothing`,
  `managed_ssh_block_end_without_a_verdict_releases_the_keys_to_the_local_shell`, `managed_ssh_verdict_before_ownership_is_honoured_for_each_verdict`
  (the managed arm), `managed_ssh_a_second_verdict_is_ignored`, `ssh_keys_typed_in_the_agent_view_editor_during_connect_are_held_and_handed_over_once`,
  `ssh_window_armed_at_preexec_for_a_users_submit_holds_the_agent_view_editor_keys`, `ssh_output_does_not_end_the_hold_ownership_does`,
  `a_young_hold_give_up_asks_for_the_request_decision` (the `retries` count), `a_precmd_does_not_commit_input_to_the_editor_so_a_precmd_read_gets_the_pin`,
  `a_hold_whose_wait_a_preexec_cleared_is_released_by_the_latch`, `a_command_running_past_the_prompt_hold_cap_keeps_its_keys_held_and_the_hold_on`
  (the read after the second cap), `a_subshell_that_exits_during_the_setup_ends_the_net` and
  `a_give_up_unregisters_the_probe_id_and_a_late_probe_answer_is_ignored` (both compared two lengths taken inside one update: 0 and 0).
- **If one of these fails in the next unit run:** the old assertion could not fail, so the failure is new information. Read the
  recorder's contents in the message: bytes there mean the app wrote where the test says it does not (APP, a key written early or a
  write the test's author never saw), or the test's claim was never true of the sequence it builds (TEST). A split delivers the first
  half's events before the second half runs, as the app does between two keys; only the test's recorder subscribes to the view's
  events in these tests, and nothing between the halves awaits, so timers and model events do not run there.
- **`with_ssh_hold_path` no longer hands its body the recorder.** The helper runs the whole body in one update, so all nine bodies
  that asserted `pty_writes.borrow().is_empty()` asserted nothing. Those nine now use `ssh_hold_path_writes_nothing` (or
  `ssh_hold_path_writes_nothing_in(label, ..)` in a loop over modes), which reads the recorder after the update and fails with what was
  written: `ssh_key_via_editor_route_before_handover_joins_the_hold`, `ssh_keys_by_every_route_before_handover_are_delivered_once_in_order`,
  `ssh_keys_in_a_focus_gap_join_the_hold`, `ssh_keys_during_connect_are_delivered_once_in_order`,
  `ssh_failed_connect_returns_the_text_to_the_input`, `ssh_paste_with_a_pending_read_keeps_typed_order_around_it`,
  `ssh_paste_with_a_pending_read_is_cancelled_with_the_hold`, `text_replayed_into_a_new_ssh_connect_is_held_not_dropped`,
  `ssh_key_offered_while_the_queue_is_busy_is_held_in_order`. In each the keys stay held or end in the input editor, so "nothing
  written by the end of the update" is the claim the body made. The four bodies that never looked at the recorder keep
  `with_ssh_hold_path`. A new scenario that expects a pty write reads its own recorder after its own update (not through these helpers).
- **Carried reads are kept and marked.** 27 in-update reads in `view_test.rs` (and one each in `view/group_1411_tests.rs` and
  `view/shared_queue_tests.rs`) are proven by other assertions; each now has a comment that starts `In-update recorder read` and says
  what carries it. `hold_a_young_enter` (a helper its callers run inside an update) says the same above its read.
- **Guard: `script/check_recorder_reads`** (in `precheck` and the CI `guards` job; row in the guard table of 2.3). A new in-update
  read fails the gate until it is moved after the update or given the marker comment with its reason. Writing a view test: type in one
  update, read the recorder after it; when a test needs "nothing yet" and then "now", that is two updates.
- **Not audited here:** recorders in other test files that are not `view_test.rs` / `view/*_tests.rs`, and the hand-rolled recorders
  `executed` / `delivered` / `etx_writes` beyond the 10 in-update reads listed in the design note (all carried or diagnostic).
## Round 14: the reader marker, an echoing question of a precmd function (design `docs/design/r14-readmark.md`; #2052; nothing compiled, no app run when written)
- **#2052: the reader marker, bash and zsh (fish not in this cut).** A precmd function's
  echoing `read -p "continue? "` after the prompt's Precmd: the bootstraps announce the read (`TtyReaderAsks`, OSC 9278 `f` form) and
  the hand-off treats it as the third source of the one reader fact (`prompt_reader_asks`; #2050 the tty, #2038 the screen). ONE kill
  switch, both sides: `PHOSPHOR_READER_MARKER=0` (the shell defines nothing and sends nothing; the app ignores a marker that arrives).
  Worked, unproven: nothing was compiled, no app run yet.
  - **Shell, `script/test_reader_marker`** (table above). Run here on bash 5.3.9 and zsh 5.9: all pass. Not run on bash 3.2.
    The existing bootstrap scripts were run against the changed files and pass: `test_init_shell_escaping` (330/330),
    `test_hijack_bootstrap`, `test_bash_bootstrap_nounset`, `test_zsh_bootstrap_strict_options`, `test_hook_forks`, `test_child_ps1`,
    `test_line_editor_markers --only bash|zsh`.
  - **Parser, `model/ansi/mod_test.rs`:** `parse_osc_tty_reader_asks_carries_session_and_sequence_number` (the bootstraps' exact
    bytes, the hex DCS form, an unregistered session dropped).
  - **Model, `model/terminal_model_test.rs`:** `a_tty_reader_marker_notes_the_reader_in_the_handoff_in_stream_order`.
  - **Hand-off, `model/typeahead_handoff_tests.rs`:** `a_precmd_reads_marker_takes_input_back_from_the_editor_and_gets_every_key` (the
    control is the first assertion: the tty look of #2050 notes nothing for an echoing read),
    `the_readers_marker_needs_no_tty_sample`, `the_readers_marker_is_honoured_only_for_the_prompt_the_app_is_at` (older / newer seq,
    another session, no session, no seq, after the line editor's marker, while a command runs, before any Precmd, the kill switch),
    `the_reader_markers_kill_switch_is_off_only_for_zero`, `a_readers_marker_parsed_before_the_precmd_commits_keeps_input_with_the_pty`,
    `a_marker_reader_ends_on_events_and_its_unread_keys_are_the_shells_line`, `a_readers_marker_ends_keys_following_the_editors_text`,
    `on_conpty_the_readers_marker_sends_the_first_key_to_the_reader_without_a_hold` (and with keys already held the marker changes
    nothing: the hold's cap decides from the screen, as before).
  - **View, `terminal/view_test.rs`:** `a_precmd_reads_marker_takes_the_keys_from_the_focused_editor` (Legacy and Table; control arm =
    no marker: the keys are the editor's and nothing is written), `a_precmd_reads_marker_is_found_at_the_wakeup_of_its_question`.
  - **Fuzz, `fuzz/fuzz_targets/typeahead_handoff.rs`:** event 28 is the marker followed by the view's look (the event range grew by
    one, so the bytes of an old corpus entry that chose event 28, the probe installation, now choose the marker).
  - **appci, new case `precmd_question_echo`** (`appci/cases_precmd_secret.py`, `cases.PROVING`, both session modes; Windows: Git Bash
    pane). A function registered by one sourced line asks ONCE at a later prompt (trigger file) with echo on; the answer is typed at
    10-25 ms per key with its Enter. Judged per arm: the question is on screen before a key (OCR, both modes), the answer file holds
    the answer whole, no `hop=enter_begin` shows the answer in the editor (`input_type=AI` there = sent to the model; since #2040
    also no `enter_begin` with a count-only buffer above 0, the form the log takes while a noted reader has the keys), no command the
    shell received holds it, the next typed line runs. Recorded, not judged: `echo_noted_by_marker_<arm>` (the log has
    `hop=prompt_reader_asks by=shell_marker`; when it does not, the note names the `hop=tty_reader_marker_ignored why=..` values or
    says no marker was seen). Arm `own`: the pane's own shell, no relaunch (Linux bash, macOS zsh, Git Bash). Arm `bash`: only where
    the pane is not bash and the platform is not Windows (macOS): one relaunch with `session.startup_shell_override = "bash"` (the
    system bash 3.2) and one to put the profile back. An arm whose shell is not what it wants is UNVERIFIABLE. Self-test
    `precmd_question_echo_pure_parts`.
  - **Why the case asks at a LATER prompt.** bash-preexec and zsh iterate a copy of `precmd_functions`, so a function appended after
    the bootstrap runs after `warp_update_prompt_vars` at the first prompt after its registration, outside the stage the marker
    covers. A case that asked at that very prompt would test the known limit, not the fix.
  - **Hops to read.** `prompt_reader_asks by=shell_marker took_from_editor=true`, `marker_reader_takes_input site=output|key`,
    `hand_route reason=prompt_reader` per key, `prompt_reader_end why=line_editor_signal`; in agent mode
    `reader_question_in_conversation site=output shown=true` then `shown=false`.

## Round 14, wave 1 (first half): five new app cases (`appci/cases_r14_w1a.py`; design `docs/design/r14-w1a.md`; #2072; nothing compiled or run when written)

Source: `docs/design/r14-test-gaps.md` 7.1, T1 to T5. All five are in `cases.PROVING` (fix tier until the owner graduates them), run in both
modes, type at 10 to 25 ms per key with an instant Enter, and judge the exact line the shell received. The received line comes from
`cases_r14_w1a.Received`: `rec.log` where the pane's shell has the rc hook, PSReadLine's history file in the Windows PowerShell pane. When
that record is missing the row is NOREF, never a pass on the effect file alone. Cost is an estimate per platform pass, both modes together;
the first run records the real numbers.

| case | checks | platforms | est. min |
|---|---|---|---|
| `history_up_recall` | Three commands; Up, Up, Enter runs the second again once; Up, an edit at the end of the line, Enter runs the edited line; Up then Down gives an empty line and a new command runs alone. The record holds exactly those six lines; the effect files hold exactly their tokens. | Wayland, X11, macOS, Windows PowerShell, Windows Git Bash (cmd.exe pane: SKIP, no record) | 2 |
| `scroll_keys_position` | 500 numbered lines, then a background job printing ten lines a second. PageUp three times: the view moved up, and after 3 s of new output the same numbered lines are on screen and none of the new ones. Block-up then Home: the view is above that, and 3 s later the screen has not changed. One typed key: one of the job's last lines is on screen. The command that key starts is exact. | Wayland, X11, macOS (OCR). Windows: SKIP, no OCR engine and no scroll-position hop | 3 |
| `find_basic` | Ten blocks of 30 lines, a token three times on one line of the third. A query that is nowhere: `hop=find_state` says 0 (control). The token: 3 matches; the match is on screen (the app's `hop=find_scroll` geometry; with OCR a neighbour word that was not on screen before); Enter moves the focus, Shift+Enter returns it; after Escape a typed command reaches the shell exactly and the record holds nothing else. | Wayland, X11, macOS (OCR and log); Windows Git Bash (log only). PowerShell pane: SKIP (needs `rec.log`) | 2 |
| `tab_lifecycle_keys` | A tab running a loop that appends a line twice a second: the close key asks (app log line), Escape keeps the tab and the loop, the close key and Enter close the tab and the loop is gone within the undo-close window (60 s) plus 15 s; on POSIX the tab's shell pid is gone too. A second tab in its own directory with one command: close key (no question), undo key (`ctrl+alt+t`, `APPCI_KEY_REOPEN`): the tab is back in its directory and nothing ran again. Tab counts from `hop=tab_activate`. | Wayland, X11, both Windows panes, and macOS since round 15 (#2061: Cmd-W through `appkey`, undo `cmd+shift+t`; the question is the app's own native alert, Escape = Cancel, Return = 'Yes, close') | 3 |
| `routing_table_powershell` | The PowerShell rows of the routing corpus, a command on PATH, two shell-structure lines (#1560), the prose lines, the installed-head English lines and, in agent mode, the mistyped-command lines (#1980). Shell = the exact line in PSReadLine's history; agent = not in the history and the app logged an agent-routed Enter. A line in neither is LOST. | Windows PowerShell pane only (the Git Bash pane has `routing_table`) | 3 |

Notes for whoever reads the first run:

- **A new trace line.** `hop=find_state event=<query|next> count=<n> focused=<index|none> scanning=<bool>` is logged after a Find query edit and
  after next / previous (`TerminalView::log_find_state`; format pinned by `find_state_hop_detail_format_is_pinned` in
  `app/src/terminal/find/model_tests.rs` and by the self-test). Trace only: nothing is read unless input-order logging is on. Counts only,
  never the query.
- **`scroll_keys_position` streams from a background job** because, while a foreground command runs, PageUp and Home are written to that
  program (#2080). The case therefore does not cover a foreground stream; since round 15 `scroll_keys_foreground` does (Shift+PageUp /
  PageDown / Home / End scroll there, see the round 15 section). Its scroll-to-top step is block-up then Home (Home alone moves the cursor in the input).
- **`tab_lifecycle_keys` waits for the undo-close window.** A tab closed with a running command keeps its shell for
  `general.undo_close.grace_period` (60 s) so the close can be undone; "the loop is gone" is judged at 75 s (`APPCI_UNDO_CLOSE_WAIT_S`).
  The close / undo half runs inside that wait. Escape and Enter are sent only after the app logged that it asked: without that line the case
  fails and sends neither.
- **macOS PageUp.** `backend.MacBackend.SPECIAL` gained `pageup` (116) and `pagedown` (121) for `scroll_keys_position`.
- **Each oracle can fail.** The self-test `r14_w1a_wave1_cases_pure_parts_and_registry` feeds every verdict helper a wrong result (a recall
  that picked another line, a merged line, a view that followed the output, a wait with no output, a focus that did not move, a loop that
  keeps beating, prose in the shell) and pins the app texts and keys the cases depend on.
## Round 14 wave 2: agent and state cases T11 to T15 (design `docs/design/r10-r14-w2a.md`; source `docs/design/r14-test-gaps.md` 7.1; nothing compiled or run when written)
Five appci cases in `script/realapp/appci/cases_agent_w2.py`. All are in `cases.PROVING` and `cases.PROVING_FAKE`: the fix tier plays them in its
`agent@fake` pass (agent mode, the scripted `fake_model.py`; no real provider is ever sent anything). They stay in `PROVING` until the owner moves
them. Platforms: Linux (Wayland; X11 plays them too), macOS, the Windows Git Bash pane (the PowerShell pane SKIPs with the reason in
`winmap.GITBASH_ONLY`). Each case edits the scratch profile's `settings.toml` with the app stopped and puts the file back byte for byte at the end,
so each costs two to four relaunches. Cost is an estimate per platform pass; none is measured.
| case | min (estimate) | what it does | how a defect shows |
| `agent_model_switch` (T11) | 3 | two fake providers on two ports, each with its own key header. Prompt 1 goes to A. `/model` + Enter, the model's name, Enter (keyboard only), prompt 2; the same back to A, prompt 3 | prompt 2 is not provider B's newest user turn exactly once, or A received it in any request of any purpose (`fake.seen`); B's request does not carry turn 1 exactly once (user prompt and reply); the app's `[byop] opening stream: model=` line names the wrong model; after the switch back the same for A with turns 1 and 2; A's key header at B or B's at A. A provider that never received its OWN key makes the key part `noref` |
| `agent_anthropic_wire` (T12) | 4 | the provider is `api_type = "anthropic"` at the same fake, which answers `POST /v1/messages` with the Anthropic event stream. A text turn, then the bodies of `agent_approval`, `agent_question_answer` and `agent_fault_disconnect` | the first prompt does not arrive on the Anthropic wire (nothing else is judged then) or arrives on the Ollama wire; the turn does not end `success`; no `anthropic-version` header; any failure of the three borrowed oracles; a step whose chat requests did not all use the Anthropic wire. A SKIP inside a borrowed body is a FAIL here (the model is scripted). A session whose keyring cannot be read is `noref` with that reason (the app does not send a keyed provider's request without the keyring) |
| `agent_autorun_permissions` (T13) | 4 | the safe allow list (`agents.warp_agent.permissions.safe_command_allowlist_enabled`, list `["ls"]`). Control with it OFF: `ls d`. ON: `ls d`, `rm f`, `ls d; rm f`, `ls $(rm f)`, `cat script \| sh`. The command reaches the model through the prose prompt "Please run scripted command KEY" (a typed `;`, `\|` or `$(...)` could be routed to the shell by its syntax) | OFF: `ls` does not stop at a card. ON: `ls` shows a card, or the model never gets the listing; any other command runs without a card, its file is gone before Enter or after a reject, or (where the app logs pty writes) the command was written to the pty; the approved `rm` does not remove its file (then the hold proved nothing) |
| `agent_conversation_resume` (T14) | 3 | `restore_session` on; one finished turn whose title the fake model sets to "Tagged <tag>"; quit (Linux) or kill (macOS, Windows); relaunch; `/conversations` + Enter, the tag, Enter; a follow-up | a model request on its own after the relaunch; the pane is not in the agent view after the reopen; the earlier prompt is not on screen (OCR) or, with no OCR, the app put back no AI block for that conversation (`hop=conversation_restored`); the follow-up request carries the earlier prompt or the earlier reply 0 times (a new conversation) or twice |
| `agent_block_context` (T15) | 3 | custom secret regex `APPCISEC_[A-Z0-9]{16}`, display mode `asterisks`. Per setting (redaction OFF, then ON): one turn, `cat` of a file with a token line and a secret line, a keyboard copy of that block's output, then a question | OFF (the owner's setting): the question's user message has no `<attached_context>`, lacks the token line, or does not hold the secret unchanged; the copy lacks the secret. ON: the question's message still holds the secret, ANY request of any purpose since the question holds it, or the copy holds it. A copy that did not select this block is `noref` for the copy |
Harness pieces added for them (all self-tested in `script/realapp/appci/selftest_agent_w2.py`, which `selftest.py` appends to its checks):
- `fake_model.py` speaks a second wire. A POST whose path ends in `/messages` is an Anthropic Messages request: `anthropic_to_messages` reads
  `system`, text, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks into the role / content list every trigger and oracle already reads, the same `reply_for`
  answers, and `anthropic_events` writes `message_start`, one text block as `text_delta`s, each tool call as a `tool_use` block whose input comes
  as two `input_json_delta` pieces, `message_delta` with `stop_reason`, `message_stop`. `"stream": false` gets one message object (titles).
  Faults with an Anthropic form: `status`, `disconnect`, `delay`; any other fault kind on that wire is answered 501 and listed in `fake.unknown`.
  `fake.by_wire` counts chat requests per wire.
- `fake.seen` / `seen_with(token, since, wire, purpose)`: the text of every POST of every purpose, for "did this text reach this provider at all".
- `start(active=False)` starts a second provider without replacing `FakeModel.ACTIVE`.
- A title request whose user text holds `conversation tag <TAG>` is answered `Tagged <TAG>`; every other title is unchanged.
- `Please run scripted command <KEY>` answers with `fake_model.SCRIPTED_COMMANDS[KEY]` as a `run_shell_command` call.
- App, trace only: `hop=conversation_restored conv=<id> ai_blocks=<n> startup=<0|1>` (`terminal/view/load_ai_conversation.rs`,
  `restore_conversations_from_block_params`), once per conversation whose AI blocks were put back into a pane. Unit test
  `conversation_restored_detail_names_conversation_count_and_origin` pins the format. It goes through the input-order hop logger, so the Windows
  `RUST_LOG` already shows it.
Not covered by these cases: a terminal-mode twin (the scripted model exists only in the `agent@fake` pass); the `/auto-approve` switch with the
command deny list (T13 tests the allow list path); an explicit "attach this block" key (T15 uses the automatic attachment of blocks run since the
last prompt); the strikethrough display mode's copy.
Run one: `APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1 python3 script/realapp/appci/run.py --modes agent --cases agent_model_switch` (any of the five names).
## Round 14, wave 2b: agent attention and state across restarts (T16 to T20; design `docs/design/r14-w2b.md`; nothing compiled or run when written)
Five app cases from `docs/design/r14-test-gaps.md` 7.1, in `appci/cases_r14_state.py`. All five are in `cases.PROVING` (fix tier) and
stay there: no case leaves PROVING before a numbered release. Worked, unproven: only the self-test ran. Typing is at 10 to 25 ms per
key with instant Enter and every typed line is checked against what the shell received (`rec.log`; the PSReadLine history in the
PowerShell pane). Costs are estimates per platform pass, both modes together; the first run records the real ones.
| case | modes | platforms | est. | what a defect looks like |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_hidden_tab_attention` | agent, fake-model pass (`PROVING_FAKE`) | Linux, macOS; Windows when the profile has vertical tabs on (else SKIP: no live settings rewrite there) | 3 min | the row of a hidden tab never shows the waiting state, shows it for the wrong tab, or keeps it after the answer; keys typed in tab 1 answer the card |
| `settings_ui_toggle_persists` | terminal, agent | Linux (Wayland, X11), macOS; `winmap.NOT_WINDOWS` | 3 min | a keyboard change writes other keys, is not applied, is gone after a relaunch; a hand edit is not reloaded (#2026) |
| `osc52_write_read` | terminal, agent | Linux, macOS, Windows Git Bash (`winmap.GITBASH_ONLY`); the ssh half needs the ssh test host | 2 min | a program's OSC 52 write does not reach the clipboard; a read query is answered |
| `history_survives_restart` | terminal, agent | all five (both Windows panes) | 3 min | a command typed before a quit or a kill -9 is not recalled, is recalled as another line or twice; an agent prompt lands in the shell's history file |
| `restore_shows_history` | terminal, agent | Linux, macOS, Windows Git Bash (`winmap.GITBASH_ONLY`) | 3 min | the restored view does not hold the earlier output or conversation; a command re-runs |
Estimated extra fix-tier time: Linux about +14 min, macOS about +14 min, Windows about +10 min over both panes.
Two trace-only app log lines were added for these cases (through `warpui::input_order::log_hop`, so they are on wherever the other
`hop=` lines are, the Windows launcher included; one `enabled()` check when logging is off; no behaviour change):
- `hop=vtab_row_status view=<id> status=<name>` (`workspace/view/vertical_tabs.rs` `log_row_status_hop`): the status badge the
  vertical tabs panel draws for a terminal row, written when it changes for that view. Names: `ConversationStatus::hop_state_name()`
  (`blocked`, `in_progress`, `success`, `error`, `transient_error`, `cancelled`, `waiting_for_events`; `hop=turn` uses the same
  function now), `none` for an agent row with no badge, `no_agent` for a plain terminal. Unit tests in `vertical_tabs_tests.rs`:
  `conversation_status_hop_names_are_the_ones_the_cases_read`, `row_status_name_follows_the_badge_the_row_draws`,
  `row_status_hop_has_a_fixed_format_and_logs_only_changes`.
- `hop=osc52_clipboard op=<write|read> access=<deny|write_only|read_write> allowed=<bool>` (`Osc52ClipboardAccess::hop_detail`,
  logged where `terminal/view.rs` decides a `ClipboardStore` / `ClipboardLoad`). Unit test in `terminal/settings_tests.rs`:
  `osc52_hop_detail_names_the_request_the_setting_and_the_outcome`.
Per case:
- `agent_hidden_tab_attention`. The waiting state is an icon badge on the row; the word "Blocked" is only in the hover sidecar, so
  OCR cannot be the oracle (it only notes whether the row's title was read; the screenshot is for a person). Tab 2 asks the scripted
  model with the `ask_slow` fault (the question arrives 12 s after the prompt); the case shows tab 1 and proves it answers (`pwd`).
  Then nothing is typed until the row is judged: the ask action reaches `blocked`, a `hop=vtab_row_status ... status=blocked` line
  follows within 5 s, logged after the switch, for exactly one view, and no row was `blocked` before the question arrived (the two
  controls: a hop that never, or always, says `blocked` fails). A burst of shell lines and one prose line typed in tab 1 are exact
  and leave the ask open (no tool result at the model). Tab 2's key and Enter: the ask is `done`, the model gets the answer, the
  turn ends `success`; back in tab 1 that row ends `success`. A question that arrives before tab 2 is hidden is NOREF, not a pass.
- `settings_ui_toggle_persists`. Only the Network page has a keyboard focus ring, so the two changes are made through the command
  palette ("vertical tab layout", "Increase font size"; `ctrl-shift->` is tried when the palette row did nothing). Oracles: the
  settings key opens one more tab (`hop=tab_activate count=`); the file's flat key set differs in exactly
  `appearance.vertical_tabs.enabled` and `appearance.text.font_size` (`toml_flat`, any other key is named in the failure); the
  pane's `stty size` moves (no Pillow needed); after a relaunch both values are in the file and "Decrease font size" writes the
  saved value minus one (an app that ignored the file writes its default minus one); a hand edit moves `stty size` (control); the
  file put back to the bytes the app wrote last moves it back (#2026); the app's next write keeps the undone value. The original
  file is restored at the end. SKIP when the profile writes the vertical tabs key in a form `toml_text` cannot read.
- `osc52_write_read`. The expectation follows `terminal.osc52_clipboard_access` when the profile sets it (unset: write allowed,
  read denied, #1963). Write: `printf '\033]52;c;<base64>\a'`, the clipboard is a sentinel first and must hold the token after;
  one `op=write` hop. Read on Linux and macOS: `appci/osc52_reader.py` (raw tty) sends the query and DSR 5; it must get `ESC[0n`
  (control: replies reach it) and no `ESC]52;` bytes nor the clipboard's base64; one `op=read allowed=false` hop (the query did
  arrive). Git Bash has no termios in the harness Python: the query goes out with `printf`, the hop is the verdict and the exact
  lines typed right after show no reply landed in the shell's input. Then the write and the query again from the remote shell of
  `ssh fake`. No ssh test host: a note in a local run, NOREF where the run requires the host (#2043).
- `history_survives_restart`. Per round three append-commands, the stop, the relaunch, three recalls: Up + Enter (the last
  command; on Windows the command's own prefix is typed first, because the harness types a key-proof line after every relaunch),
  a typed prefix + Up + Enter, Ctrl-R + a fragment + Enter. Each must make the shell receive exactly the original line once, and
  the effect file must hold each token twice. Round 1 stops with the quit key on Linux and by pid elsewhere (said in a note),
  round 2 with kill -9 (`taskkill /T /F` on Windows). The shell's own history file (`.bash_history`, `.zsh_history`, PSReadLine's)
  holds each typed command at most once before the recalls, and never the agent prompt typed between the rounds (agent mode).
- `restore_shows_history`. `restore_session` on for the case (`fresh_app` puts it back). The token is printed by
  `printf '%s%s\n' A B`, so only the OUTPUT holds it. Find is judged from the app's `hop=find_scroll` lines, no OCR: `result=scroll`
  for the token before the stop (precondition) and after the relaunch; a token never printed must not give `result=scroll`
  (control). Agent mode adds one agent turn and the same Find for its text (with the fake model the token is in the reply only;
  with a real provider it is the prompt's); no provider, a turn that did not end `success`, or a Find that does not reach the
  conversation before the stop make that half NOREF with the reason. Nothing re-ran: the effect file and `rec.log` are unchanged.
Self-test: `r14_w2b_state_cases` (`appci/selftest.py`) runs every pure part on the input a defect would produce (no waiting row,
two waiting rows, a row waiting too early; another settings key changed; an OSC 52 reply split over two reads; a recall that ran
the typed prefix; a Find with no match), pins the registry rows and the app texts the cases read, and fails when a case loses one
of its controls.
Run one: `python3 script/realapp/appci/run.py --cases history_survives_restart` (add `APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1` for
`agent_hidden_tab_attention`).
