key with an instant Enter, the exact received line checked from `rec.log` and effect files. No fake model. Self-test:
`r14_window_use_cases_pure_parts` (every judge passes the right result and fails a wrong one; the app's line shapes are pinned against the Rust
source; no case skips after its first check). One trace-only app line was added for T26: `input_order hop=grid_resize rows=<n> cols=<n>
pane=<id>` (`app/src/terminal/view/grid_resize_hop.rs`, logged in `TerminalView::resize_internal` when rows or columns change; unit test
`detail_names_rows_then_cols_then_pane`; no behaviour reads it).
| case | platforms | est. minutes per pass (both modes, not measured) | Windows |
| `resize_reflow_output` | Wayland, X11, macOS, Windows Git Bash pane | 2.5 (table: 4) | `GITBASH_ONLY` since round 15 wave 4 (`SetWindowPos`) |
| `context_menu_actions` | Wayland, X11, macOS (round 15, #2061), Windows Git Bash pane | 1.5 (table: 3) | `GITBASH_ONLY` since round 15 wave 4 (SendInput) |
| `tab_pointer_use` | Wayland, X11, macOS (round 15, #2061) | 3 (table: 3) | `NOT_WINDOWS`: not ported (the pointer exists since round 15 wave 4; the shell-pid probe is POSIX) |
| `focus_cycle` | Wayland, X11, macOS, Windows (both panes) | 1.5 (table: 3) | `BOTH`; typing half only |
| `minimize_fullscreen` | Wayland, X11, macOS | 3 (table: 3; 30 s of it is the hidden window, `APPCI_MINIMIZE_S`) | `NOT_WINDOWS`: no window-state call (round 15 wave 4 built the resize only) |
- `resize_reflow_output` (G34). The window is driven per backend (`Window`): sway commands addressed by the app's pid, `xdotool windowsize`, System
  Events on macOS. (1) `ui_copy_wrapped_output`'s fixture is printed and its block output copied (block-up, copy-output; the clipboard holds a
  sentinel first); the window is made narrower, then wider, and each time the copy must be byte-identical to the first. A resize counts only when
  it provably took: a new `hop=grid_resize` line, else a changed screenshot; otherwise that size is UNVERIFIABLE. (2) `bash wu_stream.sh <tag> 700
  0.02` (a SIGWINCH trap that appends `stty size`) prints 700 numbered lines while 60 resizes are sent in 10 s (macOS: as many as System Events
  manages in 11 s; the count is the metric `rapid_resizes`): the copied output holds all 700 lines in order (`judge_stream_copy` names the first lost,
  doubled or out-of-order line), the trap ran at least once, and a `stty size` typed afterwards equals the latest `hop=grid_resize` (a last resize
  that never reached the pty, or reached it out of order, fails here). (3) `vim -u NONE -N` is open while the window is resized; `:call
  writefile([&lines.' '.&columns], ...)` must report the pty's size (vim missing: UNVERIFIABLE). (4) The original size returns (`stty size` equal to
  the first reading, and to the grid). Controls: the first copy is judged against the printed lines before any resize; a log with no
  `hop=grid_resize` makes the grid comparison UNVERIFIABLE, never a pass. `APPCI_RR_LINES` changes the line count (minimum 200).
- `context_menu_actions` (G35, F13). Linux pointer backends. Every pointer position is the app's own `appci_find` line (#1789): the printed token,
  a probe typed into the input, and the menu entries `Copy output`, `Copy command`, `Paste` (the reader here takes tokens with a space;
  `cases_ui.FIND_RE` does not). A menu entry must be drawn after the right click; an older sighting is never used. Right click on the block, `Copy
  output`: the clipboard is exactly the output token (the typed command does not contain it). `Copy command`: exactly the command line. Right click
  in the input, `Paste`: the app's `hop=enter_begin` at the next Enter holds exactly the clipboard text; in a terminal session `rec.log` and the
  effect file hold it too (in an agent conversation a line the app sends to the agent is noted and stopped). SKIP: no pointer tool (macOS), the
  profile's `terminal.input.right_click_behavior` is paste, or the window position cannot be read. UNVERIFIABLE: no `appci_find` line for the
  token or the probe (an app without the hook). On Wayland without the virtual pointer holder a missing pointer effect is NOREF, as in
  `ui_mouse_select_copy`. No OCR anywhere in this case (self-test).
- `tab_pointer_use` (G36). Linux pointer backends. Four tabs, each in its own directory named by a token registered with the find hook before any
  title holds it; each tab runs `echo <token> $$ >> ...` (the tab's shell pid). The strip's spot of each title is the topmost sighting on one row,
  left to right in tab order (horizontal bar), or the leftmost, top to bottom (vertical panel); `pick_tab_spots` refuses anything else, and OCR is
  the fallback for a title the hook never reported. In the layout the profile shows: click on the third tab (its own `pwd`), the second tab dragged
  onto the third (tab number keys 2 and 3 answer from each other's directory), middle click on the last tab (its shell pid is gone within 15 s, the
  app's tab count drops by one, no other tab's shell died). Then `appearance.vertical_tabs.enabled` is flipped in the settings file (the screen must
  change) and the same three actions run on the three tabs left; the file's bytes are written back. A failed step ends the round (the order is no
  longer certain) and the other layout is then not played. UNVERIFIABLE: titles not locatable in a layout, or a settings form `toml_text` cannot
  edit.
- `focus_cycle` (G37). The reference terminal of the platform (`cases.ref_terminal`: foot / xterm, Terminal.app, conhost / Windows Terminal) takes
  the focus; three lines are typed there (its own effect file must hold them, else "away" is UNVERIFIABLE). The focus returns and one line is typed
  with no settle: its effect file and the pane's `rec.log` (PSReadLine history in the PowerShell pane) hold exactly that line and none of the
  reference's, and `key_event_audit` over the app log of the away window counts 0 keys. POSIX only: `printf '\033[?1004h'; python3 bytes_reader.py
  ...` runs in the pane, the focus goes away and back once, a `k` is typed: the reader received exactly `1b5b4f 1b5b49 6b 03`
  (`judge_focus_bytes`: one focus-out, one focus-in, in that order, then the key; any other byte is a key typed into the other window). On Windows
  the focus-reporting half is noted as not run (ConPTY turns focus changes into console records; `bytes_reader.py` needs termios; the Windows
  reference has no switch-back), so a Windows PASS is the typing half only. SKIP: no reference terminal (the reason is the launcher's).
- `minimize_fullscreen` (G38). A stream (`wu_stream.sh`, one line per 50 ms) runs 5 s shown (the control), then the window is hidden for 30 s:
  Wayland by switching sway's workspace away (sway has no minimise; the window is not shown and gets no frame callbacks), X11 by `xdotool
  windowminimize`, or `windowunmap` when the display has no window manager, macOS by `AXMinimized`. The row's `hide` metric says which. After the
  return: with `hop=frame_drawn` in the log the first frame is within `APPCI_RESTORE_FRAME_MAX_MS` (2000) of the show call (macOS: a frame line
  within 3 s); the largest main-thread item (`hop=ui_item`) of the next 3 s is within the larger of the 16 ms warn bound and 3x the control's
  largest item (the control keeps a software renderer's ordinary frames from failing it); the copied output holds every line; `stty size` is
  unchanged; a typed burst is exact. Fullscreen: F11 on Linux (the app's `root_view:toggle_fullscreen`; the sway window is made floating and
  smaller first, a borderless tiled window already covers the output), `AXFullScreen` on macOS (the guard refuses cmd-ctrl-f). `stty size` must
  grow, typing is exact, and after the second toggle the size is the one before. UNVERIFIABLE: the window could not be hidden; an X display with
  no window manager where F11 changed nothing (the job's Xvfb: the request needs a manager); a log with no frame line.
What the first run must show: a `hop=grid_resize` line in the app log of every resize; `appci_find` lines for the menu entries; which halves
come back UNVERIFIABLE on X11 (no window manager) and whether tab titles are locatable in the horizontal bar. None of these cases has run.
## Round 14 wave 3a: pointer and pane cases, T21 to T25 (design `docs/design/r10-r14-w3a.md`; source `docs/design/r14-test-gaps.md` 7.1; nothing compiled or run when written)
Five new app cases in `script/realapp/appci/cases_pointer.py`, all in `cases.PROVING` (fix tier; graduation is the owner's). Both session modes. Typing at 10 to 25 ms per key with an instant Enter; every typed line is checked against `rec.log`. No Rust changed and no app hop was added: every arm is judged by an effect (the clipboard, PRIMARY, an effect file, the bytes a program received, `stty size`, what a recording opener was handed, an `strace` file). Positions come from the app's find hook when it is on, else from OCR (on Linux today always OCR, see the finding below). A screen read that finds none of a case's words is UNVERIFIABLE (status `noref`), never a pass.
| case | platforms | what a defect looks like | cost, both modes (estimate, not measured) |
| `link_and_path_click` (T21) | Wayland, X11. macOS since round 15 (#2061): runs only where the owner installed the recording URL handler, else SKIP with `NEEDS:`. Windows SKIP (not ported to the Windows pointer, `winmap.NOT_WINDOWS`). | Hover alone calls the opener; Ctrl+click on a URL or an OSC 8 link hands the opener nothing, something twice, or not exactly the URL / the link's target (the OSC 8 text is a different word); Ctrl+click on `file:140` opens nothing, another file, or the file at line 1; the `strace` file shows a destination beyond loopback and the configured model (the printed hosts are 192.0.2.x, so a fetch by the app itself is seen). | 3 min (two relaunches per mode) |
| `selection_modes` (T22) | Wayland, X11, macOS since round 15 (#2061), Windows Git Bash pane (round 15 wave 4). | The clipboard (sentinel first) is not exactly the word after a double click, the line after a triple click, the tail of line 1 and head of line 2 after a drag over two blocks, one block's output after a plain click + copy-output, three blocks' outputs after Shift+click + copy-output, or the dragged words while the program under them rewrites its last line ten times a second. | 3 min |
| `primary_and_middle_click` (T23) | Wayland, X11. macOS, Windows SKIP. | With `terminal.copy_on_select` off: PRIMARY does not hold the dragged / double-clicked text, or CLIPBOARD lost its sentinel. With it on: CLIPBOARD does not hold the same text. Either arm: `echo ` + middle click in the input + ` >> file` is not received as `echo <word> >> file` (CLIPBOARD holds another text then, so a paste from the wrong selection shows). | 2 min |
| `wheel_scroll` (T24) | Wayland with the virtual pointer, X11. macOS, Windows SKIP. | Wheel up over 240 printed lines does not show earlier lines, or wheel down does not come back; the same in `less`; a program that asked for SGR mouse reporting does not get press + release for a click on its banner, `ESC[<64` for wheel up, `ESC[<65` for wheel down, or the key typed afterwards is not last and alone. | 3 min |
| `pane_resize_maximize` (T25) | Wayland, X11, macOS (keys only). Windows SKIP. | After split right the probe (`sh -c 'echo $PPID $(stty size)'`) runs in the old shell or the panes are not narrower; maximised, the pane is not as wide as the unsplit one or the probe runs in the other shell; restored, the size is not exactly the split size; `Move divider left` from the command palette (twice) does not make the right pane wider and the left narrower with the total kept; Linux: a 120 px drag of the divider does not, by about that many columns, or a program in the pane saw another size on SIGWINCH; after `exit` the first pane is not as wide as at the start. | 3 min |
Details a reader of a red row needs:
- **Modifier clicks.** X11: `xdotool keydown ctrl|shift`, the click, `keyup`. Wayland: one `wtype -M <mod> -s 1500 -m <mod>` runs while the virtual pointer clicks (`cases_pointer.Held`). A held modifier is not a key in the injector accounting. A link opens only after a hover (the app highlights it first; a file path is an async scan), so the pointer rests on the word, moves 2 px and waits before the click.
- **The recording opener.** `<scratch home>/lc_bin` holds `xdg-open` and the names the `open` crate falls back to; each appends `call<TAB>name<TAB>args` to a log and exits 0. It is first on the app's PATH only for the case's own launch (`App.extra_env`), which runs under `strace -f -e trace=network` when `strace` works (else that claim is UNVERIFIABLE). The case ends with a normal relaunch.
- **The path arm has two right answers.** `code.editor.open_file_editor` decides (default: the system handler). The recorder got exactly the absolute path, or the file is drawn in the app: the file has one token on line 1 and another on line 140, neither is printed in the terminal, and the clicked line's token must be the one on screen. The metric `path_opened_by` says which happened. `root_view:add_file_pane` (named by the gap note) is dispatched only for a file the OS hands over, not for a click in the terminal, and is not used.
- **Shift+click is the block range** in this app (`BlockSelectAction::MouseUp`), not a text extension; the case judges copy-output of the selected blocks, which carries no prompt.
- **PRIMARY.** `xsel -p` / `wl-copy --primary`, `wl-paste --primary`. A display where a written PRIMARY cannot be read back SKIPs with that reason. A profile with `system.linux_selection_clipboard = false` or `terminal.input.middle_click_paste_enabled = false`, or with `terminal` written as a dotted key or inline table, SKIPs with the reason. The settings file's bytes are restored in `finally`.
- **The wheel.** X11: `xdotool click 4|5`. Wayland: `axis` on the virtual pointer (60 units a step); without the holder the case SKIPs (the sway seat has no wheel). Where the profile sets `terminal.mouse_reporting_enabled` or `terminal.scroll_reporting_enabled` to false the program must receive nothing for it (`reporting_expected`).
- **`alt_screen_mouse_reporting` (F12).** The click of `wheel_scroll` goes ON the program's banner word. The old case clicks 60 px below the banner (X11) or sweeps `x = window left + 140` (Wayland, inside the vertical tabs panel of the owner's layout). If the new click arm passes where the old case fails, the old case's placement is the fault (TEST). Not proven until a run; the old case is unchanged.
- **Resize by keyboard is the palette entry.** The resize bindings have a default key on macOS only (`cmd-ctrl-arrows`) and the macOS backend refuses every Ctrl+Cmd chord, so all platforms run `Resize pane > Move divider left` from the command palette (self-test pins the entry's text and that the backend still refuses the chord).
- **The divider drag** (Linux): the divider is 2 px wide. A SIGWINCH logger runs in the right pane, and the pointer drags from 1, 2, ... 40 px left of that pane's first column until the logger sees a resize. No hit is UNVERIFIABLE, not a failure.
Self-tests (`script/realapp/appci/selftest_pointer.py`, run by `run.py --self-test` and `selftest.py`): `pointer_cases_registry_r14_w3a` (PROVING only, both modes, Windows reasons, this section, the maximise key and the palette text against the app's sources), `pointer_fixture_and_screen_read_parts`, `pointer_sgr_and_reporting_parts`, `pointer_selection_and_clipboard_parts`, `pointer_link_opener_parts`, `pointer_pane_probe_parts`. Each judge is fed the wrong results it must reject (only the key arriving, arrow keys instead of wheel reports, a screen that did not move, the OSC 8 text opened instead of its target, a file opened at line 1, a maximise that did nothing, a divider that moved the other way).
Run: `python3 script/realapp/appci/run.py --cases link_and_path_click,selection_modes,primary_and_middle_click,wheel_scroll,pane_resize_maximize`.
Harness finding, not changed here (#2082): `app.py` sets `PHOSPHOR_APPCI_FIND_FILE` only in the Windows launcher, so the find hook (#1789) has never been on in a Linux or macOS run and every Linux pointer case has placed the pointer by OCR (r12a rows carry "app find hook gave no position"). The statement above in 2.8 that `app.py` sets it holds for Windows only.

## Round 15 wave 4 core: the grid snapshot hook and the freeze step, T34 and T36 (design `docs/design/r15-w4core.md`; #2075; source `docs/design/r14-test-gaps.md` 7.1; nothing compiled or run when written)
Two harness capabilities and the cases that use them, in `script/realapp/appci/cases_w4core.py`. `grid_snapshot_render` and `freeze_and_wake` are in `cases.PROVING` (fix tier; graduation is the owner's), `freeze_and_wake` also in `PROVING_FAKE` (it needs the scripted model, agent mode only); the lab arm `lab_freeze_and_wake.*` is in `PROVING_LAB`.

**The grid snapshot hook (app side, `app/src/terminal/appci_grid.rs`).** A test-only hook, off unless `PHOSPHOR_APPCI_GRID_DIR` names a directory (then one cached check per painted grid; no release user has it set). The harness appends a token (6 to 64 letters or digits) to `<dir>/request`; the app re-reads that file when its size or mtime changed, at most every 200 ms. Whenever `render_grid` paints a grid whose visible rows show a listed token, the app writes `<dir>/<token>.grid` (temporary file, then rename; rewritten only when the content changed): one JSON object, `{"v":1,"token":T,"cols":N,"cursor":null|{"row":R,"col":C,"shape":"block|underline|beam|hollow_block|hidden"},"rows":[{"row":R,"text":X,"cells":[[col,text,fg,bg,attrs],..]},..]}`. A cell that paints nothing is not listed. Colours are named as the escape sequence gave them, not resolved through the theme: `named:red`, `named:brightgreen`, `named:foreground`, `idx:196`, `rgb:ff8800`. Attribute letters, in this order: `b` bold, `d` dim, `i` italic, `u` underline, `U` double underline, `s` strikeout, `r` reverse, `h` hidden, `W` wide character, `S` its spacer cell, `L` the spacer left at a row's end when a wide character wrapped. `cursor` is present only when the cursor of that grid is drawn: always on the alternate screen while the program shows it; in a block's output only while the block is latched as interactive. A grid whose secrets are being redacted is never written, and nothing goes to the log. `app.py` sets the variable to `<scratch home>/appci_grid` in the Linux, macOS and Windows launchers. Rust unit tests: `app/src/terminal/appci_grid_tests.rs` (token rule, colour names, attribute letters and their order, cursor shape names, which cells are listed, the JSON object, only a grid that shows a listed token is reported).

| case | platforms | what a defect looks like | cost (estimate, not measured) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grid_snapshot_render` (T34) | Wayland, X11, macOS, Windows Git Bash pane (the PowerShell pane SKIPs: one pane is enough, the scripts are printed with `cat` and stepped with bash `read`). Both session modes. | Normal screen: a cell of the fixed script is not what the script asked for, each difference named with its class: `colour16` (SGR 31, 92, 44, 103), `colour256` (38;5;196, 48;5;21), `truecolor` (38;2;255;136;0, 48;2;0;51;102), `attribute` (1, 2, 3, 4, 4:2, 9, 7, 8, and 1;4;31 together), `reset` (the plain space after every `ESC[0m` must paint nothing), `wide` (two CJK cells, each with its spacer), `combining` (`e` + U+0301 is one cell), `emoji` (U+1F600 takes two columns), `box` (six box-drawing cells). Alternate screen: the token is not magenta at row 2 column 4, the wide cell or the box corners are elsewhere, the cursor is not a bar at (6, 9), or after Return not an underline at (1, 2) with `step2` on row 8; the command list does not finish after the second Return (the keys did not reach `read`). No snapshot file at all fails (a build without the hook). | about 1 minute per mode |
| `freeze_and_wake` (T36) | Wayland, X11, macOS; the fake-model pass (agent mode). Windows SKIPs with `NEEDS:` (no suspend / resume in `winapi.py`). | See below. | about 4 minutes (60 s frozen, a 120 s scripted reply) |
| `lab_freeze_and_wake.*` (T36) | the ssh lab (Linux), one arm: `lab_freeze_and_wake.bash.lan.nohelper`, agent mode. | The same body with the lab's link to the session stalled for `APPCI_FW_STALL_S` (90 s) from just before the freeze. | about 5 minutes |

**`freeze_and_wake` in order.** Tab 1 is the typing tab. A new tab starts a scripted reply (`Please stream long reply <TAG> chunks N gap 100`, sized to last the freeze plus 60 s); another new tab runs `ssh <host>` and proves the host's shell with one line. Back in tab 1 the app is stopped with SIGSTOP for `APPCI_FW_FREEZE_S` (60 s) and continued with SIGCONT (the `finally` continues it whatever fails). Controls first: the typing tab takes a line before anything is opened, and the host takes a line before the freeze; either failing ends the case as failed. The freeze itself is proven: the OS reports the process stopped at both ends (`/proc/<pid>/stat` on Linux, `ps -o state=` on macOS) and the app's log did not grow in between; a state that cannot be read is UNVERIFIABLE. Then:
- **Keys typed while frozen.** Five seconds into the freeze one `echo <held> >> file` line is typed into the frozen window. It must not take effect before the wake. After the wake the file must gain exactly `[held, after]`, where `after` is a line typed right after SIGCONT; `[after]` alone means the display system did not hold the keys (NO-REFERENCE for that half, not a failure). A partial, merged, repeated or reordered line fails, and `rec.log` must hold exactly the same lines.
- **Local typing at once.** The effect of the line typed right after SIGCONT is there within `APPCI_FW_WAKE_S` (5 s; the metric `wake.wake_to_effect_s` is the measured time, which includes typing the line).
- **The ssh tab** (last tab key). One line is typed. `alive`: the host's file gains exactly it. `dropped`: it ran in the local shell exactly AND the app logged `hop=ssh_pty_owner ssh=false` since the freeze began. Neither file gaining it, or a local run without that hop, fails.
- **The agent tab** (previous-tab key from the last tab). After the reply's stream ends or breaks, `Please follow up check <TAG>` is typed. No follow-up reaching the model fails (the turn neither ended nor errored). A chunk in the conversation twice, a marker of another conversation, or a token typed in another tab fails. An incomplete reply that takes the follow-up is an errored turn: allowed, and the note says so with the chunk counts.
- **Nothing in the wrong place.** The typing tab's tokens are not in the host's file, the host's `rec.log` or any model request; the ssh tab's tokens are not in the typing tab's file or any model request; exactly one request carried the stream prompt.

Self-tests (`script/realapp/appci/selftest_w4core.py`, run by `run.py --self-test` and `selftest.py`): `w4core_grid_scripts_and_judge` (the expectation tables against an independent reading of the script bytes; a lost colour, an attribute that outlives its reset, a wide cell without its spacer, a dropped combining mark, a narrow emoji, a wrong or missing cursor each make exactly the difference the case reports; half-written or other-version snapshot files are not read), `w4core_grid_hook_two_sides_agree` (the variable, the request file name, the format version, the JSON keys and the attribute letters against `appci_grid.rs`; `render_grid` calls the hook; the three launchers set the directory), `w4core_freeze_pure_parts` (the process state, the freeze proof, the typing-tab, ssh-tab and agent-turn judges with the input each defect would produce), `w4core_registry_and_docs`.
Run: `python3 script/realapp/appci/run.py --cases grid_snapshot_render,freeze_and_wake` (the second needs `APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1` outside the fix tier); the lab arm: `--cases 'lab_freeze_and_wake.*'` in the lab job.
What is not judged, and why: the cursor on the normal screen (a block's cursor is drawn only while the block is latched as interactive; under ConPTY nothing latches it, so the alternate screen carries the cursor checks on every platform). On Windows the console layer (ConPTY) re-encodes what the program printed before the app sees it; a difference there names its class, which is where to start a TEST-or-APP verdict.
## Round 15: tier reach (design `docs/design/r15-tiers.md`; #2056 #2057 #2058 #2063 #2064; harness and CI only; nothing compiled, no pipeline played when written)
Source: `docs/design/r14-test-gaps.md` 5.1 (G1, G2, G6, G7) and 7.0 a to f. Worked, unproven: only the self-tests ran.
**The fix tier's daily-use slice (#2057).** Thirteen old full-tier cases are in `PROVING` and so in every fix-tier run until the owner graduates them:
`session_restore`, `crash_kill9_restore`, `ui_resize_typing`, `ui_split_panes`, `ui_ctrl_r`, `ui_ghost_accept`, `ui_tab_menu`, `big_paste`,
`paste_multiline_prompt`, `ssh_password_prompt`, `remote_session_legacy`, `alt_screen_programs`, `agent_approval`. No case was changed. None needs the
scripted model: `agent_approval` runs in the ordinary agent pass with the configured provider and skips with its reason without one. Windows: each keeps its
`winmap` entry (`crash_kill9_restore`, `paste_multiline_prompt` both panes; `ui_resize_typing`, `ui_split_panes` SKIP with the missing capability; the rest
Git Bash only). Cost: not measured; `session_restore` and `crash_kill9_restore` relaunch the app, `alt_screen_programs` and `remote_session_legacy` are the
long ones. The first fix-tier run records it.
**X11 in the fix tier, both modes (#2058).** `app-test-linux-x11` no longer leaves with exit 77 when `APPCI_TIER=smoke`; it runs `SMOKE + PROVING` (and the
`agent@fake` pass) under Xvfb like the Wayland job does under sway. `ci_seq.py` passes `APPCI_MODES=terminal,agent`. Agent mode had never run on X11.
**One app job at a time on the box, in a fixed order.** `ci_seq.box_app_sequence(tier)` is the list and the driver plays each entry only after the one
before it has ended: `app-test-linux-wayland`, `app-test-linux-x11`, the lab job, and in candidate / release `app-test-replay-linux`. All of it after the
box's unit suites (and in candidate / release after `integration-linux`, `-pwsh` and `usage-test-linux`). The resource group `little-thing-gui` only kept
two app jobs from overlapping; it did not order them. A reused Linux build follows the same order with the `-reuse` jobs and, new, also waits for the unit suites.
**The lab in the candidate and release tiers (#2063).**
| machine | job | play-time variables | when |
| box | `sshlab-image` | none | at the start (a no-op when the image tag exists); every lab job waits for it |
| box | `lab-helper` | none | right after `check-linux`, before the builds and unit suites |
| box | `app-test-lab-linux` | `APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1`, `APPCI_LAB_MATRIX` = `ci_seq.LAB_CANDIDATE_MATRIX` | after wayland and x11 |
| box | `app-test-replay-linux` | the job's own (`lab_replay*`, 15 minutes per mode) | last on the box, before the release tier's heavy suites |
| Mac | `app-test-lab-macos` | `APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1`, `APPCI_LAB_MATRIX=quick` | after `app-test-macos`, before the Mac's heavy suites |
| Windows | `app-test-lab-windows` | the same | after `app-test-windows`; the lab cases run in the Git Bash pane (`winmap.lab_skip_reason`) |
`LAB_CANDIDATE_MATRIX` is `shells=bash,zsh,fish,nu;lat=lan,150;helper=nohelper,helper,upload,upgrade,never;faults=1;scenarios=1`: 372 arms, 509 rows, at
least one arm of every lab family (46 with the replay). The quick matrix reaches 38 of them: `helper_install`, `helper_policy`, `helper_digest_mismatch`,

## Round 15 wave 4: the pointer and the window size on Windows, T31 and T33 (#2060; design `docs/design/r15-w4win.md`; source `docs/design/r14-test-gaps.md` 7.1; nothing run on Windows when written)
The Windows backend had no pointer, no window resize and no way to rewrite the settings file the running app reads, so eight cases skipped there
by `winmap.NOT_WINDOWS`. All three capabilities now exist and the eight cases run in the **Git Bash pane** (each reads `rec.log` or uses bash
lines; the PowerShell pane SKIPs with that reason). No app code changed.
| capability | where | how it proves itself |
|---|---|---|
| pointer (T31) | `winapi.Pointer`, `backend.WindowsBackend.ptr_move / ptr_button / ptr_wheel / mod_hold`, `cases_ui.Mouse` | `SendInput` with ABSOLUTE positions on the virtual desktop (`winapi.mouse_norm`). Every move is read back with `GetCursorPos` (1 px, waited for at most 1 s); a press is refused unless the top-level window under the pointer belongs to the Phosphor pid, and always while the reference console is the target. Before a case uses it, `cases_ui.mouse_or_skip` hovers the middle of the app window (`ptr_ready`). |
| positions without OCR (T31) | `cases_ui._hook_word`, `find_token`, `words`, `wl_check` | The app's find hook (#1789): `appci_find token= x0= y0= x1= y1=` in device pixels of the window's client area, plus `ClientToScreen` of the app window. The VM has no OCR engine, so nothing else is tried. |
| window size (T33) | `winapi.set_window_rect`, `backend.WindowsBackend.window_save / window_resize / window_restore`, `cases_ui.resize_to`, `cases_window_use.Window` | `SetWindowPos`, posted (`SWP_ASYNCWINDOWPOS`: a busy app cannot hang the harness), no z-order change, no activation; the size is read back with `GetWindowRect` (`winapi.resize_verdict`: Windows clamps a size to the desktop, so a changed size is the proof, an unchanged one is the error). A maximised window is restored first and maximised again at the end. |
| the settings file the app reads (T33) | `cases_ui.settings_path` | On Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\phosphor\Phosphor\config\settings.toml` (`WindowsApp.config`). It used to return the profile's source file there, which the running app never reads. `WindowsApp.start()` installs the profile's file on every start, so a case's rewrite cannot outlive a relaunch. |
**What a row can say, and what it means.**
- `noref` with `TEST CAPABILITY MISSING ... NEEDS:`: the pointer did not arrive (the cursor is not where `SendInput` was told to put it) or the
  window did not take a size. `NEEDS:` names the machine condition: the runner on the unlocked, connected interactive console session, the app
  window on screen and not covered. This is never a skip (it would read as "does not apply") and never a pass.
- `noref` with `UNVERIFIABLE ... the app logged no usable appci_find line`: the word was not located. The hook attaches a hit when text is laid
  out, so a token must be registered before it is drawn; the cases do that. A build without the hook, or `RUST_LOG` without
  `warpui::appci_find=info` (`app.WINDOWS_RUST_LOG` has it), gives the same row.
- `noref` in `resize_reflow_output` with `NEEDS: a desktop of at least WxH`: the VM's desktop is smaller than the sizes the case cycles through
  (`cases_window_use.desktop_too_small`); two sizes clamped to the desktop would be the same size.
- `fail` with `harness exception: PointerError(...)`: a point the app reported is off the screen (the window is partly outside the desktop), or
  the pointer stopped arriving in the middle of a case. Read the text: it is a harness or machine condition, not the app ignoring a click.
- Any other `fail` is judged exactly as on Linux: the clipboard, the effect file and `rec.log`.
| case | Windows specifics | est. minutes, both modes (not measured) |
|---|---|---|
| `ui_mouse_select_copy` | Full tier elsewhere; on Windows also in the fix tier through `winmap.PROVING_WINDOWS`. | 1 |
| `ui_copy_wrapped_drag` | As on Linux; both words from the hook. | 1 |
| `ui_vertical_tabs_panel_click` | The panel rows come from the hook (`cases_wrap_vtabs.hook_panel_rows`): of a tab token's sightings since the tabs were opened, the newest in its leftmost column is the panel's (the same token is drawn further right in the tab's pane). Fewer than two rows located is UNVERIFIABLE. A wrong pick cannot pass: the oracle is the clicked tab's own `pwd -W`. | 2 |
| `selection_modes` | Shift is held with the backend's own key-down / key-up (`cases_pointer.Held`), released whatever the body raises. | 2 |
| `context_menu_actions` | Unchanged: it never used OCR. The window origin is `ClientToScreen`. | 1.5 |
| `ui_resize_typing` | Full tier elsewhere; on Windows also in the fix tier through `winmap.PROVING_WINDOWS`. The window gets its place, size and maximised state back. | 1.5 |
| `resize_reflow_output` | The stream is 300 lines (`cases_window_use.WIN_RR_LINES`, `APPCI_RR_LINES` overrides): each `sleep` of the bash loop is a process start in an msys shell. The SIGWINCH trap, `stty size` and vim are the Git Bash pane's. | 2.5 |
| `ui_vertical_tabs_many` | The panel is switched on by writing the file the app reads; next / previous tab are `ctrl+Next` / `ctrl+Prior`, which the Windows key table now knows (`ctrl-pagedown` / `ctrl-pageup` in `workspace/mod.rs`). | 3 |
**`winmap.PROVING_WINDOWS`.** `ui_mouse_select_copy` and `ui_resize_typing` are older full-tier cases, so `cases.PROVING` is the wrong place for
them (it would put them in the Linux and macOS fix tier). Their Windows arm is new, so `winmap.tier_plan` adds this tuple to every Windows
fix-tier pass. A case leaves it when the owner says so, like `PROVING`. It adds about 2.5 minutes to a Git Bash pass.
**Not ported, with the reason in `winmap.NOT_WINDOWS`** (the reasons no longer say "no pointer"): `tab_pointer_use` (POSIX shell-pid probe),
`link_and_path_click` (recording `xdg-open`, strace), `wheel_scroll` (OCR scroll position, termios), `alt_screen_mouse_reporting` (termios),
`pane_resize_maximize` (POSIX probe), `ui_right_click_paste` (superseded on Windows by `context_menu_actions`), `minimize_fullscreen` (no
minimise / fullscreen call: `cases_window_use.WIN_STATE_WHY`), `ui_settings_live` and `settings_ui_toggle_persists` (not reviewed for Windows).
`focus_cycle` (T29) is unchanged: its focus-reporting half stays a note on ConPTY.
**Self-tests** (`script/realapp/appci/selftest_w4win.py`, run by `run.py --self-test`): `w4win_mouse_events_pure_parts` (structure layout, the
pixel an absolute move names on five desktops, buttons, wheel sign), `w4win_pointer_delivery_is_proven` (a move not applied raises with the
`NEEDS:` text; a late one is waited for), `w4win_window_helpers_and_resize_verdict`, `w4win_backend_pointer_guards` (no press over another
process's window or while the reference console is the target; a release always goes out), `w4win_backend_window_size` (clamped is a change,
unchanged is an error, maximised is restored and put back), `w4win_mouse_class_drives_the_windows_backend` (a drag releases the button when a
move raises), `w4win_positions_come_from_the_hook_only` (no tool is run for a position on Windows; a missing line is UNVERIFIABLE; an
undelivered pointer is `noref`), `w4win_panel_rows_from_the_hook`, `w4win_settings_file_the_app_reads`, `w4win_registry_winmap_and_docs`.
After every case `run.post_case_invariants` asks the backend to release what a case left down (`WindowsBackend.release_held`: mouse buttons,
held modifiers); anything it had to release is a `harness_state_reset_after_<case>` row.
**What the first Windows run must show.** `ptr move` / `ptr button` lines in `inject.log`; `appci_find` lines for the printed tokens, the menu
entries and the panel rows; whether the app reloads the settings file live on Windows (`vtabs_on_screen_diff`); whether an msys bash under

is known; a failure there needs a TEST-vs-APP verdict from the log before anything is called an app defect). Run:
by hand on the VM as in 2.8, `run.py --run <dir> --bin <exe> --backend windows --platform windows --cases ui_mouse_select_copy,ui_copy_wrapped_drag,ui_vertical_tabs_panel_click,selection_modes,context_menu_actions,ui_resize_typing,resize_reflow_output,ui_vertical_tabs_many`.
