Four items. Each changes or adds cases in `cases.PROVING` only; nothing graduates.
| case | what changed | runs where | oracle | control (what a wrong result trips) | min (estimate) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sudo_su_real_shell` (T47) | the sudo arm runs as the test user named by `APPCI_SUDO_USER` (else root through `sudo -n true`); su also through passwordless root sudo; arms the machine cannot run are `NOT RUN:` notes, no longer NOREF | Linux, macOS, terminal mode | `id -u` typed into the inner shell is the target's uid; exact lines; `exit`; the pane's own uid again | the CI user's uid in the file = sudo never started a shell | 1 |
| `subshell_ready_relay_shape` (T47) | same target; the effect file is an absolute path both users can write (it was `~/w/...`, the target's home wherever sudo resets HOME) | Linux, macOS, both modes | setup written behind sudo on the judge's `kind=Relay` or `leader=Shell`; the line ran once as the target uid; root shell proven by PID after `exit` | the uid, and the PID proof | 1 |
| `subshell_ready_docker_t_without_i` (T47) | the skip names which of three things is missing | Linux, macOS, both modes | as written | as written | 1 |
| `gpu_real_render` (T48, NEW) | the app on the machine's render node against a forced software launch | Linux, both modes | adapter of each launch from the app log; the GPU launch's own share of a frame p50 <= 4 ms and p95 <= 16 ms; the two pictures differ in <= 2 % of the pixels | the cleared pane against the drawn pattern must differ by 5x the tolerance; the software launch must really be software | 3 |
| `soak` (T49) | process sampling without `/proc`; macOS closes its tab without a close key; Windows lines, flood and paths | macOS and Windows in the fix tier (10 min), every platform in the full tier (60 min) | memory growth rule, idle CPU, exact commands, as on Linux | the sampler's first reading must be this app (main pid among the pids, >= 20 MB); more than 3 minutes without a reading fails | 13 per pass |
| `agent_code_recycle` (#2071) | the answer is `fake_model.snippet_reply`; agent mode; a letters-only token | every platform, the `agent@fake` pass | recycle line, rebuild line, snippets stable across the rebuild, copy exact | the prompt must have reached the model (`fake.fresh`) and the snippets must be on screen before anything is judged | 3 |
**T47, the privilege boundary (`appci/priv_boundary.py`).** The three cases SKIPPED on every machine: they asked for passwordless root sudo of the CI user. `priv_boundary.sudo_target()` now finds who the pane may become with no password: the user named by `APPCI_SUDO_USER` (environment, or the machine-local `~/.config/phosphor-ci/ci.env`) when `sudo -n -u <user> true` succeeds, else root when `sudo -n true` succeeds. A target with the CI user's own uid is refused (no boundary). The inner shell writes its effect file into a directory both users can reach (`shared_dir`: the work dir for root; for another user a 0777 directory inside it when every parent lets others through, else one under `/var/tmp`, removed afterwards). Typed lines: `sudo -n -u <user> env -i HOME=<home> PATH="$PATH" bash --noprofile --norc -i` (the sudo arm), `sudo -s` for root or `sudo -n -H -u <user> -s` for a test user (the relay case; the self-test checks both against the app's built-in sudo subshell regex in `warpify/settings.rs`, so the banner is offered).
NEEDS: on a machine with neither, the skip carries the exact change (the harness never edits sudoers, adds a user, pulls an image or starts a daemon):
- sudo, the smaller way: `sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash appci-priv` (macOS: `sudo sysadminctl -addUser appci-priv -shell /bin/bash`); a file `/etc/sudoers.d/appci-priv`, mode 0440, checked with `visudo -cf`, holding `<ci-user> ALL=(appci-priv) NOPASSWD: ALL` and `Defaults:<ci-user> use_pty`; and `APPCI_SUDO_USER=appci-priv` in the CI user's `~/.config/phosphor-ci/ci.env`. The CI user can then become only that user, never root. The other way: `<ci-user> ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL`.
- su: the runner is root, or passwordless ROOT sudo (then `sudo -n su -s /bin/bash nobody`; macOS needs `APPCI_SU_USER=<user with a login shell>`, its `su` has no `-s`). A test user alone cannot run su: `NOT RUN:` with that reason.
- ksu: never run by the harness (the realm and the principal are the owner's site).
- docker: three separate reasons, each with its change: docker not installed; the daemon not usable by the CI user (`sudo usermod -aG docker <ci-user>`, restart the runner service); the `alpine` image absent (`docker pull alpine` once by hand).
Expectation change, stated because it loosens a row: `sudo_su_real_shell` used to be NOREF whenever any arm could not run. ksu can never run, so no machine could give a PASS. The row is now judged on the arms that ran (metrics `boundaries_run`, `boundaries_not_run`); the unrun arms are `NOT RUN:` notes.
**T48, `gpu_real_render` (`appci/cases_r15_w5c.py`).** Two launches on the same profile: the default one, and one with `WGPU_BACKEND=gl LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` (Mesa's software rasteriser; the app reads `WGPU_BACKEND` through `wgpu::Backends::from_env`). Each draws the same screen (`gpu_pattern.sh`: 24 coloured rows, then `seq 1 4000`, then the rows again on a cleared pane). Read from the app log: `Surface configured: backend= adapter="" present_mode= frame_latency= alpha_mode= software_renderer=` (which adapter drew; the wording is pinned by the unit test `surface_config_summary_names_the_adapter_and_flags_a_software_renderer` in `crates/warpui/src/rendering/wgpu/resources_tests.rs`), the adapter list the app logs while choosing, and `hop=frame_drawn total_ms= acquire_ms= present_ms=`. The judged frame figure is the app's own share, total less the swapchain wait and less the present call. Knobs: `APPCI_GPU_FRAME_P50_MS` (4), `APPCI_GPU_FRAME_P95_MS` (16), `APPCI_GPU_SHOT_DIFF` (0.02). Needs Pillow.
Outcomes that are not a verdict, each stated on the row:
- no `/dev/dri/renderD*`: SKIP, NEEDS: a machine with a GPU render node;
- a node the CI user cannot open: SKIP, NEEDS: the CI user in the `render` and `video` groups;
- a node, but the session offers no hardware adapter the app can present to (Xvfb has no DRI3): SKIP, NEEDS: the headless-sway job with `WLR_RENDERER=gles2`, and Mesa's driver packages;
- a presentable hardware adapter listed and a software one used: FAIL;
- fewer than 30 frames, no `Surface configured:` line, a software launch that did not come up or did not take the software rasteriser, a control pair that does not differ: NOREF with the reason;
- "a lost device recovers" (the spec's third oracle; #2091): built in round 17 as its own case, `gpu_lost_device_recovers` (see "Round 17 misc"); every `gpu_real_render` row says so. It was `NOT RUN:` on every row before. NEEDS: nothing on the machine (the app's test hook reports the loss; the kernel's reset switches need root and are not used).
**T49, the soak on macOS and Windows (`appci/procsample.py`).** `procsample.sample(ctx)` returns the app's pids, memory in KiB and CPU seconds: `/proc` on Linux (the same figures as before), `ps -axo pid=,rss=,time=,command=` filtered to the job's private bundle on macOS (the main process and its terminal-server helper; before, one process), and on Windows the app's Win32 job for the exact pids plus `GetProcessTimes` / `GetProcessMemoryInfo` for those running the app's exe (the calls `Get-Process` wraps; without a job, one `Get-Process` by the exe path). The Windows memory figure is private bytes (#1340: the working set is trimmed and shared).
- Tiers: `APPCI_SOAK_MIN` wins; else 10 minutes in the fix tier and 60 elsewhere (`cases_robust.soak_minutes`, also the case's time limit in `run.py`). In the fix tier the soak runs on macOS (both modes) and on Windows in two of the four passes (terminal in the PowerShell pane, agent in the Git Bash pane: each mode and each pane once); the other two Windows passes and Linux SKIP with that reason. The full tier is unchanged on Linux and soaks every pass on macOS and Windows.
- A run under 18 minutes takes a second memory sample at each minute boundary, so the growth rule (3 windows of 5 after a warm-up of 3) still gives a verdict in 10 minutes. The thresholds are the 60-minute ones.
- macOS has no close chord the backend may send. The throw-away tab's shell writes its pid, Ctrl-D ends it, and the pid going away is the proof; if it stays, the command palette's `Close Current Session` is tried; if it still stays the soak fails and stops, NEEDS: a close chord (T32, `APPCI_KEY_CLOSE`), because tabs piling up would read as memory growth. With `APPCI_KEY_CLOSE` set the key is used, as on Linux and Windows.
- `script/ci/collect_results.py` `soak_verdict` (the soak column of `test-results/INDEX.md` and the README line) lists every platform with a soak row and its worst status; it used to stop at the first row found, which a Linux fix-tier skip would now be.
- Windows: `Add-Content` lines in the PowerShell pane, `1..300000` for the flood, an absolute path for the token typed in the new tab (a new tab does not start in the work dir), a fixed 3 s settle where the pane has no prompt log, 90 s for the sentinel behind the flood. `winmap.py`: `soak` moved from `NOT_WINDOWS` to `BOTH`.
**#2071, `agent_code_recycle`.** F10: SKIP, NOREF or fail on every platform, on a real model's wording. The fake model has a new trigger, "Please write code snippets `<TOK>` count `<N>`", answered with N fenced bash blocks `echo RCY<TOK>_NN` (`fake_model.snippet_reply`). The case is agent-only and in `PROVING_FAKE` (the fix tier's `agent@fake` pass); with any other provider it SKIPS with NEEDS:. No skip is left that depends on what a model wrote: a prompt that did not reach the model, or an answer that is not on screen, is a failure. A second cause of the old skips, found while reading: the token was `T12_ABCD` and the screen text is searched after everything but letters and digits is removed, so with an OCR engine the snippets were never "seen". The token is now four letters.
Self-tests (`script/realapp/appci/selftest_r15_w5c.py`, run by `run.py --self-test`): `w5c_cases_registered_proving_and_classified`, `w5c_recycle_answer_is_scripted_and_the_token_is_readable`, `w5c_sudo_target_and_needs_text`, `w5c_shared_dir_and_typed_commands`, `w5c_process_sampling_parsers`, `w5c_soak_tier_rules_and_lines`, `w5c_gpu_adapter_and_frame_judges`, `w5c_gpu_pattern_is_the_same_every_time`.
Run: `python3 script/realapp/appci/run.py --cases sudo_su_real_shell,subshell_ready_relay_shape,subshell_ready_docker_t_without_i,gpu_real_render,soak,agent_code_recycle` (`APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1` for the last; `APPCI_SOAK_MIN=10` for a short soak outside the fix tier).
## Round 15 wave 4, desktop integration: scale, notifications, drag and drop, IME (design `docs/design/r15-w4desk.md`; `r14-test-gaps.md` T35 / T37 / T38 / T39; #2075 #2078 #2085; nothing compiled, no app run when written)
Five cases in `script/realapp/appci/cases_desk.py`, all in `cases.PROVING` (fix tier until the owner graduates them); `desktop_notification_agent_question` is also in `PROVING_FAKE`. Minutes are estimates per platform pass, both modes together; none is measured.
| case | runs on | min | Windows (`winmap`) | SKIPs with |
| `scale_matrix` | Wayland, X11 | 6 | `NOT_WINDOWS` | Windows: `NEEDS:` a settable VM display scale and pointer synthesis (T31). macOS: `NEEDS:` another display mode and a pointer tool. X11 without `xrdb`: `NEEDS:` package x11-xserver-utils. xwayland pass: judged in the other two |
| `desktop_notification` | Wayland, X11, Windows (both panes); macOS behind `APPCI_MAC_NOTIFY_OK=1` | 2.5 | `BOTH` | macOS: `NEEDS:` the owner answers the notification permission prompt once, then sets the variable. No reference terminal: the reason |
| `desktop_notification_agent_question` | the `agent@fake` pass of the same platforms | 2 | `BOTH` | as above; no fake model |
| `drag_drop_file` | X11, Wayland | 1.5 | `NOT_WINDOWS` | no drag source: `NEEDS:` packages python3-gi + gir1.2-gtk-3.0, or dragon-drop. Windows: `NEEDS:` an OLE drag source and pointer synthesis. macOS: `NEEDS:` a pasteboard drag source and a pointer tool |
| `ime_compose` | Wayland, X11, Windows Git Bash pane | 3 | `GITBASH_ONLY` | Linux: `NEEDS:` packages fcitx5 + fcitx5-chinese-addons (or ibus + ibus-libpinyin, X11 only). Windows: `NEEDS:` Chinese (Simplified, China) with Microsoft Pinyin in the runner user's language list. macOS: `NEEDS:` the owner's input sources; the arm is `intl_ime_pinyin` / `intl_ime_japanese` |
**The session hook (`app.py`).** The Linux launcher's `INNER` script sources the file named by `APPCI_SESSION_PRE` inside the app's private D-Bus session, just before it publishes the app's pid and starts the app. A case writes the lines to `<run>/desk/<name>_pre.sh`, sets `App.extra_env["APPCI_SESSION_PRE"]`, relaunches (`cases_robust.start_app`) and removes the variable in its `finally`, then relaunches again. Whatever the lines start stays in the launcher's process group, which is all `App.stop()` signals; nothing may daemonize. Unset (every other case) the line does nothing.
**The recording notification service (`notify_recorder.py`).** No package: the D-Bus wire protocol in plain Python (unix socket, EXTERNAL auth, `Hello`, `RequestName` with replace-existing and do-not-queue). `serve --log F --ready R` owns `org.freedesktop.Notifications`, answers `Notify` with an id, writes one JSON line per notification (`t`, `id`, `app`, `summary`, `body`, `actions`, `timeout`, `sender`) and two seconds later emits `NotificationClosed(id, 1)`. `R` gets `{"ok": true, "address": ...}`, or `{"ok": false, "why": ...}` when another connection keeps the name. `send --address A SUMMARY BODY` is the harness's control. The log holds the test's own command lines; it stays under `<run>/desk/`.
**The drag source (`dragsrc.py`).** A GTK 3 window (python3-gi) whose whole area starts a `text/uri-list` drag of the paths on its command line; X11 (override-redirect, placed with `--at`) and Wayland (`app_id` `appci_dragsrc`; the case adds `no_focus` and `for_window ... floating enable` rules to sway first). `--ready F` gets the window line, then one line per drag event (`begin`, `data`, `end`, `failed`). The case pins `GDK_BACKEND` to the app's display system so the source cannot open any other display. `dragsrc.py --probe` says whether GTK loads. `dragon-drop` is used when GTK does not load.
**The app's trace line.** `input_order hop=desktop_notification title_chars=<n> body_chars=<n> t=...` (`crates/warpui_core/src/input_order.rs` `log_desktop_notification`, called from `AppContext::send_desktop_notification`): one line per desktop notification handed to the OS, counts only, never the text. Unit test `desktop_notification_lines_carry_counts_and_no_text` pins the format the harness parses (`cases_desk.NOTIFY_HOP_RE`).
What each case judges:
- `scale_matrix` (G9, H5; #2078). Knob: sway `output <name> scale <s>` on Wayland, the `Xft.dpi` X resource (`xrdb`) on X11. For 1.25, 1.5 and 2 the window gets the logical size of the output at that scale, first at scale 1 (**the control**), then at the scale. `stty size` at the scale must equal the app's own `hop=grid_resize` and the control within 8 % or two cells (cell sizes snap to device pixels); a grid laid out in device pixels differs by the factor, one that ignored the scale by its inverse. A dimension too small to tell is UNVERIFIABLE. Then six words are printed and the fifth is double-clicked at the position the app's `appci_find` line gives (device pixels, mapped through the output's scale): the clipboard, a sentinel before, must hold exactly that word. A typed burst is exact. Wayland only: `swaymsg create_output`, the new output gets scale 2, the window moves there (checked from the sway tree) and both oracles run again; no second output is UNVERIFIABLE. The scale, the floating state, the second output and the X resources are put back, and `stty size` must return to its value before the case.
- `desktop_notification` (H7). The profile's settings get `[notifications.preferences]` `mode = "enabled"`, `long_running_threshold = 3` (a settings file that writes the table inline is a SKIP: the owner's file is not rewritten); the app is relaunched; both are put back at the end. Linux: the recording service must own the name and record a control notification sent by the harness, else UNVERIFIABLE. Arms: a 12 s command ends while Phosphor has the focus: **none**. The same command ends while the reference terminal has the focus (`cases.ref_terminal`, as `focus_cycle`): **exactly one**, and on Linux its text names the command's token. A 2 s command ends unfocused: **none** (not played on Windows, where opening the reference takes longer than the command). On Linux the service's count and the app's hop count must both match; elsewhere the hop judges. A focus that left too late is UNVERIFIABLE.
- `desktop_notification_agent_question`. The scripted model's `ask_slow` fault delays a question; the focus goes to the reference terminal first; no notification before the card; when the card is answerable **exactly one**; the focus returns, Enter answers, the turn ends `success`, and the total is still one.
- `drag_drop_file` (F2, H8). `ls -d ` is typed, the pointer is parked on the middle of the window (the app drops at its last pointer position and sees no motion during the drag), the source starts, the pointer presses on it, moves in steps, dwells and releases, then ` > file` + Enter is typed. The shell must have received one line whose words (`shlex`) are `ls -d`, the path as ONE argument, `>`, the file; the file must hold the path. A source that reported no `begin` is UNVERIFIABLE (the harness never offered the file); `begin` without `data` is a failure (the app did not take it). **Wayland (#2085, round 15 `r15-wldnd`):** the native Wayland backend now has a drop target (below), so the Wayland pass is judged like X11 and no longer announced as a failure; with the GTK source it has one check more: the source must not report `failed` (the app finished the offer; a `failed` after `data` means the data was taken and the offer was then destroyed without `wl_data_offer.finish`). The failure texts name the issue and the kill switch. `ui_drag_drop_file` (always SKIP) is unchanged and stays registered.
- `ime_compose` (F6, H9; the test #1892 did not have). The input method runs inside the app's session (Linux: fcitx5 or ibus through the session hook, selected with `fcitx5-remote -s` / `ibus engine` and read back; Windows: `WM_INPUTLANGCHANGEREQUEST` to the Phosphor window, read back with `GetKeyboardLayout`, the user's language list snapshotted first as `intl_altgr_*` does). A selection that cannot be read back is UNVERIFIABLE. Then `cases_caseintl.compose_raw` (not on Windows: the reader needs termios): `nihao` typed, nothing reaches the raw reader, Space commits, the reader gets exactly the UTF-8 bytes of the first candidate; and `compose_editor` for `nihao` and `zhongwen`: nothing runs while composing, the shell receives exactly `echo <text> >> file`.
Self-tests (`script/realapp/appci/selftest_desk.py`, run by `run.py --self-test` and `selftest.py`): `desk_cases_registry_r15_w4` (registration, tiers, the separate-statement additions, Windows classes, this section, the launcher hook and `bash -n` of the launcher), `desk_cases_skip_with_the_exact_need`, `notify_recorder_wire_roundtrip`, `notify_recorder_service_records_each_notify_once`, `notify_recorder_serves_a_bus_end_to_end` (a stand-in bus on a unix socket, including a bus where another daemon keeps the name), `notification_verdicts_and_settings` (also pins the hop format against the Rust source), `away_gives_and_takes_the_focus`, `scale_grid_verdict_trips_on_a_wrong_scale`, `scale_outputs_and_pointer_mapping`, `drag_source_and_drop_verdict`, `ime_plan_and_launcher_lines`.
Run: `python3 script/realapp/appci/run.py --cases scale_matrix,desktop_notification,drag_drop_file,ime_compose` (and `desktop_notification_agent_question` with `APPCI_FAKE_MODEL=1`).

### Wayland drop target (#2085, `docs/design/r15-wldnd.md`; nothing compiled, no app run when written)
The vendored winit's Wayland backend had no `wl_data_device` code, so a file dragged onto the window on native Wayland was never offered to the app. It now has one (`lib/winit/src/platform_impl/linux/wayland/dnd/`, `lib/winit/CHANGES-PHOSPHOR.md`): a data device per seat, a drag offering `text/uri-list` is accepted with the copy action, the data is read through a pipe on the event loop, and `HoveredFile` / `HoveredFileCancelled` / `DroppedFile` are emitted as on X11, with one `CursorMoved` at the drop position before the `DroppedFile` events (the app drops at its last pointer position, and no pointer event reaches a window during a drag). The app side is unchanged. Kill switch: `PHOSPHOR_WAYLAND_DND=0` (no data device; a Wayland drop does nothing, as before).
- **Unit tests** (`lib/winit/src/platform_impl/linux/wayland/dnd/logic.rs`, 20 tests). `lib/winit` is its own workspace and no CI job runs its tests, so the file (it uses only `std`) is also compiled into `warpui`'s tests by `#[path]` from `crates/warpui/src/windowing/winit/linux/mod.rs` and runs in the ordinary unit suite as `windowing::winit::linux::wayland_dnd_logic::tests::*`. Keep that file clean under the root `.rustfmt.toml` (`script/check_rustfmt` reaches it through the `#[path]`). Kill switch: `only_zero_is_the_kill_switch`. Mime choice: `uri_list_is_the_only_accepted_mime_type` (text types are refused: a dragged piece of text is not a file), `the_chosen_mime_type_keeps_the_spelling_of_the_source`. Parser (RFC 2483): `one_file_uri_with_crlf`, `a_space_is_percent_twenty_and_stays_one_path`, `unicode_is_decoded_from_percent_bytes_and_taken_raw`, `a_name_that_is_not_utf8_keeps_its_bytes`, `several_files_keep_their_order`, `comments_and_blank_lines_are_skipped`, `a_hash_inside_a_name_is_not_a_comment`, `bare_lf_bare_cr_and_a_trailing_nul_end_a_line`, `other_schemes_are_skipped_and_the_files_beside_them_kept`, `host_forms` (empty, `localhost` in any case, `file:/path`; another host, no path, a relative path are skipped), `percent_edge_cases`. Event order of one drag (`Drag`, no compositor needed): `hover_then_drop_reuses_the_data_read_on_enter`, `a_drop_before_the_data_waits_for_it`, `a_leave_cancels_the_hover_once_and_the_read_still_ends`, `a_drop_with_no_file_asks_once_more_and_then_gives_up`, `a_drag_whose_data_could_not_be_asked_for_on_enter_asks_at_the_drop`, `the_drop_position_comes_before_the_files_and_finish_is_last`.
- **Not unit-tested** (needs a compositor): the SCTK glue in `dnd/mod.rs` (binding, accept / set_actions / receive / finish requests, the calloop pipe source, the window lookup). `drag_drop_file` on the Wayland pass is its test.
- **App case**: `drag_drop_file` (above), Wayland pass. Self-test `drag_source_and_drop_verdict` pins that the case no longer announces a Wayland failure, names the kill switch and has the `failed` check.
- **Log lines** (app log, `log` crate target `winit::platform_impl::linux::wayland::dnd`, info, so they need the harness's `winit=info`; counts only, never a path; `drag_drop_file` reads them with `cases_desk.wl_dnd_hops`, records the metric `wayland_dnd_hops` and puts them in every Wayland failure text): `wayland_dnd hop=off reason=kill_switch|no_data_device_manager`, `hop=enter accepted=true|false`, `hop=leave`, `hop=drop waiting_for_data=..`, `hop=data bytes=N usable=..`, `hop=finish accepted=.. finished=..`; warnings `hop=receive_failed`, `hop=read_failed`, `hop=data_too_large`. A failing Wayland drop is placed by the last of these: no `hop=enter` = the compositor never sent the drag to the app's data device; `accepted=false` = no `text/uri-list` offered or the surface is not a window; `hop=data bytes=0` = the source gave nothing; `finished=false` after `accepted=true` = no copy action was selected.
Machine changes these cases wait for (owner; none made): `xrdb` if the box lacks it; python3-gi + gir1.2-gtk-3.0 or dragon-drop; fcitx5 + fcitx5-chinese-addons; the Chinese (Simplified) language on the Windows VM; the notification permission answer and `APPCI_MAC_NOTIFY_OK=1` on the Mac.

## Round 15 wave 4: the macOS pointer and the app-only chords (#2061; r14-test-gaps T32, gap G5 / H2; design `docs/design/r10-r15-w4mac.md`; nothing compiled or run when written)

Until this round the macOS backend had no pointer, no close key and no quit key, so every pointer case and every clean-quit case SKIPped there. It has all three now. Nothing is installed on the runner: the tools are Swift sources compiled by the job, as `htype2` is. (The runner has no PyObjC: `python3 -c 'import Quartz'` fails for `/usr/bin/python3`, checked read-only on 2026-11-11; `swiftc` 6.3 is there.)

**Tools** (`script/realapp/mac/tools/`, compiled by `mac/ci/app_test.sh` into `$APPCI_MAC_TOOLS`, cached by source hash). A compile error in one of these four does not stop the run: the tool is absent, `mac_pointer_chord_proof` FAILS naming it, and the cases that need it SKIP with `NEEDS: the <tool> tool compiled ...` (`swiftc-<tool>.log` is in the artifacts).

| tool | what it does | its own fence |
|---|---|---|
| `mptr.swift` | pointer by CGEvent: move, 1 to 3 clicks of the left / middle / right button, an 8-step left drag, wheel lines, modifiers held around the ops. `mptr info` prints the main display in points and pixels; `mptr owner X Y` the window a press would hit. Coordinates are points. | every press, drag end and wheel step is refused (exit 4) unless the TOPMOST on-screen window at that point belongs to the PID of the app under test; a point outside the main display is refused before anything is posted; modifiers are always released before exit. The Dock's display-sized see-through backing window is looked through, and only at a point clear of the Dock bar and the menu bar (round 14, #2118, below); a refusal lists every window at the point. It writes the cursor position read back from the window server (`LOC`), which is the proof the events were accepted |
| `appkey.swift` | sends Cmd-W, Cmd-Shift-W or Cmd-Q, and nothing else | refused unless the PID is running, its executable is inside the job's own `Phosphor.app` (`APPCI_MAC_BUNDLE`), and that PID is the frontmost application at that moment. Delivery is `CGEvent.postToPid` (the event goes to that one process whatever happens to the focus); `APPCI_MAC_CHORD_VIA=hid` posts at the HID tap instead, as `htype2` does for every other key |
| `ocrw.swift` | Apple Vision with word boxes (`word<TAB>x<TAB>y<TAB>w<TAB>h`, image pixels), for placing the pointer. `ocr.swift` (lines only) is unchanged | reads a file, posts nothing |
| `openrec.swift` | the recording URL handler of `link_and_path_click` and the query `openrec --handler URL` (which application would open it) | does nothing unless the OWNER installed it (below) |

**The chord rule** (`backend.MacBackend`, section 3.3). `chord_kind(spec)` sorts every key spec into `plain` (htype2 behind the frontmost-app guard, as before), `refused` (never sent by any path: Globe / Fn, every Ctrl+Cmd chord, Cmd with Tab, Space, H, M, and every Cmd-Q / Cmd-W variant not listed next, such as Cmd-Shift-Q = log out) and `app`: exactly Cmd-W (close the tab or pane, `CloseCurrentSession`), Cmd-Shift-W (close the window) and Cmd-Q (quit). An `app` chord is sent by `MacBackend.app_chord()` only: never through htype2, never while a reference terminal is the injection target (`guard_override`), never without the PID the harness started and the job's bundle path, after the frontmost-app guard, through `appkey`, which checks all of it again in its own process. `keys([...])` keeps the order when a list mixes both kinds. The injector accounting sees the chord as one Cmd key-down (`cmd_chords`), like Cmd-V.

`APPCI_KEY_CLOSE` STARTS empty on macOS, so the cases written against "no close key" (soak, the editor cases, `close_extra_tabs`) behave exactly as before until `mac_pointer_chord_proof` has PASSED in the same run; from then on it is `cmd+w` (round 16, owner 2026-11-11: `APPCI_KEY_CLOSE_WHEN_PROVEN`, `cases_robust.proven_close_key`; "Round 16: harness decisions"). The cases enabled here ask `cases_robust.close_key(ctx)` / `quit_key(ctx)`; `stop_for_restart(..., mac_quit=True)` quits by key only where the quit is the subject. Once the chord path has a passing run, `APPCI_KEY_CLOSE="cmd+w"` in `app_test.sh` gives every other case the key.

**The pointer in the cases** (`appci/macptr.py`, `cases_ui.mouse_or_skip(ctx, r, mac=True)`). The cases place the pointer in screenshot pixels on every platform. `macptr.MacMouse` has the methods of `cases_ui.Mouse` and divides by the display scale, measured once from a real screenshot's width over the display's width in points (2 on the Retina runner); a ratio that is not a whole number is an error, not a guess. A case that does not say `mac=True` still SKIPs on macOS (`MAC_NOT_ENABLED`). Positions come from the app's find hook first: `MacApp.start` now sets `PHOSPHOR_APPCI_FIND_FILE` (#2082 for macOS), and the hook's device pixels are added to the window's corner (`winrect` points times the scale; the app's windows have no system title bar, so the window's corner is the content's corner). Else from Apple Vision word boxes (`cases_ui.words`, `need_tesseract(r, ctx)`, `have_word_ocr`). `APPCI_NO_FIND_HOOK=1` switches the hook off, as on Linux. A modifier (`cases_pointer.Held`) is held inside the `mptr` call that clicks; the Linux cases' Ctrl for a link is Cmd on macOS (`app/src/terminal/links.rs`).

**New case `mac_pointer_chord_proof`** (`appci/cases_macptr.py`; `cases.PROVING`, both modes, order 2: right after `mode_proof`, before every case that uses the tools; macOS only, SKIP elsewhere and `winmap.NOT_WINDOWS`). About 1 minute per mode (estimate). It exists so that a red pointer or quit case can be read as the app's fault or the harness's.

| half | what it checks | the control: what a wrong result trips |
|---|---|---|
| tools | `mptr`, `appkey`, `ocrw` are compiled | a missing one fails here |
| pointer | the display scale is a whole number; the cursor is where two different moves put it; the find hook and Apple Vision agree (within 24 px) on where a printed word is; a double click on that word plus the copy key puts exactly it on the clipboard (sentinel first) | a cursor that does not move cannot be in two places; a click on the menu bar, which is not the app's window, must be REFUSED by `mptr`; a hook position a title bar's height off fails with the offset and names `APPCI_NO_FIND_HOOK=1` |
| chords | Cmd-W closes a tab the case opened (the pane that answers a `pwd` probe is the first tab again) | Cmd-H, Cmd-Shift-Q and Ctrl-Cmd-F raise before anything is sent; Cmd-W raises while the reference terminal is the target. A tab that does not close fails and sets `app_chords_proven = False` on the backend: no later case sends an app chord in that run (`cases_robust.mac_chords_why_not`); the cases that need one SKIP naming the failed proof |

Cmd-Q is not sent by the proof (it needs a relaunch); `quit_24_tabs` and `agent_restart_quit_*` are its cases.

**Cases enabled on macOS** (all were already in `cases.PROVING`; none is promoted):

| case | what changed for macOS | what stays different from Linux |
|---|---|---|
| `ui_mouse_select_copy`, `ui_copy_wrapped_drag`, `ui_vertical_tabs_panel_click` | `mouse_or_skip(..., mac=True)`, the Vision word reader | none |
| `selection_modes` | the same; Shift+click through `Held` | none |
| `context_menu_actions`, `tab_pointer_use` | the same, and `window_origin` on macOS (both place the pointer from the find hook only); the middle click is `otherMouseDown` button 2 | none |
| `link_and_path_click` | Cmd+click; no relaunch | the recorder is not a PATH stand-in (the app calls `-[NSWorkspace openURL:]`): the case runs only where `openrec --handler https://...` names `PhosphorAppciOpenRecorder.app`, else it SKIPs with `NEEDS:` and the exact machine change. A path handed to the system is seen as another application coming to the front (noted; that application is left running). `no other outbound connection` is not judged on macOS (no strace; T41) and the case says so in a note |
| `tab_lifecycle_keys` | Cmd-W (`close_key`), undo `cmd+shift+t` | the close question is the app's native alert (same Escape / Return answers; the `Displaying unsaved changes warning for pane` log line is the same) |
| `quit_24_tabs` | `need_quit_app`: Cmd-Q; the orphan check reads cwds with `lsof -a -d cwd -Fpn` (no `/proc`); `MacBackend.windows()` | the quit question is the native alert: Return ('Yes, quit', the first button) is the only answer tried, twice |
| `agent_restart_quit_stream`, `agent_restart_quit_queued`, `agent_restart_quit_blocked` | `need_quit_app`, and the stop that is the subject quits by Cmd-Q (`mac_quit=True`) | the setup and cleanup stops are still by pid, as before |

Not enabled, each with a stated SKIP: `primary_and_middle_click` (macOS has no PRIMARY selection: by design), `wheel_scroll` (the tool has the wheel op; the case's macOS arm is not written), the divider drag of `pane_resize_maximize` (a note, as before), and the full-tier pointer cases that do not pass `mac=True` (`ui_right_click_paste`, `alt_screen_mouse_reporting`, the network-gate pointer cases).

**The machine change `link_and_path_click` needs** (owner; the job never does it): `script/realapp/mac/ci/open_recorder.sh install`, run once in the runner user's GUI session, builds `~/Applications/PhosphorAppciOpenRecorder.app` from `openrec.swift`, registers it and asks macOS to make it the default handler for http and https; macOS confirms in a dialog. From then on every http / https link that user opens is appended to `~/Library/Caches/phosphor-appci/open-recorder.log` and opens nothing. `open_recorder.sh status` and `remove` are the other two verbs.

**Self-tests** (`script/realapp/appci/selftest_macptr.py`, run by `run.py --self-test` and `selftest.py`): `macptr_registry_and_docs_2061` (the proof case's registration and order, this section, the tool sources and their fences, the job's non-fatal compile loop), `macptr_chord_rule` (every spec's kind, each refusal reason alone, order kept by `keys`, htype2 never carries an app chord), `macptr_pointer_math_and_ops` (PNG size, scale, pixel to point, the op strings against the tool's parser, `MacMouse`, the skip / error of `mouse_or_skip`), `macptr_vision_words_lsof_and_recorder`, `macptr_case_gates_on_macos` (which cases reach the Mac pointer, which skip and why; quit / close keys per platform; a failed proof switches the chords off; the key names against `bindings.rs`; the alert's button order against `quit_warning/mod.rs`), `macptr_proof_case_parts`. Two older assertions changed with the behaviour: `NO_CLOSE_WHY` no longer says the chord is refused by policy, and `tab_lifecycle_keys` no longer has a macOS skip constant.

Run: `APPCI_CASES=mac_pointer_chord_proof,ui_mouse_select_copy,selection_modes,context_menu_actions,tab_pointer_use,tab_lifecycle_keys,quit_24_tabs` on `app-test-macos`. What the first run must show: all four `swiftc` compiles succeed; `display_scale` 2; `cursor_readback` equal pairs; the menu-bar click refused; `word_at` with a hook and an OCR position that agree; `chord_via pid` and the tab closed. If Cmd-W does not close the tab and the app log has no `hop=os_key_event` after it, `postToPid` did not deliver: rerun with `APPCI_MAC_CHORD_VIA=hid`.

## Round 15: the lab: the helper artifact, the families that never played, kl3's keys (design `docs/design/r15-lab.md`; #2062 #2063 #2005; nothing compiled, no lab or app run when written)

### The helper reaches every lab job (#2062)

- **Where a helper arm takes the helper from**, first hit (`cases_lab.resolve_helper_bin`): `APPCI_LAB_HELPER_BIN`; the `lab-helper` job's artifact in the
  checkout, `./helper-artifacts/` (override: `APPCI_LAB_HELPER_ARTIFACTS`); the box's helper cache. The artifact is used only as THIS checkout's helper
  (`lab_helper.py artifact_entry`): `meta.json`'s key must equal the key computed in the checkout, or, where no key can be computed, `export.json` must name
  the job's own pipeline. Another commit's file is refused by name and the cache is asked next.
- **Mac and Windows** (`app-test-lab-macos`, `app-test-lab-windows`): `needs: lab-helper` with `artifacts: true` (and `optional: true`), next to the build
  job; `APPCI_APP_PINNED_DIGESTS=0` as on Linux. Order of play on those machines: `sshlab-image`, **`lab-helper`**, the build, the lab job. `lab-helper` is
  seconds when the box has the helper cached. While a manual `needs` job has not been played GitLab does not offer the job that needs it (stated from
  GitLab's documented behaviour, not tried here). A `lab-helper` that FAILS (it is `allow_failure`) does not block them.
- **Linux** (`app-test-lab-linux`, `-reuse`): no `needs: lab-helper`. It runs on the machine that holds the cache the artifact is copied from, and a `needs`
  there would make the fix tier's lab job unplayable until someone plays `lab-helper` (`ci_seq.py` does not: `docs/design/r12-policy.md` 3, open item 5).
  Its `before_script` prints `lab_helper.py artifact`, then `path`.
- **`NEEDS:`.** When the build tools are missing, `lab_helper.py build` fails as before and writes one line, `NEEDS: <tools> installed for the CI runner
  user on the build box (owner: machine change; ...), then the manual lab-helper job played once`, to `helper-artifacts/NEEDS.txt` (the job's artifact is
  now `when: always`) and to `<cache>/NEEDS.txt`. A helper arm quotes that line as its reason; on Linux, with no record, it adds the same line for zig when
  zig is not where the build looks (`lab_helper.zig_needs`: `PATH`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.local/zig-*/`). The row is a SKIP that carries the line
  (`cases_lab.helper_missing_reason`, section 'Round 15: tier reach'; it was UNVERIFIABLE when this was written), never a pass.
  The first build that succeeds removes the record. Until the box has zig, cargo-zigbuild and the musl target, every helper arm on every platform reads
  `NEEDS: zig ...`.
- `lab_helper.py artifact` prints the artifact's binary or exits 3 with the reason. Self-tests: `lab_helper.py --self-test` (the artifact accepted and
  refused five ways, the NEEDS record written, quoted and cleared, each missing tool named) and `r15_lab_helper_from_the_artifact` in
  `appci/selftest_r15_lab.py` (the resolver's order, the reason a helper arm gives, the CI wiring).

### Every lab family is in a tier (#2063)

- **`PROVING_LAB` was two statements.** Round 14 merged two branches that each rewrote the tuple; Python used the second, `ci_seq.py` read the first. The
  harness's list had no `lab_agent_nld_predict_ssh`, and the fix tier's lab job was never given `lab_raw_key_arrival`. Now one assignment and one
  `PROVING_LAB += (...)` line per later entry; `ci_seq.proving_lab_globs` (`fold_tuple_assignments`, the one reader) folds them: with one assignment exactly what Python computes; should a second
  assignment come back, the union of both, never only one. Self-tests `r15_proving_lab_is_one_list` and two rows of
  `ci_seq.py --self-test`.
- **The families that had never produced a row** (`docs/design/r14-test-gaps.md` 4.5; 36 of the 46 registered families) are in `PROVING_LAB`, 28 of them, one a line: `lab_tab_remote_dir`,
  `lab_path_detect`, `lab_chips`, `lab_no_helper_chip`, `lab_nu_agent_pager_env`, `lab_ssh_drop_reconnect`, `lab_fam_fs_basic`, `lab_fam_git_read`,
  `lab_fam_run_command`, `lab_nohelper_*`, `lab_read_files_remote`, `lab_diff_apply_remote`, `lab_file_tree_remote`, `lab_diff_panel_remote`,
  `lab_gh_chip_remote`, `lab_git_write_remote`, `lab_remote_edit`, `lab_skills_remote`, `lab_codebase_index_remote`, `lab_helper_*`, and, named exactly
  because the quick matrix leaves scenario users and network faults out, `lab_password_prompt.p_password|p_kbdint.lan.nohelper`,
  `lab_path_detect.p_exec|p_tinypath.lan.nohelper`, `lab_ssh_drop_reconnect.bash.lan.nohelper.rst|stall10`.
- **Cost, counted from the registry, not measured:** at `APPCI_LAB_MATRIX=quick` the fix tier's lab job goes from 76 rows (the list `ci_seq.py` was
  reading) to 331: 203 no-helper rows (44 before) and 128 helper rows (32 before), which end at once as a SKIP with the `NEEDS:` line until the box
  builds the helper. At the 30 s a row the only timed lab run averaged (an upper figure: most of its rows ran to their timeouts), the 159 new no-helper
  rows add about 80 minutes. A no-helper-only play is `APPCI_LAB_MATRIX="shells=bash,zsh,fish,nu;lat=lan,150;helper=nohelper"`. Which tier carries them
  is the tier plan's and the owner's.
- **`cases.LAB_NOT_IN_FIX_TIER`** names the families that job does not play, with the reason: `lab_replay` (its own manual job,
  `app-test-replay-linux`), and the seven `lab_helper_*` families that have only upload / upgrade / never arms (a CI dev build refuses every upload; owner
  question, `r12-policy.md` 3 item 3). Self-test `r15_every_lab_family_is_in_a_tier`: a lab family is in `PROVING_LAB` or in that dict, never both, so a
  new family cannot be registered and never played.
- **`codebase_index_remote`** SKIPs unless the job sets `APPCI_FAKE_EMBEDDINGS=1`. Round 16 (owner 2026-11-11): the three lab jobs set it ("Round 16: harness decisions"), so the case is judged.

### Three drivers that did not exist

The three cases ended UNVERIFIABLE with "no keyboard path" / "no pointer click on the file tree". The first of those was not true.

| case | driver | oracle | UNVERIFIABLE when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lab_diff_panel_remote` | the command palette's `Toggle code review` (`cases_lab.open_code_review`). The app answers `hop=right_panel open=<bool> repo_context=<bool>` (trace only, `workspace/view/right_panel.rs`, format pinned by a unit test). Nothing is typed into the app after the panel opens: the prompt the shell backend refreshes on is made to return from outside (`cases_lab.hold_line`: the foreground waits for a file the harness creates over its own ssh connection) | as before: the snapshot's source and files; an edit from outside is pushed by the helper, and without the helper appears only after the next prompt. New: panel open and no `hop=diff_state` snapshot is a FAIL (`panel_no_snapshot_verdict`) | the app logged no `hop=right_panel` line (a build without it); a fish / nu login shell (#2019) |
| `lab_remote_edit` | a repository with one file; the palette's `Toggle project explorer` (it takes the focus), Down x4 (the selection stops at the last row), Enter | the app's `Opening remote file: ... path=<the file>` line, then: a typed edit saved with Ctrl/Cmd-S is in the host's file, byte for byte; every `hop=backend_route family=buffers` line names the arm's backend; after a change made on the host from a second connection and a second save, the host's change is still in the file (`conflict_verdict`: a save that replaces it fails) | the app did not log that it opened the file (nothing is typed then); a fish / nu login shell |
| `lab_git_write_remote`, app layer | the panel by the palette, then the pointer: the `Commit` button, the message, the dialog's `Confirm` (the dialog binds Escape only). Linux backends | `app_commit_verdict`: the host's last commit carries the typed message AND the app logged `hop=backend_route family=git_write backend=<shell|helper>` for the arm. A call on the wrong backend, a call with no commit, or a commit with no route line is a FAIL | no pointer (macOS, Windows: `NEEDS: pointer synthesis`); the panel not confirmed open; a button the OCR did not find; clicks made and no git call (whether the dialog opened is not known) |

Each driver leaves the window as it found it (the panel toggled closed, the editor pane closed after undoing unsaved typing, the file tree closed); a
close the app does not confirm is a note on the row with a screenshot. Self-test `r15_lab_panel_drivers_pure_parts`: every verdict function is fed the
results it must reject, `open_code_review` is run against a scripted app (an already-open panel is toggled twice; no trace line is `unknown`), and the
palette entries, the button words, the two app lines and the file tree's clamp are read from the app's sources.

Not built: the app-driven push / pull / stage / discard (the host layer and `contract_tests.rs` hold them); the helper families' own gaps
(`lab_helper_policy`, `lab_helper_scp_fallback`, the write half of `lab_helper_killed` end UNVERIFIABLE by their own text).

### The keys kl3 posts are counted (#2005)

Rounds 11 and 12 (after 15093ac33 and #2041): no row is TAINTED, no row has an Enter mismatch, and "app logged N more than were injected" is left on six
rows, all macOS: `latency_paint`, `latency_paint_ab`, `latency_key_views_ab`, both modes (39, 78, 78). Those are the cases whose keys `kl3` posts itself
(key to first changed pixel); no injector record was kept for them. `MacBackend.kl` now records each kl3 command as a call (`backend.kl_keys`: `K` one
key, `R` a Return, `T`/`F` text and a Return, `W` text; `kl_posted`: an answer without a post time is an errored call), marked `ref` when it is aimed at
the reference terminal, with `tool=kl3` in `inject.log`. Self-test `r15_kl3_keys_are_recorded`: the round 12 note reproduced without the record, gone with
it, and a key the app never saw still counted as lost.

## Round 15 wave 5 part A: T41, T42, T45, T50 and the Linux-only safety cases (design `docs/design/r15-w5a.md`; #2076 #2077 #2087 #2088; nothing compiled, no app run when written)
Source: `docs/design/r14-test-gaps.md` 7.1 (T41, T42, T45, T50) and gap G8. Three new app cases in `script/realapp/appci/cases_r15_w5a.py`, all in `cases.PROVING` (fix tier; graduation is the owner's), and four existing safety cases taken off "Linux only". Two app defects were found while building `editor_daily`; both have an issue, a change with an off switch and unit tests.
| `zero_network_startup` (T41) | Linux (strace, unchanged), macOS, Windows Git Bash pane | macOS / Windows: the app or one of its processes holds a connection to an address that is not loopback during launch + idle, or to anything but the configured model endpoint during the scripted session | 4 min (120 s idle) |
| `network_gate_switch` (#2077) | Linux (unchanged), macOS, Windows Git Bash pane | as on Linux: an OFF line with no key, not exactly one OFF line with `gate_enabled = false`, the origin's host in the log, a page action without its hop or without the file change | 3 min |
| `claude_plugin_offline`, `agent_plugins_offline` (#2077) | Linux, macOS | as on Linux; new on both: the no-network prefix did not block (then NOREF, not a pass) | 2 min each |
| `keychain_startup_macos` (T42, #1977) | macOS, terminal mode | first frame after the bound; a `Failed to read ... from secure storage` ERROR; with no default keychain not exactly one `The default keychain could not be opened` line and one notice; with a keychain present either of those; a locked keychain asks again after Cancel | 3 min |
| `keybinding_rebind` (T45) | all five panes, both modes | the chord named in `keybindings.yaml` opens no tab; the default chord still does; Ctrl-R still opens command search after the file moved it; the moved chord does not; the app rewrote the file | 3 min per mode |
| `editor_daily` (T50) | Linux, Windows (both panes), macOS (no close question), both modes | one Enter in the replace field replaced no match or more than one; replace-all left a match or touched a near-miss word; the close key did not ask (whatever `general.show_warning_before_quitting` says, #2092); Escape lost the edit; a file changed on disk was not reloaded, or was changed under unsaved edits without the banner state, or the app wrote it on its own; a save while the banner shows wrote the file without asking, Escape on that question changed the disk, Enter alone on it wrote the file or dropped the edits (it must cancel), or Tab then Enter did not write the editor's text (#2092) | 4 min per mode |
**The polled network trace (`appci/nettrace.py`).** macOS and Windows have no strace. The operating system's own connection table is read every 0.25 s for the app's processes, from before the launch until the scripted session ends: macOS `lsof -nP -i -a -p <pids>` (every process inside the job's bundle and their descendants), Windows `netstat -ano` (the members of the app's job object). A row counts when its remote address is not loopback, unspecified or link-local.
- **Control.** Before the app is stopped, a child of the harness connects to a listener on this machine's own non-loopback address and holds it; the tool must list that connection for that pid. If not, the case SKIPs with `NEEDS:` and the command that has to work. A tool that sees nothing can therefore not pass the case.
- **What a poll cannot see** (the result says so in a note, and records `trace = poll ...`): a connection that opens and closes between two polls, a UDP datagram sent without `connect()`, and DNS (the resolver service asks, not the app). The Linux strace run sees all three; a macOS or Windows pass is weaker evidence than a Linux pass.
- `pf` anchors and firewall rules were not used: both need root or an elevated runner.
**`network_gate_switch` off Linux.** The settings file of the NEXT launch is the profile's (`cases_robust.settings_file`; `start()` installs it). What the RUNNING app reads and writes is `cases_robust.live_settings_file`: the same file on Linux, `~/.phosphor/settings.toml` on macOS, the config folder under `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows. `cases_agent_netgate.origin_count` reads that one. After the page half the case proves the shell is in front again (`cases_netless.shell_back_in_front`) and ends with one more relaunch so the cases after it run on the restored file. Windows: the settings chord (`ctrl+comma`) had never been played; if the page shows no action at all the page half is NOREF, the launch half is still judged.
**The plugin cases off Linux.** macOS: `sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)(deny network*)'` in place of `unshare -rn`. On every platform the prefix is now proven first (`prefix_blocks_network`: a connect to a loopback listener made inside it must fail, and the same connect without it must succeed). The bundled plugin folders are also looked for in `Contents/Resources` of a macOS bundle (`bundle_roots`); the note in the result says which folder was used. The macOS launcher now logs the `CLI agent event received` line. Windows: SKIP. The Claude and Gemini plugins ship bash hooks only; the Codex plugin's PowerShell hooks need a console capture and a per-process network block (an elevated firewall rule), neither built.
**Still Linux only, with the reason in the skip text:** `agent_gate_deny_allow`, `network_gate_notice` (pointer and OCR: T32 on macOS, T31 on Windows), `agent_gate_off_live`, `agent_gate_key_never_leaves` (not ported: the strace oracle and the Linux close key), `keyring_unavailable_startup` (the Secret Service; macOS has `keychain_startup_macos`, Windows has no keyring service by design).
**`keychain_startup_macos`.** The app runs with a private `HOME`. The case first proves that the Security framework follows that `HOME`: a keychain created by `security create-keychain` with a relative name must land under it (it is deleted again). If it lands in the runner user's real home the case SKIPs with `NEEDS:`; it never changes the runner user's own default keychain, and it compares the runner's `default-keychain` and `list-keychains` before and after (a difference fails the case and is put back). Arms: `none` (played only when the private `HOME` has no default keychain), `unlocked` (a test keychain, default, unlocked), `locked`. Unlock prompts are windows of the `SecurityAgent` process, counted and cancelled through System Events (`watch_prompts`); without Accessibility permission for `osascript` the locked arm is not played and the case is NOREF with `NEEDS:`. Bound: `APPCI_KEYCHAIN_FIRST_FRAME_MAX_MS` (2000). The `finally` block stops the app (a pending prompt goes with it), deletes the test keychain and relaunches.
**`keybinding_rebind`.** `keybindings.yaml` (in `cases_robust.app_config_dir`) is read at launch only, so each arm is a relaunch; the user's file is put back and the app relaunched at the end. Test chords are `ctrl-shift-F8` and `ctrl-shift-F9` (every letter chord is a default; the self-test scans the Rust sources for a default on either). The macOS backend got the F-key codes. Tab counts: `hop=tab_activate` at a last-tab key; where the pane has a prompt log, also one more prompt. Command search: a frame that rendered `CommandSearchView` (`warpui::frame_cause`); the control's Ctrl-R must show it, else that half is NOREF. Until round 16 not played: a user file that puts a second action on Ctrl-R without moving command search (the focused input answered first). The owner decided it on 2026-11-11 (#1988: the user's line wins) and it is arm C now; see "Round 16: keys" below.
**`editor_daily`.** Keys: find `ctrl+shift+f` (`cmd+f`), the replace row `ctrl+alt+r` (`cmd+alt+r`), replace all `ctrl+alt+Return` (`cmd+alt+Return`), save, and the close key. Fields are emptied with End and BackSpaces before typing, so a remembered query cannot add to the text.
- *Find and replace.* The file has four matches of a per-run query, multi-byte text before the first, and two near-miss words. `replaced_once` accepts any ONE match replaced and nothing else changed; then replace-all must give `original.replace(query, replacement)` byte for byte. A build without #2088's bindings leaves the file unchanged and fails here with that text.
- *Close question* (not macOS: native dialog, NOREF there). `Displaying unsaved changes warning for pane` after the close key; Escape, then a save has the edit; close and Enter, then the file is the saved text or that plus the new edit (the metric says which). Since round 16 (#2092, owner decision 2026-11-11) the question must come whatever `general.show_warning_before_quitting` says: a profile with the setting off used to make this arm NOREF and is now judged like any other (a stricter expectation, because the decision changed the behaviour).
- *File changed on disk.* Both changes are made by rename (`replace_file`). Clean buffer: after `editor_disk outcome=reloaded external=true` (or 3 s on a build without the trace) a token typed and saved must sit on top of the NEW content. Unsaved edits: `editor_disk outcome=conflict external=true flagged=true` within 10 s, and the disk still holds the other program's text 2 s later. `flagged=false` or a reload over the edits fails with #2087.
- *A save while flagged* (#2092, owner decision 2026-11-11; until round 16 this was recorded and not judged, the save being the banner's Overwrite). The save key must give `editor_save_ask outcome=asked` within 5 s with the disk still the other program's text 1 s later (`save_ask_verdict`; metric `save_while_flagged` = `asked`, `overwrote`, `not_shown` or `nothing`, only `asked` passes). Escape must give `outcome=cancel` and leave the disk alone. A second save must ask again (this also proves the keyboard went back to the editor and the edits are still there). Enter ALONE must then give `outcome=cancel` with the disk still the other program's text 1 s later (`enter_alone_verdict`; metric `save_ask_enter_alone` = `cancelled`, `overwrote`, `reloaded` or `no_answer`, only `cancelled` passes). A third save must ask again, and Tab then Enter (`press_overwrite`) must give `outcome=overwrite` with the disk the editor's text, byte for byte (metric `save_ask_overwrite`). Changed expectation, because an owner decision changed the behaviour (2026-11-11: Enter is Cancel, never Overwrite): until then the case pressed Enter to overwrite; it now proves that Enter does not, and chooses Overwrite explicitly. Reload is not played. The question is the in-app dialog on every platform, so this part runs on macOS too; `close_editor` answers it with Tab then Enter when a save before a macOS close meets it (on a build before the change, or with the kill switch, Tab does nothing in the question and Enter is Overwrite, so the same keys overwrite there too).
**App changes of this round** (unit tests in `app/src/code/global_buffer_model_tests.rs` and `app/src/code/editor/view/vim_handler_tests.rs`; not compiled when written):
- #2088: `find:toggle_replace` (`alt-cmdorctrl-r`) and `find:replace_all` (`alt-cmdorctrl-enter`) in the code editor's find bar. Off: `none` in `keybindings.yaml`.
- #2087: a file changed on disk while its buffer has unsaved edits is remembered and the editor's conflict banner shows; the echo of the editor's own save is told apart by a hash of the written text. Off: `PHOSPHOR_EDITOR_DISK_CONFLICT=0`. Trace: `editor_disk outcome=<reloaded|conflict> external=<bool> flagged=<bool>` (target `editor_disk`, debug; all three launchers enable it).
- #2092 (round 16, `docs/design/r16-editor.md`; unit tests `app/src/quit_warning/mod_tests.rs`, `app/src/workspace/native_modal_tests.rs`, `app/src/code/save_conflict_tests.rs`; not compiled when written): (1) closing or quitting with unsaved editor edits asks whatever `general.show_warning_before_quitting` says; that dialog has no "Don't show again". Off: `PHOSPHOR_UNSAVED_EDITS_ALWAYS_ASK=0`. (2) A save while the conflict banner shows asks Overwrite / Reload / Cancel and writes nothing until the answer; the banner's own Overwrite button does not ask again. Off: `PHOSPHOR_EDITOR_SAVE_CONFLICT_ASK=0`. Trace: `editor_save_ask outcome=<asked|overwrite|reload|cancel|not_shown|banner_overwrite>` (target `editor_disk`, debug, already enabled by all three launchers). ## Round 16: the effect file of a burst is not read while a line may still open it (#2093; design `docs/design/r10-r16-fastwin.md`; no app run when written)
Round 13, Windows, PowerShell pane, terminal mode: `fast_typing` `ft0: file has 29/30 lines`, reported as "Phosphor-side (#1482)". The app log and
the PSReadLine history slice show the 30th line delivered and run (`pwsh_command_via_pipe`, `preexec_received` 11 ms later, `precmd_seen`, history
30/30 exact). The harness began polling the effect file (`ctx.lines`, an open and read every 50 ms) the moment the last Enter was posted;
Windows PowerShell's `Add-Content` does not share the file with a reader, so the last command of a gap-0 burst can be refused the file and write nothing.
TEST fault; no app change.
- `effect_run` (fast_typing, rollover and its other callers) and the reference burst of `run_enter_control` wait through `cases.await_effect_file`. On
  Windows that is `Ctx.await_file_size` (stat only, no read handle) until the file has the size of all its lines (`cases.effect_file_bytes`: CR LF
  from Windows PowerShell and cmd.exe, LF elsewhere), then the one read as before. A file that never gets there is read after the same timeout
  (`20 + n * 0.5` s): a lost line fails as it always did. Off Windows the line poll is unchanged.
- A `HARNESS:` note appears when every line is in the file and the size was never reached (the newline assumption is wrong for that shell; the burst
  then waits out its timeout).
- PowerShell pane: when PSReadLine history has every typed line exactly and the effect file lacks lines, a note says the lines were accepted by
  PowerShell, so the missing line is a command that ran and did not write, not lost typing. The failing check stays.
- Triage rule: a PowerShell-pane "file has N-1 lines" where the history or `preexec_received` shows the command ran is first a harness read colliding
  with `Add-Content`, not an app loss. Other cases that poll an effect file right after an Enter still have this exposure (design note, "Left open").
- Self-test `effect_file_is_not_read_while_a_burst_line_may_open_it_2093`: a writer that refuses to append while a reader holds the file loses the
  30th line under the old poll and keeps it under the size wait; a line that never comes is bounded by the timeout; the wrong-size note; source pins
  (no line poll in `effect_run` / `run_enter_control`, the exact-lines check still there, `await_file_size` opens nothing).
## Round 16: harness decisions (owner 2026-11-11; design `docs/design/r10-r16-harness.md`; harness and CI only; nothing compiled, no pipeline played, no app run when written)

Eight decisions, each a change to what a row or a tier means. Nothing in the app changed.

**1. `latency_key_log` is judged on the key -> pty write share on Linux and Windows.** The case has no reference terminal by construction, and off macOS the app logs no display-wait split, so the row was NOREF on Linux and Windows in every run (#2070). Now `cases.key_pty_share_gate` puts the app's own share of a key typed into a running `cat` (`key_write_pairs`: keydown to the event loop's `input_order pty_write` line, #1176) into the latency record as `app_share` (`what=key_to_pty_write`, `gate_only`), and `lat_checks(..., share_judges=True)` judges the row on it:

| the share (median, warm-up dropped) | row |
|---|---|
| <= 1 ms with n >= `APPCI_MIN_SAMPLES` (30) and >= 90 % of the keys typed | judged: PASS unless another check fails; the note says `JUDGED on the app's own share (key_to_pty_write)` |
| > 1 ms, whatever n is | FAIL: `the app's own share (key_to_pty_write) ... exceeds its 1.0 ms budget` |
| no keydown -> `pty_write` pair, or too few | NOREF with the reason (never a pass) |

The bound is `APPCI_KEY_PTY_SHARE_MAX_MS` (default 1, the #1176 target; r12a medians 0.33 to 0.69 ms). **Expectation change, stated because it changes a row:** a Linux or Windows run whose share is over 1 ms used to be NOREF with a note and is now a FAIL; one within it used to be NOREF and can now PASS. The regression verdicts (previous build, baseline) stay on the key -> frame median exactly as before: the share is a gate only and `regress_basis` is not touched. macOS is unchanged: it keeps its own-share gate (key -> frame less the display wait, 2 ms, #2037) and no key -> pty gate is applied there. Off macOS the NOREF question is asked of the budget verdict, so a regression WARN on the median cannot turn a row with no usable share into a pass (on macOS that case is as it was: recorded in the design note as a finding, not changed). The UI-item rule and the p50 / p99 sanity bounds are unchanged. Self-test: `key_log_is_judged_on_the_key_to_pty_write_share_off_macos` (a passing share, a failing one, exactly on the bound, no figure, thin figures on both sides of the bound, the median regression gate with a passing share, macOS left alone).

**2. `sudo_su_real_shell` passes only on an arm that ran and passed.** `cases_coverage_a.priv_arms_verdict`: arms the machine cannot run stay `NOT RUN:` notes (`boundaries_not_run`); the case PASSES only if at least one arm actually ran and passed (new metric `boundaries_passed`: an arm passes when its inner `id -u` gave the target user and it recorded no failed check); arms ran and none passed is a FAIL of its own; zero arms run is a SKIP whose text now STARTS with the `NEEDS:` machine change (`priv_boundary.sudo_needs()`), so the row and the trend list it as a machine change and never as coverage. Self-test: `r16_sudo_su_passes_only_on_an_arm_that_ran_and_passed` (the pure rule, and the case itself played with the machine and the pane replaced: both arms, one arm, none, a failed arm, a failed arm next to a passing one, an inner shell that never was the target user).

**3. `APPCI_FAKE_EMBEDDINGS=1` on the lab jobs.** `app-test-lab-linux` (and its `-reuse` variant, which extends it), `app-test-lab-macos` and `app-test-lab-windows` set it as a job variable, so `run.py` starts `script/fake_embeddings.py` on loopback, `profile.py` configures it as the BYOP embeddings provider, and `lab_codebase_index_remote` is judged instead of SKIP. `app-test-replay-linux` extends the lab job and sets it back to `"0"`: the replay's profile is unchanged. Side effect to know when reading a lab run: with the provider configured, codebase context and auto indexing are ON in the profile of every lab case of that job, not only the index case.

**4. The Mac and Windows lab jobs play only the `PROVING_LAB` globs in the candidate and release tiers.** `ci_seq.lab_tier_vars(plat, tier)` passes `APPCI_CASES=<the PROVING_LAB globs>` to `app-test-lab-macos` and `app-test-lab-windows` in the tiers named by `ci_seq.LAB_PLAT_PROVING_ONLY_TIERS` (`("candidate", "release")`; the release tier was added by r16-declare, owner 2026-11-11), with the quick matrix and the scripted model: exactly what the fix tier's Linux lab job plays (`lab_fix_vars`), instead of the quick matrix of every family. "For now": the jobs' own `APPCI_CASES: "lab_*"` is unchanged, so a hand play of either job still plays every family. No tier plays the quick matrix of every family on macOS or Windows any more: those rows (about 340 a platform) have never been played there. The Linux lab job is unchanged (every family, `LAB_CANDIDATE_MATRIX`).

**5. The ssh wrapper is pinned on macOS too.** `app-test-macos` sets `APPCI_SSH_WRAPPER: "1"` (as `app-test-linux-wayland` and `app-test-windows` since #2066), so `ssh_connect_typing_wrapper` and `ssh_nested_typeahead_wrapper` run in the macOS pane instead of SKIP with `NEEDS:`. The cases already refuse only the Windows PowerShell pane. The jobs that extend `app-test-macos` (the lab, the reuse variant) inherit the variable. Unproven: these two cases have never run on macOS.

**6. The macOS close key is given by the proof, in the same run.** `mac/ci/app_test.sh` still exports `APPCI_KEY_CLOSE=""` and now names the key in `APPCI_KEY_CLOSE_WHEN_PROVEN` (`cmd+w`; a hand-set empty value keeps the old behaviour). A shell variable cannot know a case's verdict, so `mac_pointer_chord_proof` calls `cases_robust.proven_close_key`: at its start the key is taken back (nothing is proven yet in this session mode's pass), and as its last step the key becomes `APPCI_KEY_CLOSE` / `cases_robust.CLOSE_PANE` only when the case has no failed check AND its chord half set `app_chords_proven` (Cmd-W closed a tab it opened). A proof that failed, skipped, raised or was not selected (the lab job) leaves the key empty, and every case after it keeps its Ctrl-D / palette path. The proof's row says which (`close_key_after_proof`, and a note). What changes after a passing proof: every macOS case that reads `APPCI_KEY_CLOSE` / `CLOSE_PANE` (soak, the editor and viewer closes, `close_extra_tabs`, the tab cases) sends Cmd-W through the app-only chord path (`MacBackend.app_chord`, the appkey tool) instead of taking its no-close-key path. That is about a dozen cases on a path that has never run; a failure there right after this change is first a harness question. Self-test: `r16_macos_close_key_only_after_the_proof_passed`.

**7. The never-played lab families: one fix-tier run, then the candidate tier (MOVE-AFTER-ONE-RUN).** The #2063 entries stay in `PROVING_LAB` for ONE fix-tier run of `app-test-lab-linux`. They are NOT moved now. `grep -rn MOVE-AFTER-ONE-RUN script docs` finds the marker in `appci/cases.py` (above the tuple `LAB_MOVE_AFTER_ONE_RUN`) and here. After that run the coordinator moves these out of the fix tier (delete their `PROVING_LAB += (...)` lines, give each family a line in `LAB_NOT_IN_FIX_TIER` naming the candidate tier, delete the tuple and its self-test); the candidate tier's Linux lab job already plays every one of them (`lab_*` under `LAB_CANDIDATE_MATRIX`, scenario users and faults included). A family that failed in that run is triaged first, and the owner is asked which ones go (no graduation without asking). The entries:
`lab_tab_remote_dir`, `lab_path_detect`, `lab_chips`, `lab_no_helper_chip`, `lab_nu_agent_pager_env`, `lab_ssh_drop_reconnect`, `lab_fam_fs_basic`, `lab_fam_git_read`, `lab_fam_run_command`, `lab_nohelper_*`, `lab_read_files_remote`, `lab_diff_apply_remote`, `lab_file_tree_remote`, `lab_diff_panel_remote`, `lab_gh_chip_remote`, `lab_git_write_remote`, `lab_remote_edit`, `lab_skills_remote`, `lab_codebase_index_remote`, `lab_helper_*`, and the six exact arms `lab_password_prompt.p_password|p_kbdint.lan.nohelper`, `lab_path_detect.p_exec|p_tinypath.lan.nohelper`, `lab_ssh_drop_reconnect.bash.lan.nohelper.rst|stall10`. Staying in the fix tier: `lab_agent_remote_*`, `lab_fam_agent_*`, `lab_enter_no_network_wait`, `lab_enter_start` (150 ms), `lab_ctrl_c_no_esc_i`, `lab_agent_nld_predict_ssh`, `lab_raw_key_arrival`, `lab_freeze_and_wake`. Self-test: `r16_never_played_lab_families_wait_one_run` (every entry is still in `PROVING_LAB`, the tuple is exactly the #2063 block, and the candidate matrix selects every arm the entries select today).

**8. The guards job names the #2086 and #2089 / #2090 checks.** `guards` ran `selftest.py`, which runs both checks only as long as the two lines at the file's tail that register `selftest_registered.py` and `selftest_r15_lab.py` survive every merge, and nothing noticed when such lines were lost (#2086 is that story). Now the job runs `python3 script/realapp/appci/selftest.py --require every_check_function_is_registered_2086,r15_proving_lab_is_one_list`: `--require` fails the run when a named check was not among those that ran AND passed. The job also runs `python3 script/ci/ci_seq.py --self-test` (pure; it reads `.gitlab-ci.yml` and `cases.py`), which holds the rows for the one `PROVING_LAB` reader and for decisions 3 to 5 and 8.

Self-tests: `script/realapp/appci/selftest_r16_harness.py` (four checks, run by `run.py --self-test` and `selftest.py`), one check in `selftest.py`, eight rows in `ci_seq.py --self-test`.

**What the next runs should show.** Fix tier, Linux: `latency_key_log` PASS in both modes on Wayland and X11 with `JUDGED on the app's own share (key_to_pty_write)` in its notes (a FAIL names the share and the 1 ms budget; that is then an app number to look at, #1176); `sudo_su_real_shell` SKIP with a text that starts `NEEDS:` until the sudoers entry exists, then PASS with `boundaries_passed` not empty; the lab job judges `lab_codebase_index_remote.*` (PASS or FAIL, no longer SKIP "the fake embeddings provider is not running"); every MOVE-AFTER-ONE-RUN family has a row. Fix tier, macOS: the two `*_wrapper` cases are judged; `mac_pointer_chord_proof` carries `close_key_after_proof`. Candidate tier: the Mac and Windows lab jobs play the `PROVING_LAB` arms only. The guards job prints both required check names as `ok`.
## Round 16: keys (design `docs/design/r10-r16-keys2.md`; #1988 #2079 #2080; owner decisions of 2026-11-11; nothing compiled, no app run when written)
Four behaviour changes, each with a kill switch read at app start. Worked, unproven.
| issue | change | kill switch | unit tests | app case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #1988 | A binding the user bound to Ctrl-R (`keybindings.yaml`, or the settings page) wins over command search wherever that binding applies, also at the prompt. Command search is the one built-in binding marked as yielding (`util/bindings.rs` `BINDINGS_YIELDING_TO_USER_BINDINGS`); macOS: its menu item gives up the key equivalent while a user binding claims it | `PHOSPHOR_USER_BINDING_WINS=0` | `warpui_core` `keymap/matcher_test.rs`: `user_bound_binding_outranks_a_yielding_default_of_a_deeper_view`, `user_bound_binding_outranks_a_yielding_default_of_the_same_view`; `util/bindings_tests.rs` `test_command_search_yields_to_a_user_binding` | `keybinding_rebind` arm C (new) |
| #1988 B | Alt-R (Linux, Windows) / Option-R as Meta (macOS) opens the history search, `input:search_command_history`; in the input only, so a program in front still gets `ESC r` | `PHOSPHOR_ALT_R_HISTORY_SEARCH=0` (ships unbound) | `util/bindings_tests.rs`: `test_history_search_default_keystroke_per_platform_and_kill_switch`, `test_history_search_binding_default_and_no_collision` | `keybinding_rebind` control and arm C (new steps); `ui_readline_keys` (unchanged: Alt-R with a program in front is `1b72`) |
| #2079 | Off macOS, in the text editor (the input and the app's single-line fields): Ctrl-A start of line, Ctrl-E end of line, Ctrl-Y yank; select-all is Ctrl-Shift-A (all three editors' `editor_view:select_all`; a file or a notebook keeps its fixed Ctrl-A select-all); `editor_view:delete_all_left` ships without a key in the text editor; the Linux "emacs bindings" banner is not offered; a user binding already on Ctrl-A / Ctrl-E keeps winning (the two new defaults yield). macOS unchanged | `PHOSPHOR_READLINE_INPUT_KEYS=0` | `util/bindings_tests.rs`: `test_readline_input_keys_kill_switch_and_platforms`, `test_readline_input_keys_default_bindings_per_platform` | `meta_and_word_keys` (expectation changed, below) |
| #2080 | Shift+PageUp / PageDown / Home / End also scroll at a prompt, and are editable bindings (`terminal:scrollback_page_up`, `_page_down`, `_top`, `_bottom`). Shift+Home / Shift+End: only while the terminal input is empty; with text they select, as before. The alternate screen keeps the keys | `PHOSPHOR_SCROLLBACK_KEYS_AT_PROMPT=0` (a running command only, as in round 15); `PHOSPHOR_SCROLLBACK_KEYS=0` (none registered) | `terminal/view/scrollback_keys_tests.rs` (`the_keys_are_live_at_a_prompt`, the alternate screen in both settings, the names, the switch); `editor/view/mod_test.rs` `shift_home_end_select_except_in_an_empty_terminal_input`; `util/bindings_tests.rs` `test_scrollback_keys_are_editable_bindings` | `scroll_keys_foreground` (new first half, below) |
**Changed expectations (each because an owner decision changed the behaviour; none is weaker).**
- `meta_and_word_keys`: the Ctrl-A, Ctrl-E and Ctrl-Y steps accepted the app's IDE default on Linux and Windows as `app_default`. They
  must give the readline line now; a Ctrl-A that selects all, a Ctrl-E that does not move and a Ctrl-Y that deletes to the line start
  are failures. The Ctrl-Y step off macOS is the macOS one (Ctrl-K kills, Ctrl-Y yanks it back at the cursor). The self-test
  `r14_w1b_pure_parts` now asserts that no step carries a default and that a Ctrl-E that does nothing fails on every platform.
- `util/bindings_tests.rs`: round 14 pinned `alt-r` / `meta-r` as unbound while #1988 was open. That pin is replaced by
  `test_history_search_binding_default_and_no_collision` (the history search is the only claimant).
- `terminal/view/scrollback_keys_tests.rs`: "the prompt keeps the keys" is now the kill-switch arm
  (`without_the_prompt_half_...`); with the default the prompt has them.
**`keybinding_rebind`, new steps.** Control: Alt-R must render `CommandSearchView` (judged only when the control's Ctrl-R showed that
view; else NOREF). Arm C, a third relaunch with `"workspace:new_tab": ctrl-r` alone: Ctrl-R opens one tab, no frame renders
`CommandSearchView`, a line typed next runs in the shell, and Alt-R still opens the search. Alt-R is not played on macOS without
Option as Meta, nor on Linux / Windows with the left Alt set to act as Meta (`alt_r_playable`; a note says so). About 40 s more per mode.
**`scroll_keys_foreground`, new first half (at the prompt, after the 300-line `cat`, before the foreground program).** Empty input:
Shift+PageUp twice, Shift+Home, Shift+PageDown, Shift+End must each log their `hop=scrollback_key` line(s), exactly. Then with
`echo sfgold<tok>` typed and not entered: Shift+Home must log NO hop, and `echo sfgnew<tok>` typed next with Enter must be the one line
the shell receives (the selection was replaced). A build without the prompt half fails the first four with "did not scroll at the
prompt". Not covered at the prompt: the view's position by OCR (the foreground half reads it), and the PowerShell pane (the case SKIPs
there as before). About 10 s more.
Self-tests: `r15_scroll_keys_pure_parts` (the two new verdicts with the input a defect produces, the Rust names and predicate text),

## Round 17, queue 3: #1999, #2000, #1991 (design `docs/design/r10-r17-queue3.md`; owner decisions of 2026-11-11; nothing compiled, no app run when written)
Kill switches, in `app/src/terminal/input_queue/switches.rs` beside the round 14 ones (read once per process; `0` / `off` / `false` /
`no` turn the change off; names pinned by `the_switch_names_are_stable`): `PHOSPHOR_BARE_ENTER_HOLDS_LINES` (#1999),
`PHOSPHOR_KEEP_DEFERRED_ENTER_KEYS_WITH_LINE` (#2000), `PHOSPHOR_SUBSHELL_LINE_EDITOR_PROOF` (#1991). A switch is read once, so a
unit test cannot flip it: each change has a pure function that takes the switch as an argument, and the tests cover both values there.
- **#1999, lines typed behind a bare deferred Enter wait behind it.** Unit, `terminal/input/enter_queue_tests.rs` (new file):
  `a_bare_enter_held_for_an_unready_shell_holds_the_lines_typed_behind_it` (`enter_gate_holds_lines_typed_behind` for every row and
  both switch values: a non-empty line always holds, a bare Enter held for an unready shell holds only with the switch on, a submitted
  Enter's gate with an empty buffer never). View, `terminal/view_test.rs`:
  `typeahead_handoff_releases_held_shell_lines_to_the_pty_when_the_submit_runs_nothing`, EXPECTATION CHANGED by the owner's decision
  (not weakened): it expected `echo 1\recho 2\r` at the pty when the report arrived, while the bare Enter typed before them was still
  held. It now expects nothing at the pty, the lines as one entry behind the bare Enter's own gate (the `HandoffReport` gate closed),
  and at the hold's give-up `\recho 1\recho 2\r`, once, with the queue idle. Not covered: the readiness path for a bare Enter (the
  #1997 readiness test covers the release order for a non-empty line; a bare line takes the same `release_unready_enter_gate_after_run`),
  the switch off in the view. No appci case: the state needs a shell that refuses a command at a prompt (#1572's window), which no
  case builds; `giveup_keys_reach_shell` reports "no hold gave up" in its runs. Hop to read if it happens:
  `hop=held_lines_kept_behind_enter entries=N` with `enter_held_gate` just before it.
- **#2000, an event that keeps a deferred Enter unrun keeps the keys behind it with its line.** New file
  `terminal/view/keep_deferred_enter_tests.rs` (a child of `view_test.rs`):
  `an_unrun_deferred_enter_keeps_its_keys_with_its_line_unless_switched_off` (pure: `unrun_deferred_enter_keys_then` for the three
  callers' reasons and both switch values; `kept_enter_keys_stay_with_line` for an empty line and a secret read;
  `gate_keys_may_follow_a_waiting_enter` for the three `GateKeysThen`),
  `a_line_typed_behind_a_deferred_enter_kept_unrun_stays_with_that_line_in_the_input` (Legacy and Table, once per caller reason:
  `cd build`, a deferred Enter, `make clean` + Enter behind it, the report, then `keep_deferred_enter_text`; nothing at the pty,

  idle; before the change `make clean\r` was written), `keys_behind_a_bare_deferred_enter_kept_unrun_are_released_as_before` (an empty
  input: `echo 1\r` reaches the pty once, nothing becomes editor text),
  `keys_behind_an_unrun_deferred_enter_go_to_a_secret_read_not_into_the_input` (#1957 kept: with the secret probe true the keys are
  written and the input still holds only line one). Not covered: each caller reached through its own trigger (a refused report needs a
