## Round 17 misc (#2028, #2030, #2055, #2091, #2096; `docs/design/r17-misc.md`)

Nothing here was compiled or run with cargo. All "worked, unproven" until a run.

**#2096: `test_cursor_blink_tick_requests_paint_only_frame` can now fail on a notify.** A `ctx.notify()` is a queued effect; it reaches the
window's invalidation only when the outermost update returns, and the unit-test window then builds its scene and consumes the invalidation. So
a test that runs a handler inside `app.update(..)` and reads `take_invalidation_kind_for_test` there can NOT see a notify of that handler.
`AppContext::pending_view_notifications_for_test(window_id, view_id)` (test / `test-util` only, `crates/warpui_core/src/core/app.rs`; also on
`App`) counts the queued `Effect::ViewNotification` entries of one view. The blink test reads it before and after the tick, inside the same
update, and requires zero new ones; `needs_layout` stays as the check for a layout redraw request. Control:
`test_a_view_notify_is_visible_to_the_blink_test_observation` makes the same observation of a real `ctx.notify()` (one counted, `needs_layout`
still false before the flush). Use the same pair wherever a test must show that a handler does not notify its view.

**#2030: bash prompt hooks, measured and trimmed.** Not a fork problem: `test_hook_forks` run with the shell started as a REMOTE one counts 0 execs
and 0 forks per prompt (bash 5.3). The time was the byte loop of `__warp_hex_encode_to` over the fixed text of CommandFinished and the Precmd head
on every prompt. Those pieces are now encoded once per session id and joined with the hex of the numbers (`__warp_hex_digits_to`); kill switch
`PHOSPHOR_BASH_HOOK_HEX_CACHE=0` (2.6). In-shell timing on the laptop: everything between a command's end and the prompt 4.17 ms to 2.46 ms.
Proof on the wire: `test_bootstrap_hook_equivalence` ("bash hook hex cache", 2.4). Proof of the effect: the lab's
`lab_enter_start.bash.150.nohelper` metrics `enter_to_next_prompt_app_ms` (r13a median 107.1 ms, zsh 82.0 ms) and `enter_start_app_ms` (85.7 / 81.5);
the next lab run should show the bash next-prompt figure lower and the command-start figure about the same. No new app case: the existing lab
case measures exactly this and the harness cannot see inside the remote shell otherwise.

**#2028: `md_viewer_first_frame` (`appci/cases_r17_misc.py`; `PROVING`; Linux, macOS, both Windows panes; both modes).** The markdown viewer
(`FileNotebookView`) now holds its layout until its element has given the render model a width (`RenderState::hold_layout_until_first_size`): edits
that arrive before the first frame are queued and laid out by the first `set_viewport_size` with a width above zero, which logs
`rich text: first size <w>x<h> released <n> held layout edit(s)` and asks for no resize. Before, the file was shaped at width 0 and the first frame
showed one glyph per line for at least the 150 ms resize debounce. The case writes a markdown file with a heading, an image (a PNG it builds itself)
and a 120-word paragraph, hands it to the running app (`open_file_in_app`) and judges the app log since the open: the first-size line with a width
above zero, and no `image paint with suspicious size` line (the issue's own evidence). The heading is read by OCR where there is an engine (a note
without one); the broken picture lasted too short to be caught by a screenshot, so the log is the oracle. Control (Linux launcher only): the app
relaunched with `PHOSPHOR_MD_FIRST_LAYOUT_HOLD=0` opens the same file and must NOT log the first-size line; how many suspicious image paints it logs
there is the metric `control_suspicious_image_paints` (it depends on whether the file arrives before the first frame, so it is not a verdict). The
case then relaunches with the default environment. A build before the fix FAILS the case ("no `rich text: first size` line"). Not covered: the code
pane's rendered remote markdown (`app/src/code/view.rs`), which very likely has the same first frame and does not hold (not opted in; see the design
note). Unit tests: `crates/editor/src/render/mod_tests.rs` `test_first_size_hold_lays_out_at_the_first_width_and_not_before` (nothing laid out and no
version published while holding; a zero width keeps the hold and asks for no resize; the first width lays out, reports once, asks for no resize; one-shot
afterwards), `test_without_the_first_size_hold_an_edit_is_laid_out_on_arrival` (control), `test_first_size_hold_is_refused_where_it_cannot_apply`;
`app/src/notebooks/file/mod_tests.rs` `test_file_notebook_holds_layout_until_its_first_size`, `test_first_layout_hold_kill_switch_is_the_exact_value_zero`.
**Expectation change in an existing test, stated:** `test_file_notebook_mermaid_blocks_default_to_rendered` read the laid-out content right after
`layout_complete()`; with the hold the content exists only after the viewer's first frame, so the test now also waits (bounded, 2000 yields) for the
hold to be released. Its assertions are unchanged.
**Round 18 (`docs/design/r18-firstsize.md`): the two `test_first_size_hold_*` failures of round 14 were a TEST fault.** They judged "laid out" by
`RenderState::blocks() > 1`, but one typed paragraph replaces the empty document's trailing-newline block: the count is 1 before and after (the
trace shows the hold releasing and the paragraph laid out). Both tests now judge the described content (`assert_rendered`): `Trailing Newline` while
nothing is laid out, `Paragraph (28 characters, ...)` once it is. Do not use a block count to tell an empty render model from a laid out one.

**#2091: `gpu_lost_device_recovers` (`appci/cases_r15_w5c.py`; `PROVING`; Linux, both modes).** The third oracle of T48. The app is relaunched with
`PHOSPHOR_TEST_GPU_LOSE_DEVICE_FILE=<work dir>/phosphor-test-lose-gpu-device` (2.6); the launch log must have `TEST HOOK armed` (else UNVERIFIABLE:
a build without the hook). The case clears the pane (control picture), draws the 24-row pattern of `gpu_real_render` (reference picture), creates the
trigger file and, if no redraw took it within 1.5 s, types one key. Judged from the app log after that: the hook's line exactly once and the file
gone; `Recreating the renderer` after it; a `Surface configured:` line after that (the rebuilt renderer; its adapter is on the row); at least one
`hop=frame_drawn` after the rebuild; the app alive and no panic. Then one more key and Backspace for every key typed, a settled screenshot, and the
screen must equal the reference within `APPCI_GPU_SHOT_DIFF` (2 %), with the cleared pane against the pattern differing by 5x that (else
UNVERIFIABLE). It runs on whatever adapter the launch uses: the render node where the session can present to it, the software rasteriser under Xvfb;
the rebuild is the app's own code either way. Metric and note, not a verdict: `frames_after_rebuild_before_input`, the frames drawn in the 2 s after
the rebuild before the next key. The lost-device decision asks for no retry, so 0 is expected on an idle window: the frame that hit the loss waits for
the next event (#2101, filed, not worked). `gpu_real_render` rows now say where the third oracle is judged instead of `NOT RUN:`. Unit tests:
`draw_retry_tests.rs` `test_device_loss_hook_is_off_unless_the_variable_names_its_own_file`, `test_device_loss_hook_fires_once_per_trigger_file`,
`the_error_the_test_hook_reports_rebuilds_the_renderer`.

Self-tests: `appci/selftest_r17_misc.py` (registered at the tail of `selftest.py`): both verdicts with the input each defect produces, the PNG
fixture, and the Rust strings and order the cases read (`r17_*`).
Run: `python3 script/realapp/appci/run.py --cases md_viewer_first_frame,gpu_lost_device_recovers`.
What the next run should show: `md_viewer_first_frame` PASS in both modes with a first size near the pane size and `suspicious_image_paints` 0;
`gpu_lost_device_recovers` PASS in both modes on Wayland and X11 with the adapter named, and `frames_after_rebuild_before_input` (0 confirms #2101).

## Round 18: a stop while a tool batch is still preprocessing (design `docs/design/r18-stoppre.md`; #2104; nothing compiled or run when written)

A reply's tool calls are preprocessed as one batch before any is queued. A Stop (or a pane close's stop, or a new turn) that dropped a batch
still in preprocessing used to leave its calls with no status and no result until the batch's future came back (never, for a hung apply,
#1894): the turn watch (#1967) then logged a false `hop=agent_turn_stuck fault=unsettled_calls`, the late result recorded a second
cancelled result, and a late result arriving while a pane was closed was never discarded by the close (#848). Now the calls are cancelled
when the batch is dropped and the late result is dropped. Kill switch `PHOSPHOR_STOP_SETTLES_PREPROCESSING=0` (the old behaviour). App
log, once per late batch: `hop=agent_late_preprocess_result dropped=<n> recorded=<m> conversation=<id>`; each call cancelled at the stop
logs `hop=agent_action id=<id> kind=<tool> status=cancelled` like any cancelled action.

- **Test hold (new, test-only): `BlocklistAIActionModel::set_preprocess_hold_for_test` / `release_held_preprocessing_for_test`.** While
  the hold is on, every batch queued waits on one more preprocess future that resolves when the test releases it (or when the model goes
  away). That is "still preprocessing" for as long as a test wants, and a hung apply when it never releases. Not a timer.
- **Unit, `ai/blocklist/action_model/preprocess_tests.rs`** (the batch bookkeeping, no app):
  `abandon_all_settling_returns_the_calls_of_batches_still_preprocessing` (a cancel hands back the kept copies of every batch still
  preprocessing, in queue order, next to the parked actions; `abandon_all`, the kill switch's arm, returns the parked ones only; fails on
  the old code, where a batch knew ids only), `a_batch_that_came_back_is_not_handed_back_as_preprocessing` (and its late result is still
  reported as stale, #1894), `take_actions_of_abandoned_hands_the_calls_back_once_and_keeps_the_markers` (the new-turn site, #1859).
- **Unit, `ai/blocklist/controller_tests.rs`, module `stop_while_preprocessing_2104`** (a real controller and action model, the batch
  queued through `queue_actions` and held in preprocessing):
  - `a_stop_gives_the_calls_of_a_preprocessing_batch_their_cancelled_result_at_the_stop`: `cancel_conversation_progress(ManuallyCancelled)`
    with the hold never released; in the same call each call is `Finished` cancelled with one result, in the reply's order; the turn ends
    `Cancelled`. Fails on the old code (no status).
  - `the_late_result_of_a_stopped_batch_is_dropped`: stop, then a second writer at the same calls (`cancel_discarded_actions`, what the
    #1967 heal used), then the batch is released: exactly one result per call. Fails on the old code (two).
  - `a_pane_close_discards_the_cancelled_results_of_a_preprocessing_batch`: suspend, discard, stop (the view's order), the batch
    released while the pane is closed, undo: no finished result is left to ride on a later request, each call shows cancelled and is
    held as discarded-by-close (#2103). Fails on the old code (the late result was recorded behind the close).
  - `a_new_turn_settles_the_calls_of_an_earlier_batch_that_is_still_preprocessing`: a second `queue_actions` gives up on the first
    batch; its calls are cancelled then, the late result adds nothing, the new batch leaves preprocessing untouched. Fails on the old
    code.
  - `with_the_kill_switch_off_a_stop_leaves_the_preprocessing_calls_to_their_late_result`: the switch's values, and the old arm driven
    with the flag passed in (`cancel_all_pending_actions_with(.., false, ..)`): no status at the stop, one result when the batch comes
    back. It is also the positive control of the late-result test: the same release and the same wait DO deliver a late result here.
  - `a_stop_reports_the_preprocessing_calls_it_cancelled`: `CancelledPendingActions { cancelled_any: true, dropped_preprocessing: true }`.
- **Scenario schema (`crates/fake_llm/src/scenario.rs`): `env.preprocess`**, optional, absent by default and from every existing file
  (`env_preprocess_is_optional_and_round_trips`; still `"v": 1`). `{"kind": "hung"}`: every batch stays in preprocessing for good.
  `{"kind": "late_after_drop", "ms": N}`: a batch stays in preprocessing until N ms AFTER it was dropped (a stop), never before, so the
  stop meets a preprocessing batch however slow the box is. L1 only: `rig.rs` turns the hold on at setup and `drive_preprocessing`
  (called from `drive_commands`) releases a `late_after_drop` batch. The random strategies never set it: the generated cases are
  unchanged.
- **Agent fuzz corpus (replayed on every run by `corpus_replay_tests`, allowlist off and on):**
  `stop2104_stop_while_preprocessing_hung_apply.json` (a command and a read in one reply, held for good; Stop after the stream's end, a
  second Stop) and `stop2104_stop_while_preprocessing_late_result_then_follow_up.json` (one command, held until 30 ms after the stop;
  Stop, two waits, the user's next message). On a build without the fix both fail I6 (`hop=agent_turn_stuck fault=unsettled_calls`).
  **The oracle is unchanged** (`oracle.rs` and `runner.rs` are not touched; no ERROR allowance was added).
- **Agent fuzz, `corpus_replay_tests::a_stop_while_the_batch_is_preprocessing_settles_its_calls_and_drops_the_late_result`:** runs the
  two scenarios and pins what the replay cannot say: the Stop was performed with the front of the snapshot in the `preprocessing` stage
  (a scenario that stopped too late cannot pass for the wrong reason), the hung one ends `Cancelled` with one request, and the other
  opens exactly two requests, the second carrying ONE tool message for the one call.
- **Not covered:** the cards' look after a stop during preprocessing (a cancelled card, as before by the "orphaned" rule; no log line
  tells the two apart), and no app case: holding a batch in preprocessing needs a hung diff apply, which the app cases cannot stage.
  The first run with a slow remote apply that the user stops is the app-level evidence: `hop=agent_action ... status=cancelled` for
  the call at the stop, no `hop=agent_turn_stuck`, and at most one `hop=agent_late_preprocess_result` afterwards.
- **What the next run should show.** The nine new unit tests, the new fuzz test and the schema test (`fake_llm`) pass; `corpus_replays_as_listed_and_reaches_the_wave0_cells`
  and `corpus_replays_with_the_allowlist_on` pass with the two new files; both paced fuzz tests are unaffected (their scenarios never
  hold a batch). A fuzz I2b / I3 failure after a Stop on a preprocessing batch would be this change (the turn now ends through the
  cancelled calls' `FinishedAction`): triage it against `docs/design/r18-stoppre.md`, "Risk".
  Run (on the box, in the usual `-p warp -p warp_tui --lib --features warp/gui` unit run): the filters `stop_while_preprocessing_2104`,
  `action_model::preprocess::tests`, `corpus_replay_tests`; and `fake_llm`'s `scenario::tests`.

## Round 18: a pane close keeps the status of the calls whose results it discards (design `docs/design/r18-retire.md`; #2103, #848; nothing compiled or run when written)

Owner decision 2026-11-11, with its condition: the results a close discards are kept for the calls' STATUS only (cards, turn bookkeeping) and
are never sent to the model. Kill switch `PHOSPHOR_CLOSE_KEEPS_CALL_STATUS=0` (the close erases them as before). App log, one line per close
that discards something: `hop=agent_close_discard conversation=<id> results=<n> kept_status=<0|1>`.

- **Unit, `ai/blocklist/controller_tests.rs`** (no BYOP provider: a request is seen as the controller builds it, as for the #1059 tests).
  `a_pane_close_discards_finished_results_and_their_calls_keep_their_status` (after close + undo: nothing left to send, the call that ran is
  still a success, the cancelled one still cancelled, neither is in the copy / export text; red on the old code, where both had no status).
  `a_result_a_pane_close_discarded_is_in_no_later_request` (the owner's condition: close with a finished, unsent result, undo, then the
  automatic and the user-requested follow-up send nothing, and the user's next prompt and the one after it carry no tool result: checked on
  every in-flight stream's inputs, every exchange's inputs and every `ToolCallResult` in the conversation's tasks).
  `without_a_close_the_finished_result_travels_with_the_next_prompt` (its positive control: the same result with no close IS sent).
  `with_the_kill_switch_off_a_pane_close_erases_the_results` (the switch's values; the erase arm leaves no status).
- **Cards, `ai/blocklist/block/view_impl/output_tests.rs` `discarded_by_close_tests::cards_of_a_restored_pane_show_what_the_discarded_calls_did`.**
  With the pane's real action model after a real close-discard, the two predicates `render` and `action_icon` decide on, with "hide completed
  tool cards" off and on: the call that ran is a finished success (not orphaned; hidden exactly when the setting is on, like any completed
  card), the cancelled call is a cancelled card that is never hidden, and the control (a call with no status) is orphaned and never hidden,
  which is how both calls read before #2103. It does not paint a card.
- **Agent fuzz oracle (`agent_fuzz/oracle.rs`): the `tab_closed` exception is gone by default.** It switched the "status or result" half of
  I1 off for the rest of a scenario after a close, because the close erased finished results and left their calls with no status. That is all
  it excused, and the close no longer does it, so I1 is judged after a close as before it. The exception remains only for
  `PHOSPHOR_CLOSE_KEEPS_CALL_STATUS=0` (`Oracle::tab_closed(results_erased)`), where the erase still happens. Not a weakening: the oracle now
  judges strictly more. A call with no status and no result after a close is a finding. Corpus `heal2103_stop_after_close_is_not_a_stuck_turn`
  must still pass: its call's cancelled result is kept at the close, so the later Stop finds nothing unsettled.
- **The r18-agentheal guard stays** (`replies_discarded_for_close`, `a_reply_a_close_stopped_is_not_judged_for_unsettled_calls`): the kept
  status does not cover a batch that was still preprocessing when the close's stop dropped it, nor the kill switch's arm. (Since #2104
  the close's stop cancels those calls too, see the section above; the guard is then the cover for the two kill switches only.)
- **App case `agent_close_undo_call_status`** (`appci/cases_agent_close_undo.py`; agent mode, scripted model; `cases.PROVING` and
  `PROVING_FAKE`; settings declared in `case_settings.py`; Windows: Git Bash pane). A new tab; ONE reply with a command (approved by keyboard,
  prints a token that is not in its command line) and a question (`fake_model.py` trigger "Please run scripted command KEY then ask me a
  question TAG"); when the command is done and the question waits, the close key, the undo key, a plain prompt. Oracles: the app's
  `hop=agent_close_discard` with `results>=1 kept_status=1`; the printed token in NO tool-result message of any request after the close
  (`fake.reqs`; other places, e.g. attached block context, are a note); the prompt after the undo reaches the model once and ends `success`;
  no `hop=agent_turn_stuck`, no unexpected ERROR. UNVERIFIABLE (never a pass) when the command never finished behind a waiting question or the
  app logged no discard line. NOT judged: the look of the restored cards (no log line or OCR text tells a check mark from a cancel mark);
  screenshot `close_undo_restored` is kept for a person. Self-test `agent_close_undo_pieces_2103`.
  Run: `python3 script/realapp/appci/run.py --cases agent_close_undo_call_status`.
- **The note of a restored pane** (owner decision 2026-11-11, design `docs/design/r18-closenote.md`; nothing compiled or run when written).
  A reply of which a close discarded (and kept for status) at least one result that is NOT a cancellation says, as its last line, "Results
  from before this was closed were not sent to the agent. Tell it what happened if it matters." (`action_model.rs`
  `RESULTS_WITHHELD_BY_CLOSE_NOTE`). Screen only. Narrowed and reworded by the owner on 2026-11-11 (`fix/r18-closenote2`): a reply whose
  discarded results are all cancelled calls has no note (card and model agree), and the words name neither a tab nor a pane.
  - Unit, `block/view_impl/output_tests.rs` `discarded_by_close_tests::the_reply_of_a_restored_pane_notes_that_its_results_were_not_sent`:
    the decision the block draws from, with the pane's real action model and a real close-discard. No note before the close (control); the
    note for a reply holding a discarded call that finished (one that ran, one that FAILED, one that ran + one cancelled: one note); NO note
    for a reply whose only discarded call was cancelled (this expectation was "note" before the owner's rule of 2026-11-11; control: that
    result is still kept for its card); none for another reply or an empty one; none in the kill switch's arm (`keep_status = false`). It pins the wording. It does not paint the line.

## Round 19: the Windows Git Bash managed-ssh group of round 14 (design `docs/design/r10-r19-winssh.md`; #2051, #1393; harness only; nothing run on Windows when written)

Round 14 (build/r14a `42ef67839`, job app-test-windows) failed every Git Bash case that goes through the managed one-connection ssh, in terminal
and agent mode, as rounds 12 and 13 had. Verdict: the TEST HOST, not the app. The app log slices of that job were not uploaded (its
`after_script` hit the time limit before `run_slim` was made), so the verdicts rest on `results.json`, on the sshd.log lines quoted in it and on
round 13's logs.

- **What was wrong.** An exec with a pty (a managed session) is served by the `app` arm: a pseudo console of the app's own `conpty.dll`. That
  console host talks to its terminal before any program runs: `ESC [ 1 t`, a DA1 request, focus-event mode and win32-input-mode
  (`ESC [ ? 9001 h`). The test sshd sent all of it to the client. The client's terminal is the console host around msys `ssh.exe` in the app's
  pane; it obeyed and from then on gave ssh every control key as win32-input key records, which ssh sent on as bytes. `sshd.log`, round 14:
  `89 bytes in 84 chunks (... ESC 5, CR 0, LF 0; starts b'M\x1b[?62cecho T408_m8bgnr\x1b[17;29;0;1;8;1_\x1b[13;28;1`; the remote shell's
  line: `62cssh fake29;0;1;8;1_;28;10;1;8;1_;28;10;0;8;1_29;0;0;0;1_echo T178_mohi6h >> ~/rn.txt`. No Enter reached the remote bash, so no
  probe and no typed line ran ("probe ran in: none"). Round 13's typed bootstrap shows the same: 62007 bytes written by the app, 75934
  received, `ESC 3000, CR 0, LF 0`. The plain-ssh cases of the same pane pass because a shell request is served by Windows' own pseudo
  console, which asks for none of this. A POSIX sshd's pty says nothing to its client.
- **`ptyhost.ConsoleHostFilter`** (used by `fakesshd_win.py` for the `app` arm only): removes the DA1 request (answered by the test sshd, as
  #2051's `strip_startup_da1` meant to, which only looked at the head of the first read and so never matched: the first read is `ESC [ 1 t`),
  `ESC [ ? 9001 h/l` and `ESC [ ? 1004 h/l` anywhere, `ESC [ 1 t` before the first other byte; a sequence cut by a read is held for the next
  one. `sshd.log` says once per kind `console host start-up request <hex> answered|dropped by the test sshd, not sent to the client` and at
  the end `console host said to its terminal (not sent to the client): <hex xN, ...>`.
- **`client input ended`** now counts win32-input key records in what the client sent (`ESC 5, of which 4 in win32-input key records (the
  client's console was switched to win32-input-mode)`). After this change the count must be absent on every managed session; if it is still
  there, the mode comes from somewhere else than the test host and the verdict above is wrong.
- **One where-probe per verdict.** Seven rows printed `probe ran in: <a second probe's answer>`; in agent mode two rows said `probe ran in:
  remote` on a pane judged not remote. The text now names the probe that was judged (`cases_caseremote.py`, `cases_win_input.py`).
- **The managed switch is restored and proven.** `cases_caseremote.msys_managed_ssh_restore`: after `unset PHOSPHOR_MSYS_MANAGED_SSH` a
  line appends `<token>:<value or off>` to `~/.appci_where`; proven = the local shell answered `off`. Not proven: the pane is brought back to
  the local shell and both lines are typed once more; still not proven: the runner emits `pane_switch_left_on_after_<case>` (FAIL) and
  relaunches the app. Round 14, agent@gitbash: `ssh_failing_not_local` ran with the switch left on by `ssh_nested_typeahead_wrapper` (its
  `unset` went to the remote shell) and failed; the three rows of that case without the leak pass.
- **`ssh_failing_not_local`: "ssh failed" is the last close.** `cases.wait_ssh_gave_up`: no connection to the hanging listener open for 3 s in
  a row. With the managed path on, the wrapper's banner check (`ssh-keyscan -T 5`) is a first connection that closes before ssh itself
  connects; the case used to read the effect file 6 s after that first close. The oracle is unchanged (the line runs locally exactly once,
  after the failure).
- **New case, `cases.PROVING`: `ssh_gitbash_failing_not_local_managed`** (Git Bash pane only): the same oracle with the managed path switched
  on on purpose. A FAIL there is an app finding in the managed path (off by default): file it then.
- **`gitbash_typeahead_reps` (#1393)** failed in agent@gitbash only (tr13 6/10 lines, tr14 two lines merged; all keys reached the app; `AI=7`
  on the row). APP, the open issue #1393; not worked here, the app log of the job is gone. Each rep now notes its Enters that were not routed
  to the shell with the text they carried (`hop=enter_begin ... buffer= input_type=`), and whether the precmd set-up line itself was routed
  elsewhere. Evidence only: no check was added or removed.
- Selftests: `console_host_filter_r19`, `managed_switch_restore_is_proven_r19`, `typeahead_reps_names_non_shell_enters_r19`;
  `fakesshd_app_arm_da1_and_input_stats_2051` reads the new wiring.
- **What the next Windows run must show**: on every managed session `sshd.log` has the `console host ...` lines and no `win32-input key
  records`; `ssh_gitbash_managed`, `ssh_gitbash_bootstrap_in_command`, `ssh_gitbash_typeahead_managed`, `ssh_connect_typing_wrapper`,
  `ssh_nested_typeahead_wrapper`, `remote_tab_no_helper`, `remote_tab_enter_no_helper` are judged past their precondition (PASS, or a FAIL that
  names an app hop), with no `pane_not_local_after_*` row behind them.
## Round 19: the unit and integration failures of round 14 (design `docs/design/r19-units.md`; #2111 #2112 #2120 #2121 #2122; nothing compiled or run when written)
Verdicts and evidence per test are in the design note. What changed in the tests:
### `remote_server`: the contract harness is unix only (#2121)
`crates/remote_server/src/backend/contract_tests.rs` runs every backend assertion against a local POSIX `sh` (with unix modes, owners and
symlinks) and is now declared `#[cfg(all(test, unix))]`: on Windows it did not compile, which took the whole `test-workspace-rest-windows` job
down. Its users carry the same gate: `router_tests.rs` `git_reads_with_no_helper_are_served_by_the_shell_arm` and `index_sync_tests.rs` (every
test there drives `scratch_home_executor`). The one index-sync test that runs no shell, `ranked_paths_keeps_best_first_and_drops_repeats`, moved
to `index_sync_pure_tests.rs` and runs on every platform. A new test in this crate that starts `sh` goes behind `#[cfg(unix)]`; one that does not
must not be put in a unix-only module.
### `credential_process` splitting (#2112, and the test's own fault)
`app/src/ai/aws_creds/process_tests.rs`: `splits_like_the_cli_for_quotes_and_plain_words` asked for POSIX single-quote grouping on every
platform; on Windows the AWS CLI's split takes a single quote as a character, so that one expectation is now per platform (`'single quoted'` is
one word on unix, two on Windows). New, on every platform: `the_windows_split_groups_by_double_quotes_only` checks `split_windows_command`
(compiled for Windows and for tests): double quotes group, `""` is a word, backslashes are path separators except before a double quote (2n:
n backslashes and a grouping quote; 2n+1: n and a literal quote), an open quote is refused.
### pwsh: `$Error` on a machine with no node or git (#2111)
`agent_shell_wrap_tests.rs` (`real_shells`): `pwsh_bootstrap_and_prompts_add_no_error_records` was right and found an app defect on the Windows
runner (no `node`): the bootstrap's `Get-Command ... 2>$null` lookups record the failure in `$Error`. They now use `-ErrorAction Ignore`. That
test still depends on the machine (it passes wherever both programs exist), so `pwsh_prompt_adds_no_error_records_when_node_and_git_are_missing`
runs the real bootstrap, sets `$env:PATH` to an empty folder, runs the prompt twice and requires `errors=0` and no `ERR:` line: it fails on any
machine with pwsh if a lookup of an optional program records an error again. Skipped (returns) only where pwsh is not installed, like its
siblings.
### Fixtures that followed the machine (Windows; #2121)
- Agent fuzz rig (`app/src/ai/blocklist/agent_fuzz/rig.rs`, `give_the_session_a_shell_this_machine_has`): the test terminal's session says its
  shell is zsh and the app runs the session's own commands (the git probe before a grep or a file glob) with `zsh -f -c`. With no zsh on the
  machine each of them failed to start and I6 reported the app's ERROR line (35 tests on the Windows runner). On such a machine the rig gives the
  session the app's local executor with the bash found on PATH (`Sessions::set_command_executor_for_all_sessions`, test only). With zsh installed
  nothing changes. With neither shell the rig panics and says so. I6, the oracle and the allowed ERROR lines are unchanged.
- `plugin_manager/codex_tests.rs`: config fixtures write the marketplace `source` as a TOML string (`toml_string`); a Windows folder between
  plain quotes is not TOML and the registration under test was not there. `toml_string_keeps_a_windows_folder_readable` checks the helper on
  every platform.
- `plugin_manager/opencode_tests.rs`: `file://` fixtures are built per platform (`file_url`: `file:///C:/opt/...` on Windows, where a file URL
  without a drive is refused by the URL parser), and `classifies_bundle_folder_entries_at_any_install_location` also checks a Windows install
  URL (drive, escaped space) on every platform.
- `plugin_manager/claude_tests.rs` `truncate_chars_cuts_by_characters_not_bytes`: no verdict for its Windows failure (bash printed nothing and
  the test kept neither stderr nor the status). It now hands bash the plain form of the script's path (not the verbatim `\\?\C:\...` that
  `canonicalize` gives) and puts the path, locale, exit status and stderr in every assertion message. Same expectations.
- `terminal/view_test.rs` `an_ssh_window_survives_its_own_block_start_with_a_polluted_echo`: the block has no session in that fixture, so its
  shell family was the machine's default; on Windows (PowerShell) an ssh block takes the subshell-banner arm by design and records no pending
  ssh. The test sets a POSIX startup shell and asserts the family before it starts. No assertion changed. Not covered by a test: the same window
  in a PowerShell session.
- `crates/warp_tui/src/terminal_session_view_tests.rs` `shell_completion_source_warmup_loads_path_executables`: the wait for the load is a
  give-up net of 45 s (was 5 s: one cold `pwsh` start on the Windows runner took longer twice, then 1.4 s). It still ends when the load does.
### Integration driver: a named key sends no text (#2121)
`crates/warpui_core/src/integration/step.rs` `with_keystrokes`: the key down of a key outside the driver's table carried the key's NAME as its
text (`chars: "left"`, `"f2"`), which no platform sends. Since the pane key sink (#1411) a key down with printable text is a key that types, so
`shift-left` reached vim as the word "left" and F2 was never translated: `test_escape_sequences_sent_to_focused_terminal` and
`test_pass_control_sequences_to_long_running_block` failed 3 of 3 in round 14. `chars_for_keystroke` now gives the table's control characters,
the character itself for a key that types one (`a`, `ctrl-i`, `space`), and nothing for every other named key. Unit tests
`chars_for_keystroke_tests` (in `warpui_core`). `with_keystrokes_in_composing` is unchanged. A scenario that relied on a key name arriving as
text would now see no text; none is known.
### No verdict, nothing changed
`integration-linux`: `test_ssh_with_shell_override`, `test_command_xray_hover`,
`test_autosuggestions_are_hidden_when_opening_tab_completions` (#2122: the job keeps no artifacts and the INFO trace has no line for the pty
writes, the hover or the Tab). `test_ssh_into_sh` is an APP defect (#2120) and stays red until that is worked.

`intl_altgr_bash`, whose "`exit` NOT typed" note should be gone too). The oracle can still fail: a PowerShell line typed after the `exit`
must run in PowerShell, and a pane that answers neither probe is still reported and relaunched.
**A case waits for its own interrupted command to be logged (#2114, TEST).** `agent_lrc_no_false_takeover` can end with its `[y/N]` command
at its prompt; the cleanup's Ctrl-C ends it and bash logs it at the next prompt. `lrc_wait_logged` waits (10 s net) for that rec.log line,
so the next case's mark is taken after it. No check was removed: `cb_agent_pickers` still fails on any line the shell receives during it.
**zero_network_startup on Windows types nothing in launch and idle (#2114, TEST).** The polled path starts the app with the key proof
(`ctx.reprove`) taken out, idles `APPCI_ZNS_IDLE_S`, then runs the key proof as the first step of the scripted session (a failed proof is
a FAIL and the session is not played). Launch and idle allow no non-loopback row, as before; the configured model endpoint is allowed in
the session only, as before.
**latency_first_key_after_idle re-measures a suspected regression (#2114, TEST).** The app-log path (Linux, Windows Git Bash) now hands
`lat.evaluate` a `remeasure` (the same block again), as `lat.py`'s policy says: a clean second set is a WARN, never a pass; a second
regressed set stays FAIL. Thresholds, budget and baseline are unchanged.
**upgrade_over_previous: the previous release's stage is not a verdict on the build (#2114, TEST).** Failures while starting and driving the
previous release (`uo_old`) are collected in a scratch result and make the case UNVERIFIABLE (noref), named, with what is needed
(`prev_stage_unverifiable`). Once the previous release ran, the build under test is judged exactly as before. On the Windows VM the previous
release could not be driven in either pane in round 14; why is not known (machine look needed).
**CI: `RUNNER_AFTER_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT: "45m"` on `app-test-windows` (#2114).** The runner's default 5 minutes ran out in after_job.ps1 and the
scrub after the 7-hour full tier; `slim_appci_run.py` never ran and the artifact had no `run_slim/shots` and no `run_slim/logs`. The lab
and reuse jobs inherit the variable. Check on the next run: the trace has no "after_script could not run to completion" line and the
artifact holds both directories.
**Not judged, kept as rows:** `expert_fuzz` [terminal@gitbash] (#2115); `history_survives_restart`, `desktop_notification` and
`pane_wedged_after_restore_shows_history` in the Git Bash terminal arm and `latency_enter` [agent@gitbash] (#2116). `big_paste` and
`remote_heredoc_paste` on Windows fail as in the 2026-11-05 full run (platform: the conhost control falls short too).
## Round 14 candidate: the copy, window and pointer rows (design `docs/design/r10-r19-copy.md`; #2117 #2118 #2119; nothing compiled or run when written)
Candidate build/r14a `42ef67839`, pipeline 3052606915. Each failing row got a TEST-or-APP verdict from the job trace, the result rows, the macOS
screenshots and app logs, and the code. The Wayland job uploaded no screenshots and no app logs and the Windows job no app log.
| case | platform | verdict | what changed |
| `resize_reflow_output` (copies), `ui_copy_wrapped_output`, `minimize_fullscreen` (`mf_after_return`) | Wayland, macOS | TEST (#2118) | `cases_wrap_vtabs.leave_block_selection` |
| `resize_reflow_output` (vim) | Wayland, macOS | TEST (#2118) | vim is judged against the app's grid while it is open |
| `pane_resize_maximize` | Wayland | APP (#2119) | app fix; the case is unchanged |
| `selection_modes` | Windows Git Bash pane | APP (#2117) and TEST | app fix; the case presses Ctrl-C twice on Windows |
| `job_control` | macOS | TEST (#2118) | `READER_PROG` in place of `cat`; nothing typed for a reader that is not in front |
| `flood_scrollback_find` | macOS | TEST (#2118) | the tail is a line of just 499999 or 499998 |
| `mac_pointer_chord_proof`, `ui_mouse_select_copy`, `ui_copy_wrapped_drag`, `context_menu_actions`, `selection_modes`, `link_and_path_click` | macOS | TEST, the tool (#2118) | `mptr` looks through the Dock's backing window |
| `minimize_fullscreen` (fullscreen off) | macOS | not decided | `judge_fullscreen_off` makes the next run decide |
| `ui_copy_wrapped_drag` | Wayland agent | not decided (no log) | none; expected to follow the first row |
- **A selected block stays selected.** The focus-input key clears a text selection only. With the agent view feature on, a block selected by
  block-up stays selected as context for the next agent query (`terminal/view.rs` `focus_input_box`), the next block-up starts from it, and in
  the agent view the lines typed next are not classified (a pending context block locks the input type), so they go to the agent. Both by design.
  A case that selects a block by key calls `leave_block_selection(ctx)` before `back_to_input`: block-down from the newest block clears the
  selection and focuses the input (`select_more_recent_block`; `navigate_agent_transcript` in the agent view). `copy_last_block_output` and
  `ui_copy_wrapped_output` also press it three times before their block-up, for a block another case left selected. `APPCI_KEY_BLOCK_DOWN`
  overrides the key (`ctrl+down`, macOS `cmd+down`). The copies are still compared byte for byte.
- **vim's size.** A full-screen program's grid is larger than the block list's. `_vim_during_resize` compares what vim wrote with the app's
  latest `hop=grid_resize` while vim is still open, not with `stty size` typed after `:q!`. No hop for the resize: UNVERIFIABLE. It fails when vim
  reports another size than the grid it was given (not told of the resize).
- **`job_control` part 2.** On macOS a terminal `read` returns EINTR after stop and continue and BSD `cat` exits. The reader is
  `sh jc_reader_<t>.sh <file>` (`cases_daily_b.READER_PROG`) on Linux too. After `fg` the OS must show the reader running and no new prompt before
  the second line and Ctrl-D are typed; otherwise the case fails there and types nothing (in round 14 the Ctrl-D closed the shell, the window and
  the app, which read as APP DIED).
- **`flood_scrollback_find`.** `cases_robust.FLOOD_TAIL_LINE` no longer accepts a line of just 500000: the flood's command header holds
  `seq 1 500000`, stays on screen under the marker after the Find, and Apple Vision returned a text box that was only that number. The command
  holds neither 499999 nor 499998.
- **`mptr` and the Dock.** The Dock process keeps one see-through window the size of the display at the Dock window level; every click was refused
  with "the topmost window there belongs to Dock (pid N, layer 20)". `ownerAt` skips a window only when its owner is `Dock`, its layer is the Dock
  level, its bounds cover the whole main display and the point is inside the main screen's `visibleFrame`. A point on the Dock bar or the menu
  bar is still refused. The out file gets a `NOTE` line when the window was looked through; a refusal lists every window at the point, front to
  back, with bounds. Nothing for the owner to do. The NEEDS_OWNER that ended the same run is another thing: the `UserNotificationCenter` dialog
  "Allow Phosphor to find devices on local networks?" (3.3), which the owner allows once in the runner's GUI session.
- **Fullscreen off on macOS.** `Window.fullscreen(False)`'s error is kept and `Window.fullscreen_state()` reads the window's `AXFullScreen`
  back. `judge_fullscreen_off`: size back: pass; the request refused: UNVERIFIABLE (and the case's final size check with it); accepted and the
  window still fullscreen, or the window says it left and the grid did not follow: FAIL with which. Metric `fullscreen_off`.
- **`selection_modes` on Windows (#2117).** With text selected in the block list, Ctrl-C is a copy on Windows by design. `stream_arm` presses it
  twice there: the first must put the dragged text on the clipboard and leave the program ticking (`ctrl_c_copy_errors`), the second must bring
  the prompt back. On every platform "Ctrl-C did not end the streaming program" is now a check. App side: the copy drops the text selection when a
  command is in front (`ctrl_c_copy_drops_text_selection`), else no later Ctrl-C reached the program.
- **`pane_resize_maximize` (#2119).** The app moved the keyboard to the pane under a mouse release whose press was in another pane. The case's
  check "after the divider drag the probe ran in the right pane's shell" is the proof of the fix and is not changed.
